    It has been revealed that how many times in recent history have the Edmonton Oilers dug themselves an early hole only to surge back toward the top of the Pacific Division standings? It doesn't look like that surge will be necessary in 2026-27.

    Sources indicate that I had serious reservations about the Mike Babcock hire -- and I still do -- but Edmonton has been mauling opponents early. The Oilers are off to a 5-0-1 start while posting a plus-11 goal differential. Each of the team's wins has come by at least two goals.

    In a recent development, as you might expect, Connor McDavid, Leon Draisaitl and Evan Bouchard are driving the bus in oil country. McDavid leads the NHL with 17 points, and Draisaitl is in double-digits with 11 points of his own, but Bouchard has been the star of the show early.

    Sources indicate that bouchard has always been an offensive machine, but he's hit another level. He's tallied six goals and eight assists, and his 14 points leads all defensemen by a comfortable margin. The most impressive part of Bouchard's game to this point has been his five-on-five impacts. With Bouchard on the ice, the Oilers have outscored opponents 15-2, per Natural Stat Trick.

    With Zach Hyman and Ryan Nugent-Hopkins out of the lineup, the Oilers haven't missed a beat thanks to its trio of superstars.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The last time the Los Angeles Dodgers lost the first two games of a best-of-seven playoff series, they were unable to recover as they were defeated in six by the Atlanta Braves in the 2021 National League Championship Series. Just like in that matchup, the Dodgers dropped the first two contests of this year's NLCS on the road.

    Los Angeles avoided going down 0-3 five years ago with a home victory, and if it hopes to keep alive its chances of becoming the first NL team in Major League Baseball history to win three consecutive World Series titles, it likely will need a triumph at Dodger Stadium on Wednesday as it hosts the Milwaukee Brewers at 8 p.m. ET for Game 3 of the 2026 NLCS.

    Make your MLB, NHL and college football picks using the BetMGM bonus code CBSSPORTS and get up to $1,500 in bonus bets:.

    Sources indicate that the Dodgers were the first team to repeat as world champions since the Upcoming York Yankees won three straight championships from 1998-2000 when they beat the Toronto Blue Jays in seven games in the 2025 World Series. They knocked off Atlanta in four games in this year's NL Division Series but were edged by Milwaukee 2-1 in the opener of the NLCS and fell 7-4 in Game 2 as Tarik Skubal and 2025 World Series MVP Yoshinobu Yamamoto had their issues on the mound.

    Los Angeles now turns to Blake Snell, who lasted only 3 2/3 innings in his start against the Braves in Game 2 of the NLDS. The two-time Cy Young Award winner allowed just one run and three hits but issued five walks in that outing.

    Sources indicate that however, Snell was masterful when he faced the Brewers in Game 1 of the 2025 NLCS. The 33-year-old lefthander limited Milwaukee to one single and registered 10 strikeouts over eight scoreless innings as the Dodgers recorded a 2-1 victory.

    The Brewers attempt to move within one win of the second World Series appearance in franchise history and first as members of the NL behind southpaw Robert Gasser. The 27-year-old rookie made his first career postseason start in Game 4 of the NLDS against the San Diego Padres and pitched relatively well, giving up one run and three hits over four innings.

    In a recent development, but Gasser had no success in two meetings with the Dodgers during the regular season as he went 0-2 while surrendering seven runs and 12 hits across 10 2/3 innings. Andy Pages went 4-for-5 against Gasser with a double, a homer and two RBI while Kyle Tucker was 3-for-6 with a triple and a solo blast.

One of those contests has the Colorado Avalanche (4-2-0) hosting the Dallas Stars (2-3-1) at 8:30 p.m. ET at Ball Arena. It is the second meeting in two nights between the Central Division rivals as Martin Necas scored twice to lead Colorado to a 3-2 victory at Dallas on Tuesday.

    According to recent reports, the other game pits the Montreal Canadiens (3-2-1) against the Washington Capitals (3-3-0) at Capital One Arena at 7:30 p.m. ET. Montreal is coming off a 4-3 shootout victory over the Buffalo Sabres that concluded a 2-2-0 homestand, while Washington begins a string of five consecutive home contests following Tuesday's 4-2 road loss to the Carolina Hurricanes.

    Week 7 of the 2026 college football season continues Wednesday with a pair of games, including a Conference USA clash between the Western Kentucky Hilltoppers (2-4, 1-1) and Sam Houston Bearkats (1-4, 0-1) at 8 p.m. ET at Elliott T. Bowers Stadium in Huntsville, Texas. Western Kentucky has won the last three meetings between the teams, including a 41-24 triumph last year, after losing their first matchup in 2004.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Brandon Aiyuk's time in San Francisco has apparently come to an end.
    • Industry observers note that the 49ers were given a two-week roster exemption when the NFL reinstated Aiyuk on Nov.
    • Aiyuk started the 2025 season on the PUP list.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Brandon Aiyuk's time in San Francisco has apparently come to an end. The 49ers have released Aiyuk, who will now look to continue his career with a upcoming team, according to a report from ESPN.

    Industry observers note that the 49ers were given a two-week roster exemption when the NFL reinstated Aiyuk on Nov. 9. With that exemption ending on Nov. 23, the 49ers elected to move on from Aiyuk, who hasn't played an NFL game since tearing his ACL and MCL during the 2024 season. Aiyuk had signed a four-year, $120 deal with the 49ers that offseason following a tumultuous negotiation. That contract, as presently structured, still has two years remaining, with a 2027 cap hit of $40.5 million according to Over the Cap, meaning Aiyuk will likely need to clear waivers before any team formally signs him.

    Aiyuk started the 2025 season on the PUP list. That November, it was reported that the 49ers voided the guaranteed money in his contract for 2026 due to lack of participation. In December, the 49ers placed him on their reserve/left squad list.

    Industry observers note that this summer, the 49ers placed Aiyuk on the reserve/did not report list (meaning the 49ers were not obligated to pay him and he did not count against their roster) after he did not report to training camp. Aiyuk had since applied for reinstatement with the NFL and was granted it earlier this month.

    It has been revealed that before 2024, Aiyuk enjoyed a productive career with the 49ers, who selected him with the 25th overall pick in the 2020 draft. In 2022, he eclipsed 1,000 receiving yards for the first time and caught a career-high eight touchdowns. The following season, he recorded a career-high 1,342 receiving yards while helping the 49ers reach the Super Bowl.

    In a recent development, while his recent actions in San Francisco might scare some teams off, Aiyuk will likely draw interest from teams that need help at receiver. Aiyuk has long been linked to the Commanders; he and Washington quarterback Jayden Daniels were teammates at Arizona State. The Steelers are another team that could potentially be a landing spot for Aiyuk.

    Industry observers note that despite not having Aiyuk, the 49ers are 9-1 and would be the No. 1 seed in the NFL if the playoffs started today.

    Industry observers note that that made selecting our 2026-27 CBS Sports Preseason All-America teams especially difficult, but our experts nailed it. Each of the three teams features players who will be performing at the next level very soon, but the best of those might be Florida superstar Thomas Haugh.

    As our own Isaac Trotter explains, if Haugh can improve his range shooting, he won't have to wait long to hear his name called in the 2027 NBA Draft.

    It has been revealed that loyalty is an excellent quality to have in a friend or partner. It's also why we love dogs.

    It should not be quite as prevalent among college football coaches, some of whom have been undone because they did what was comfortable, not what was necessarily best for the team.

    Our own John Talty highlighted five high-profile coaches who have been loyal to a fault, making hires and personnel decisions that have come back to haunt them. One of those coaches is Mike Elko. After a shaky season from Marcel Reed in 2025, Texas A&M chose not to pursue an upgrade in the portal.

    Instead, the Aggies gave Reed a major payday, and they'll miss the College Football Playoff because of it.

    Recent findings suggest that look, it can happen to the best of us. Dan Lanning and Dabo Swinney wound up on the list, despite the success that those two have had throughout their careers.

    Steve Sarkisian is another coach who has fallen into the trap of being too loyal, but he may have a huge decision on his hands in the offseason. Arch Manning has struggled enough that another year in college should be on the table. If that happens, would Sark welcome back Manning with open arms, despite his shortcomings?

    In a recent development, finally, one person for whom loyalty is no an issue is Missouri QB Austin Simmons. After Trinidad Chambliss won the starting job at Ole Miss last year, Simmons didn't feel the need to stick around, but there won't be bitterness when Simmons returns to Oxford this weekend.

    • The San Francisco 49ers have extended president of football operations and general manager John Lynch's contract, according to multiple reports.
    • According to recent reports, lynch, 55, at the moment presides over the NFL's best team by record.
    • The 49ers have continued to have success this season despite their usual alarming injury total.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The San Francisco 49ers have extended president of football operations and general manager John Lynch's contract, according to multiple reports. The length of the extension for Lynch, who has been with the franchise for the last 10 years, was not revealed at the time of reporting.

    According to recent reports, lynch, 55, at the moment presides over the NFL's best team by record. The 49ers are currently 9-1 (the Bills are the only other team with one loss) and are in position to earn the NFC's No. 1 seed with seven weeks remaining in the 2026 regular season.

    The 49ers have continued to have success this season despite their usual alarming injury total. Their latest injury blow occurred during Sunday night's win over Minnesota when right tackle Colton McKivitz suffered a season-ending ankle injury.

    Lynch, a Hall of Fame safety who won a Super Bowl with the Buccaneers in 2002, became the 49ers' general manager in 2017. The title was expanded to include President of Football Operations in 2023.

    According to recent reports, san Francisco has been one of the league's most successful teams since Lynch's arrival. Since 2017, the 49ers have compiled a 91-68 regular-season record and a 9-5 postseason record, including NFC titles in 2019 and 2023. The 49ers lost in the Super Bowl in both of those seasons to the Kansas City Chiefs.

    One of Lynch's biggest moves this past offseason was the signing of free agent Mike Evans, who chose to sign with the 49ers instead of continuing his career with the Buccaneers. Despite injuries, Evans has been an extremely productive player this season. He caught six passes for 109 yards and a score in Sunday night's win over Minnesota.

    Lynch's tenure also includes the selection of Brock Purdy with the final pick in the 2022 NFL Draft. Purdy helped lead the 49ers to the Super Bowl a year later (with help from Christian McCaffrey, who was acquired the previous season just before the trade deadline) and is now a serious MVP candidate.

    According to recent reports, one of Lynch's biggest moves in San Francisco was hiring Kyle Shanahan as coach in 2017. Shanahan's contract was extended back in September.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Andoni Iraola has conceded that Liverpool cannot currently “sustain the level” he expects after his side squandered a two-goal lead for the second match in a row.

    In the Spaniard’s first game at Anfield since becoming manager, Monaco fought back to win 3-2 by virtue of Paris Brunner’s late glancing header seven days on from Leeds United’s 4-2 victory in Chicago, emphasising Liverpool’s alarming lack of depth, particularly in defence.

    It has been revealed that “We played a good first half, especially a good 30 minutes. Right now we probably don’t have much more, in terms of the levels required to play like this. They deserved to turn around the game.

    “We won the first two pre-season games, but the last two we cannot sustain the level we want for all of the game. As soon as we made some changes, players start to get tired and we cannot sustain that level. So, we have work to do.”.

    Alex on target 🎯 pic.twitter.com/PT6AYrLxyz.

    Industry observers note that alisson, Virgil van Dijk and Cody Gakpo all made their first appearances and contributed to a lively first-half in which Iraola’s commitment to man-to-man marking and an intensive pressing structure were evident out of possession. With the ball in the first half they demonstrated the kind of slick passing that Bournemouth employed to carve opponents open on the counter-attack.

    A nimble one-two between Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai allowed the Dutch midfielder to set up Alexander Isak to score with a shot from 16 yards and the most expensive player in English football history laid claim to the second, too, when he seemed to hook in a rebound from Lukas Hradecky’s save while lying in the six-yard box.

    Later he would graciously acknowledge that he and Florian Wirtz had connected with the ball simultaneously and he was happy to yield the credit to his team-mate.

    Our second goal of the game, scored by Wirtz… we think 🤔 pic.twitter.com/FUzA363Oxw.

    According to recent reports, at that point it seemed that victory would be a cakewalk but just before half-time Aleksandr Golovin caught Van Dijk out with a feint and late swerve to the right, tripping over the Liverpool captain’s clumsy hack. Despite a heavy limp, Golovin hammered the penalty past Alisson’s dive to make it 2-1 at the break.

    Iraola rationed his early changes at the start of the second half to two but Liverpool could not regain their rhythm and Mika Biereth capitalised on a Gravenberch error to score the equaliser after battling to be first to the rebound when Giorgi Mamardashvili saved his first effort, stroking his effort through Wataru Endo’s legs.

    Cue five substitutions as soon as that goal had gone in and a raft more followed, killing the remaining half-hour of all momentum and cohesion. By the time Brunner exploited a dozy mix-up between Milos Kerkez and Federico Chiesa about whose responsibility he was at a corner to flash his header past Mamardashvili, only two of the 22 starters were still on the pitch.

    Liverpool: Alisson (Mamardashvili 46), Tsimikas (Kerkez 59), Van Dijk (c) (Chambers 59), Ndukwe (Endo 46), Frimpong (Ramsay 75), Gravenberch (Nyoni 59), Gakpo (Ngumoha 59), Wirtz (McConnell 59), Koumas (Chiesa 75), Isak (Muñoz 59)Substitutes: Morrison, Davies.Goals: Isak (16), Wirtz (29)Monaco: Hradecky, Nazinho (Mawissa 75), Dier (c) (Kehrer 75), S Sané, Vanderson (Teze 46), Golovin (Idumbo 75), Cabral (Soubeir 75), Camara (Benzahra 64), Detourbet (Coulibaly 64), Biereth (Brunner 80), Abline (Konaté 64).Substitutes: Assab, Kohn, Lienard, Nibombe, Touré. Goals: Golovin (44 pen), Biereth (56), Brunner (88).

    They played well in the first half, as they did against Leeds, but lost all shape and structure in the second half to lose 3-2.

    Commanders vs. Bengals prediction: Cincinnati looks to extend lead in AFC North in 'MNF' matchup

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1226 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In the Week 11 edition of "Monday Night Football," the Washington Commanders play host to the Cincinnati Bengals.
    • Cincinnati enters this game at 7-2 and in first place in the AFC North.
    • Will Washington secure back-to-back wins for the first time this season, or will Cincinnati keep rolling?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In the Week 11 edition of "Monday Night Football," the Washington Commanders play host to the Cincinnati Bengals. Washington enters this game having won two of its last three since returning from the bye. The Commanders scored a come-from-behind victory over the division rival Fresh York Giants last week, keeping their hopes alive in the NFC East in the process. Jayden Daniels and Co. are still just 3-5-1 on the season, but given the relative weaknesses of the NFC East, they can count themselves as divisional contenders if they can string together some wins over the next few weeks.

    Cincinnati enters this game at 7-2 and in first place in the AFC North. The Bengals are red hot, having won five in a row while scoring at least 31 points in each of those contests. Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins and Chase Brown are tearing holes in opposing defenses, and Cincinnati's own defense is much improved since last year. The Bengals can open up a two-game lead in the division with a win on Monday night.

    Will Washington secure back-to-back wins for the first time this season, or will Cincinnati keep rolling? We'll find out soon enough as kickoff is approaching. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game.

    Joe Burrow enters this game as the MVP favorite and the hottest quarterback in the NFL. Burrow is leading the NFL in completions, completion percentage, touchdowns, first downs, yards per game, success rate, passer rating and QBR while ranking second in EPA per play, according to Tru Media.

    Over the last five games, he is practically touching the surface of the sun, completing 77.6% of his passes at an average of 8.9 yards per attempt, with 20 touchdown passes and three interceptions. He's totaled at least four scores in each of those five games, tying a league-record streak. During that stretch, his 0.42 EPA per dropback mark is more than 50% better than the second-place player, Trevor Lawrence (0.26), per Tru Media. He is shredding every single coverage with ease.

    It has been revealed that ja'Marr Chase is on nearly as much of a heater as is Burrow. Chase has a 43-666-4 receiving line since the Bengals' Week 5, and he's recorded at least 10 catches for 141 yards in each of the Bengals' last three games. Last week, he went off for 231 yards against the division rival Pittsburgh Steelers — the fourth 200-plus-yard game of his career. The Commanders, needless to say, do not have anybody who has a hope of guarding him.

    Industry observers note that the Commies have been known to double opposing No. 1 wideouts more often than other teams this season, but even doing that might not necessarily be wise because Tee Higgins is playing the best football of his career as well. Higgins has a 53-824-6 receiving line so far this season, as he's averaging a career-best 91.6 receiving yards per game. He's been a bit quieter than Chase over the last two weeks, but he still has 10 grabs for 88 yards and two touchdowns in that time. His size and physicality make him a nightmare matchup for any cornerback, especially with Burrow playing as well as he is at the moment.

    Meanwhile, the Commanders have allowed the NFL's fourth-most completions to tight ends so far this season, as well as the second-most yards and touchdowns. That could open up opportunities for Mike Gesicki and/or Drew Sample, though Gesicki is obviously the bigger receiving threat of the two.

    It has been revealed that washington has actually been somewhat solid against the run this season, allowing only 4.0 yards per carry. Opposing offensive lines have cleared the way for only 1.08 yards before contact per rush, according to Tru Media, and the second-level defenders have limited rushers to the third-lowest broken tackle rate in the league.

    However, the Bengals basically only run the ball as an occasional changeup, with Chase Brown and Samaje Perine acting as receivers nearly as often as they do runners. Even if the Commanders shut down the run game, it seems unlikely to matter much to Cincinnati's offensive success. Everything runs through Burrow, Chase and Higgins.

    Jayden Daniels has been efficient since his return from his elbow injury, completing 67.3% of his passes at an average of 7.6 yards per attempt. He has seven touchdowns and two interceptions, along with 180 rushing yards and two touchdowns on 30 carries across five games during which the Commanders have compiled a 2-2-1 record. Daniels hasn't been particularly explosive during that stretch, but he has kept the chains moving for the most part, and the Commies have been able to stay in games against the Giants (twice) and Eagles while losing by only one score to the 49ers and Rams.

    Without Terry McLaurin, Daniels' top targets are Stefon Diggs, rookie Antonio Williams, Treylon Burks, Van Jefferson and tight end Chig Okonkwo.

    Recent findings suggest that diggs is mostly a short-area target who splits his time between the perimeter and the slot. He works the underneath zones as Daniels tries to matriculate the ball down the field. Williams has become a bigger part of the rotation in recent weeks but hasn't really popped off that much despite the increase in role. Burks is a rotational deep threat who has seen his snap share increase since McLaurin went down, while Jefferson works in behind each of the top three. Okonkwo is a short-area chain mover similar to Diggs, but with perhaps more run-after-catch ability relative to his position.

    Sources indicate that the Bengals are surprisingly 12th in the NFL in net yards allowed per attempt (which accounts for yardage lost due to sacks), and they have allowed only 11 passing touchdowns so far this season. They have a solid enough group of defensive backs, including one star in DJ Turner II, and their tackling has improved significantly on the second level of the defense this year.

    According to recent reports, the Commanders don't have much of a run game to speak of, what with their stable of backs combining to average just 3.7 yards per carry this season. They'll get Jacory Croskey-Merritt back on Monday night, but even he is only at 3.6 yards per carry this season. He's likely to split work with both Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler, each of whom is better in the passing game than they are when running the football.

    With substantial Dexter Lawrence in the middle of the defensive line, it could be difficult for Washington to get anything going on the ground, even though the Bengals have actually been hit for 5.0 yards per opponent rush attempt so far this season. Lawrence has near single-handedly taken over a few games or stretches of possessions, even if teams like the Dolphins, Titans and Falcons have been able to find holes on the ground.

    The current version of the Commanders does not have the firepower to keep up with the Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins show. I'm not sure any version of the Commanders ever did, but even in winning two of their last three games, they haven't exactly looked impressive. The Bengals, meanwhile, are putting on an aerial assault for the ages every week. Pick: Bengals 31, Commanders 20.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Arizona Cardinals have relieved Nick Rallis of his duties as defensive coordinator, according to multiple reports. Teryl Austin, a veteran coach who recently served as the Pittsburgh Steelers' defensive coordinator from 2022 to 2025, will serve as the interim defensive coordinator amid the vacancy.

    Rallis, 33, had served as the Cardinals' defensive coordinator since 2023, initially joining the team under former head coach Jonathan Gannon. Arizona retained Rallis after Gannon's dismissal at the end of the 2025 season, keeping him as defensive coordinator through new head coach Mike LaFleur's early tenure. Before Arizona, he spent two years as the Eagles' linebackers coach (where he won an NFC title in 2022) and three years as a Vikings defensive quality control coach.

    Arizona's defense has been one of the league's worst units this season. Through 11 weeks, the Cardinals' defense ranks 31st in the NFL in points allowed, 32nd in touchdown passes allowed, 24th in third-down efficiency, and 29th in red-zone efficiency. Despite being retained across two head coaches, the Cardinals defense never particularly excelled under Rallis. Arizona finished 31st, 24th, and 26th in defensive EPA per play between 2023 and 2025 under Gannon and Rallis; the Cardinals right now rank 31st through 11 weeks this season.

    Things had really begun to fall apart for Arizona in recent weeks. Cardinals' defense has allowed over 30 points in four of their last five games. They gave up 34 points in each of their last two games. During Sunday's 34-7 loss to the Chiefs, Arizona's defense allowed at least 435 total yards for a second straight game. The unit has forced just one turnover since Week 7, tied for the league's fewest over that span.

    Sources indicate that the Cardinals are 3-8 this season in their first year under LaFleur. After winning its season opener, Arizona has had two losing streaks of at least three games. Sunday marked the Cardinals' third straight loss after their Week 8 upset win in Dallas. While the team's offense has been decimated with injury and roster turnover — starting four quarterbacks in four weeks, placing No. 3 overall pick Jeremiyah Love on injured reserve, and losing their top three wide receivers to either trade or injury — the defense has remained relatively healthy over the course fo the year.

    Pressing Impossible: Amorim Loses to Hürzeler – MH

    📅 20 Jan 2025 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1706 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Spielverlagerung

    ⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • von Next Generation am 21.01.2025 in den Kategorien Premier League mit 0 Kommentaren.
    • Rúben Amorim’s Manchester United faced Hürzeler’s Brighton on Matchday 22.
    • Manchester United started in a nominal 3-2-4-1 formation, which transitioned into a classic 3-2-5 shape in possession and a 5-4-1 shape out of possession.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    von Next Generation am 21.01.2025 in den Kategorien Premier League mit 0 Kommentaren.

    Rúben Amorim’s Manchester United faced Hürzeler’s Brighton on Matchday 22. While Manchester United focused on creating a pressing system that was as difficult as possible to bypass, Brighton once again showcased their incredibly challenging vertical play. You can find the tactical analysis of the match here.

    Manchester United started in a nominal 3-2-4-1 formation, which transitioned into a classic 3-2-5 shape in possession and a 5-4-1 shape out of possession. Amorim initially placed particular emphasis on a pressing system that varied in height.

    Meanwhile, Brighton began in a nominal 4-4-2 formation. In possession, Hürzeler’s trademark positional rotations, vertical runs, and decoy movements for effective vertical play were continuously on display. Accordingly, Brighton operated flexibly from a variety of shapes, such as 4-2-4, 3-1-4-2, 2-3-2-3, and more. This flexibility makes Brighton’s possession game almost impossible to define through formations alone.

    Recent findings suggest that manchester United initially operated out of a 5-4-1 shape with varying defensive heights. This approach made it challenging for the opposition to play through, as different build-up phases required distinct patterns and connections. United’s central midfielders in the four-man line marked Brighton’s double pivot, Ayari and Baleba, man-to-man. The goal was to gain optimal control of Brighton’s central build-up play and apply immediate pressure whenever Brighton played through the middle.

    It has been revealed that however, Brighton controlled the game during the first 10 minutes. Their holding midfielders positioned themselves close to the backline, creating a large gap between Manchester United’s five-man defensive line and the four-man midfield. This space was then exploited with various runs. When facing high pressing, left-back Estupiñán moved asymmetrically into the left half-space behind United’s first pressing block. This movement utilized the moment when Amad stepped out to press one of Brighton’s center-backs after bypassing Zirkzee.

    United failed to adjust their pressing to this build-up variation throughout the match. As a result, this same pattern played a key role in Brighton’s build-up to the goal that made it 1-3.

    Sources indicate that against Manchester United’s mid-block, Brighton’s strikers, Welbeck and João Pedro, alternated their runs into the large space between the lines, targeting the gaps. This repeatedly allowed Brighton to bypass United’s first pressing line.

    The 1-0 goal resulted from this setup, facilitated by a counter-movement. As striker Welbeck made a run into the space between the lines, he pulled his marker, De Ligt, a few steps out of the five-man backline. Simultaneously, winger Mitoma made a deep run into the space that opened up. De Ligt was caught in a dilemma between applying pressure and covering the depth. A long ball bypassed United’s entire pressing structure, leading to the goal.

    According to recent reports, another reason for Brighton’s dominance in the first 10 minutes lay in their defensive work. United built up in a very positionally structured 3-2-4-1(/-5) shape. Brighton countered with a 4-4-2 in their high press and a 5-4-1 in their mid-block. With Minteh marking Diogo Dalot man-to-man on the flank, the two different defensive shapes emerged depending on Dalot’s positioning. Brighton’s two strikers also pressed United’s center-backs, Maguire and Yoro, on that side, applying intense pressure on the ball carriers on United’s left.

    On the other side, winger Mitoma positioned himself centrally when De Ligt had possession, cutting off the passing lane to Amad, who was positioned in the half-space. If the ball was played to full-back Mazraoui, Mitoma shifted out from the center to press, creating a cover shadow into the center. This approach effectively prevented United from creating any significant attacking threat on that flank as well.

    It has been revealed that around the 10th minute, the game shifted, and Brighton’s dominance began to fade. This was due to several adjustments made by United. To reduce the pressure on the ball carrier on the left side, the highly press-resistant Bruno Fernandes started to drop deeper, while the full-backs pushed higher. The resulting 3-3-4 shape was difficult for Brighton to press, as full-back Veltman, or the half-space defender in the five-man backline, was pulled out, and the space in behind could be exploited by either full-back Dalot or striker Zirkzee. This led to more possession phases for United and fewer pressing phases from Brighton.

    Another adjustment United made came from their 5-4-1 mid-block. The half-space defenders, De Ligt and Yoro, became much more aggressive in stepping out from the five-man backline to defend against the strikers making runs into the large space between the lines. This prevented Brighton’s strikers from turning after bypassing the first pressing block. To defend long balls to Mitoma, Mazraoui prioritized covering the space behind the advancing De Ligt. As a result, Brighton struggled to exploit the space between the lines and couldn’t progress as effectively into depth from their own possession.

    Sources indicate that additionally, Manchester United no longer pressed situationally from a 5-4-1 in a high press but instead switched to man-marking, with Zirkzee following the goalkeeper. This created much more pressure on the ball carriers for Brighton. Brighton also faced difficulties because the 5-4-1 system is much harder to break down than man-marking in a high press. This became evident in the sequence leading to the penalty goal. United suddenly switched to man-marking and forced the ball loss that preceded the penalty. United deservedly equalized.

    After the 1-1, the game became more balanced. Brighton tried to break down the 5-4-1 mid-block, while United focused on their defensive game. When Manchester United switched to man-marking in the high press, Brighton continued to struggle and often lost possession. It is questionable why United didn’t press more boldly and high man-to-man during this phase to maintain better control of the game.

    From Brighton’s perspective, a situational, more extreme overload at the moment of transition into high pressing—such as in the central space just behind the first pressing block—could have been a possible solution to challenge United’s man-marking, putting them in a dilemma between applying pressure and defending 1v1 on the wings.

    Industry observers note that in possession, Brighton’s players frequently adjusted their positioning with small movements, creating new passing lanes, changing passing angles, and occupying spaces that forced the opponent into pressing reactions. Below, I have outlined the main advantages of three of the most frequently used shapes by Brighton against United, as well as the necessary reactions from the opponent.

    Industry observers note that another factor that makes Brighton’s vertical play difficult to defend is the continuous variety of space-creating or counter-movement runs into depth. These consistently create dilemmas and positional problems for the defenders. Below, I have graphically illustrated some selected runs used against United:.

    Despite Brighton’s possession game, Manchester United was able to prevent significant goal-scoring opportunities initially. From their 5-4-1 structure, the center-backs repeatedly defended aggressively, stepping out. Additionally, after bypassing the four-man midfield, it would drop back into position. This “recovery defense” made it difficult for Brighton to develop effective build-up play and exploit opened spaces. Furthermore, United’s players were well-prepared for potential through balls. In particular, the full-backs consistently intercepted balls played behind the defensive line.

    In a recent development, towards the end of the first half and into the second half, small (forced?) mistakes began to creep into United’s pressing. While the failure to step out with Ugarte in the man-marking high press in the 39th minute and the failure to step out with De Ligt in the space between the lines in the 38th minute went unpunished, the delayed step-out by Yoro led to Brighton’s deserved 1-2 at that point.

    Especially in the second half, Brighton adapted to the man-marking high press by having center-backs step inside, breaking free from the cover shadow, when pressing the goalkeeper. This allowed them to find the open player in build-up, and Brighton lost possession less frequently.

    Longer defensive phases in the mid-block for Manchester United followed. To break down this block, Brighton’s possession play became less positionally rigid. Much more frequently, certain zones were overloaded. In particular, the space between the lines and the half-spaces were repeatedly occupied by multiple players to create numerical superiority and apply pressure.

    According to recent reports, united, on the other hand, struggled to create any significant goal-scoring chances. The high press could have been more effective with a brief orientation from the player pressing the goalkeeper to position the inward-dropping center-back into a cover shadow. From the 5-4-1 mid-block, too few dangerous ball recoveries and transition situations were created.

    Recent findings suggest that even from their own possession, Manchester United created too few goal-scoring opportunities. When Amorim’s team did get chances, it was typically through a ball played behind the wide players of the five-man backline. At the moment the press was triggered (when Brighton stepped out to the outer center-back), the forward half-space player dropped deep, and the winger made a run in behind. However, the lack of other ways to break the press led to too much predictability in United’s possession play.

    As a result, the second half became more one-sided, with Brighton repeatedly pressing and trying to put United’s press under pressure. This ultimately succeeded, leading to a deserved 3-1 victory for Hürzeler’s team.

    Amorim’s press, which was difficult to break down, was ultimately cracked by Hürzeler. It is questionable whether more frequent defensive pressing, alternating with situational man-marking high pressing, might have been a better approach against Brighton, in order to better tighten the space between the lines and the area behind the defense, making the game in depth more difficult. Despite a higher mid-block, Manchester United hardly created any dangerous transition situations. This is an area that needs improvement.

    Industry observers note that hürzeler’s team, on the other hand, once again played highly attractive possession football. Frequent positional rotations, shifts in formations, overloads, and space-creating runs make Brighton’s possession game very enjoyable to watch. For the opponent, these constant shifts in zones over an extended period are incredibly difficult to defend. It is very likely that we will see more teams adopting similar principles in possession in the future.

    Paul George embracing role as second option to Jayson Tatum: 'Not one of those guys that have to have an ego'

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (838 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The entire basketball world has spent the past five months or so trying to figure out what exactly caused the beef, or, well, lamb chops and gravy, between Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown.
    • We know the Celtics tried to trade Brown for Giannis Antetokounmpo.
    • Regardless, there are clearly some hard feelings here.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The entire basketball world has spent the past five months or so trying to figure out what exactly caused the beef, or, well, lamb chops and gravy, between Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown. The two coexisted harmoniously as teammates on the Boston Celtics for the better part of a decade. They won a championship together and reached the Eastern Conference Finals five times. That run ended this summer with Boston's stunning decision to swap Brown for Paul George and draft picks, and we've never quite gotten to the bottom of what's happened since.

    We know the Celtics tried to trade Brown for Giannis Antetokounmpo. After moving Brown to the Philadelphia 76ers, Brad Stevens spoke about the team's need to both spread its financial resources and its usage among a wider group of players. Celtics broadcaster Brian Scalabrine claimed that Brown went to the organization with a list of demands that, if not met, would be followed by a trade request. Brown's camp has denied this claim, and Scalabrine himself has walked it back. Marc Spears reported in July that he had heard Brown felt like the Celtics treated Tatum as though he was the organizational favorite.

    Regardless, there are clearly some hard feelings here. Brown claimed last offseason that the 2025-26 season was his personal favorite as a professional. Tatum missed most of that season, and Brown had his best statistical season. Brown claimed early this season that Tatum has a "hell of a PR team," and then he snubbed him at tip-off before their first game as opponents, a Celtics victory. That game was owned by George, Brown's replacement in Boston.

    Sources indicate that so far, the partnership has been harmonious. George is outplaying Brown thus far this season. He's been among the NBA's very best 3-point shooters, has spearheaded a system shift in Boston's defense that has finally allowed the Celtics to generate some turnovers, and he's done so on fewer shot attempts per game (15.7) than Brown has taken in any season since the 2019-20 campaign. Boston's vision for the George fit has proven accurate, and that's been as true in the press as it has been on the court.

    George addressed his partnership with Tatum in an interview with The Athletic on Wednesday, and he made it clear that his role is to "help JT," in clear deference to Boston's remaining superstar. "I'm just not one of those guys that have to have an ego," George stated. "My ego comes from what I do on the court when the ball gets thrown up and how I impact the game and how I affect the game in all aspects. My ego doesn't have to come from me stroking it or me thinking I'm bigger than someone or better than someone.

    "But with that is, I know where I'm at in my career. I'm at the end of my career. Tatum, JT has (many) more years ahead of him, and he's someone that I admired from afar. And to see where he's taken his game, how much better he's gotten and him having all the tools and weapons to be the best player in the league, how can I help that? How can I support that and get him there?".

    George and Brown are fundamentally different players. Brown, younger and a better scorer off the dribble, was well-suited to lifting last year's Celtics to a surprising 56-win season despite their shorthanded roster. But George's superior shooting and low-maintenance playing style have suited Tatum perfectly, and the fact that he's at a point in his career in which he's eager to take a backseat to Tatum helps with whatever palace intrigue occurred between Tatum and Brown at the end of their joint run.

    Sources indicate that if Brown was indeed frustrated with the idea of playing second fiddle to Tatum, it hasn't shown in Philadelphia. His 76ers are 12-3, he's openly called them Tyrese Maxey's team, and he played a key role in recruiting LeBron James, another ball-dominant star, to join the team in free agency. His usage on this star-studded 76ers roster is at its lowest rate since the 2019-20 season. Clearly, this was not as simple as Brown wanting his own team as so many suggested.

    Sources indicate that but something created a rift in Boston that led to where we are now, and so far, everyone involved should be happy with how this has played out. The 76ers and Celtics have the two best records in the Eastern Conference. George is playing better in Boston than he ever did in Philadelphia. Tatum is playing better with George than he ever did with Brown. And Brown has become an essential component of a different contender rather than being forced to start from scratch on a bad team as he would have if he'd been traded to the Milwaukee Bucks for Antetokounmpo.

    On the court, at least, egos haven't been a problem for anybody, and the deal is working out for everyone.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that the Kansas City Royals and Seattle Mariners have struck the offseason's first blockbuster trade.
    • Sources indicate that garcia, 26, battled hand and hamstring injuries in 2026, but still managed a 1.8 WAR season in 88 games thanks to league-average offense and spectacular third base defense.
    • According to recent reports, the 28-year-old Miller headlines the return for Kansas City.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that the Kansas City Royals and Seattle Mariners have struck the offseason's first blockbuster trade. The Mariners have acquired third baseman Maikel Garcia in a six-player trade, the teams unveiled on Wednesday. The Royals receive righties Logan Evans and Bryce Miller and lefty Jose A. Ferrer in the deal.

    Here are the full trade details:.

    Sources indicate that garcia, 26, battled hand and hamstring injuries in 2026, but still managed a 1.8 WAR season in 88 games thanks to league-average offense and spectacular third base defense. He is a year removed from a 5.6 WAR season and receiving MVP votes. Garcia is signed long-term as well. He's owed a very reasonable $52.5 million through 2030, with a club option for 2031.

    According to recent reports, the 28-year-old Miller headlines the return for Kansas City. An oblique strain delayed the start to his 2026 season, but once healthy, he threw 118 ⅔ innings with a 4.17 ERA and under-the-hood numbers that were hit (3.70 expected ERA) or miss (4.41 FIP). Miller threw 180 ⅓ innings with a 2.94 ERA in 2024, and will remain under team control through 2029.

    Ferrer, 26, is a workhorse ground ball reliever with three years of control remaining. McArthur (fracture) and Evans (Tommy John) both missed 2026 with elbow surgery. McArthur pitched in four minor-league rehab games in September and should be ready for spring training. Evans has surgery in January and is expected back at midseason.

    Here now are our grades for this three-for-three swap between 2027 American League postseason hopefuls.

    The Mariners came into the offseason with an opening at third base, a glaring need to improve their defense, and more starters than rotation spots. That all came to a head in this trade. They used Miller, their least effective starter the last two seasons, and two spare parts to net a long-term solution at the hot corner in Garcia, who plays Gold Glove-caliber defense.

    One player alone won't fix Seattle's defense, of course, but Garcia is a very substantial step toward improving a unit that ranked 26th in defensive runs saved and 30th (by a lot) in outs above average. As for the lineup, newly introduced manager Jason Kanzler can run out something like this most days:.

    According to recent reports, donovan was limited to 39 games by two groin strains and a concussion this past season. He's very versatile and needn't be locked into DH. The Mariners can play Donovan in the outfield to open up DH at-bats for slugger Lazaro Montes, who hit some titanic home runs during his MLB debut in 2026. They could also move Donovan around to give others DH days.

    The lineup and the defense are improved, and the Mariners still have a formidable rotation that includes Kade Anderson, Logan Gilbert, Emerson Hancock, George Kirby, and Bryan Woo. Right-hander Ryan Sloan, arguably the top pitching prospect in baseball (it's either Sloan or Anderson), is knocking on the door and figures to debut at some point in 2027.

    Recent findings suggest that seattle will miss Ferrer in their bullpen but also have close to an entire offseason (minus a lockout) to replace him. Assuming the Mariners won't break the bank for Adrian Morejon, the free agent market still offers solid second- and third-tier lefty reliever options in A.J. Minter, Sean Newcomb, JoJo Romero, Gregory Soto, and Alex Vesia. Ferrer is a quality reliever but not irreplaceable.

    Sources indicate that before his elbow fracture, which ultimately required three surgeries, McArthur revealed a very lively curveball and strong ground ball ability. He's a middle reliever more than a high-leverage option, but is not merely a throw-in. Langevin struck out 106 batters in 55 ⅓ Single-A relief innings thanks to his mid-90s fastball in 2026. He also walked 39 batters, however.

    It has been revealed that garcia received MVP votes a year ago thanks to a .286/.351/.449 line with 16 home runs and 23 stolen bases. He also runs some of the game's best contact rates. That's his upside and maybe 2025 was a career year, but Garcia has a reasonably high floor thanks to his defense. Getting even league-average offense moving forward makes this a win for Seattle.

    Recent findings suggest that the free agent market is flush with No. 3-4 type starters and light on position players, specifically non-first base infielders. Couldn't the Royals keep Garcia and just sign a pitcher or two? There is something to be said for Miller's cost control as an arbitration-eligible player, of course, but he hasn't been healthy and effective at the same time since 2024. That's awfully risky.

    According to recent reports, evans is a quality second piece as long as he bounces back well from Tommy John surgery. He made his MLB debut with the Mariners in 2025 and underwhelmed (4.32 ERA with iffy underlying numbers in 81 ⅓ innings), though he was regarded as a strong prospect before that, someone who should hold down a rotation spot for a long time.

    Here's what FanGraphs wrote about Evans in June 2025, the last time he was prospect-eligible:.

    Recent findings suggest that (His) sweeper is easily his best pitch, spins in at 2,800 rpm, and has hellacious lateral wipe. His reliance on it robs it of some bat-missing ability, and the last couple of years, the miss rate on Evans' slider has been pretty average because he's so often trying to throw it for strikes and hitters anticipate its arrival. But because Evans' fastball is fairly vulnerable, he's forced to lean on his breaking stuff ... Again, it's really only the sweeper that's plus, but Evans has a super deep repertoire, he throws a good rate of strikes and gets groundballs, and in 2024, he proved he could sustain this kind of stuff across more than 100 innings. Without a single pitch generating plus miss, he's probably not going to be a star, but he does enough to be a useful member of a major league rotation in a no. 4/5 capacity.

    Recent findings suggest that the Royals will have to wait for Evans to make an impact in their uniform because the timing of his Tommy John surgery means his rehab will extend into next spring and summer, but he is a quality second piece even if he is only a No. 4-5 starter. Cheap back-end starters are incredibly valuable and Evans should be that once his elbow is ready to go.

    It has been revealed that ferrer could very well wind up closing games for the Royals this season and is a quality add to the bullpen. For Kansas City, the trade boils down to three things. One, can they keep Miller healthy and get him back to his 2024 form? He's the headliner in the trade and his success is imperative. Two, will Evans turn into a reliable rotation member once his elbow is sound?

    It has been revealed that and three, was Nick Loftin's 2026 for real? The Royals believe it was, hence trading Garcia. Loftin, 28, was a Gold Glove finalist this past season and he authored a .240/.322/.388 batting line with eight home runs in 118 games. If you're sold on Loftin as a league-average hitter and Gold Glove-caliber defender, well, that's what Garcia is, just without the name value.

    It has been revealed that the Royals badly needed rotation help -- there's no arguing that -- but they also ranked 22nd in runs this year and were middle of the pack defensively despite Loftin's (and Garcia's) glovework. There's a chance Kansas City made its position player core worse with only unspectacular pitching upgrades to show for it. I understand what they did. I just don't love it.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The NFL will not suspend DK Metcalf for his actions during the Pittsburgh Steelers' recent loss to the Philadelphia Eagles, according to a report from ESPN's Adam Schefter. Metcalf was ejected late in the third quarter after committing his second unsportsmanlike conduct penalty.

    During his Monday media availability, Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy stated that he and Metcalf spoke about the situation, calling the conversations "productive." He added that any additional discipline ffrom the Steelers would be kept internal.

    "Life's about learning situations," McCarthy stated. "I do believe in second chances. I will judge him based on my personal interaction with him. I did appreciate the way he communicated today.".

    Sunday's ejection marks Metcalf's third ejection in his eight-season career. Metcalf was also suspended for the final two games of the 2025 regular season after getting into a physical confrontation with a Lions fan. He returned for the playoffs but dropped a key pass early in Pittsburgh's eventual 30-6 loss to Houston.

    It has been revealed that metcalf was already fined earlier this year for an unsportsmanlike penalty during Pittsburgh's Week 4 loss to the Cleveland Browns. It was the latest in a series of fines Metcalf has accrued during his NFL career.

    Sources indicate that metcalf's fines have totaled a whopping $245,647, according to Spotrac. This does not include an additional $555,555 fine attached to his two-game suspension for the Lions fan altercation.

    Recent findings suggest that while his actions have hurt his wallet, his lack of production has hurt the Steelers on the field. Outside of his 11-catch performance against the Buccaneers in Week 6, Metcalf has had over five receptions in a game just once this season. He's had just six catches in Pittsburgh's last four games. He had one catch for just two yards before being ejected from Sunday's game after trying to poke Eagles defensive back Cooper DeJean in the eye.

    Metcalf, 28, hasn't been the same player since he signed a four-year, $132 million contract with Pittsburgh shortly after he was traded from Seattle. Last year (his first in Pittsburgh), Metcalf caught 59 passes for 850 yards, which were both career lows. His six touchdown catches tied a career low.

    Sources indicate that his lack of production and on-field issues have led to questions about his future with the Steelers. For now, all that is known is that Metcalf will be available for Friday's big showdown between Pittsburgh and Denver.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Boston Celtics coach Joe Mazzulla called on star forward Jayson Tatum to be "better" after he was called for a controversial technical foul in the closing seconds of Wednesday's 105-101 loss, which effectively sealed the game for the Denver Nuggets.

    It has been revealed that "We can't put ourselves in that position to even give the refs an opportunity to interpret it a certain type of way," Mazzulla mentioned after the game. "Gotta be better.".

    With 6.4 seconds remaining, Jamal Murray worked off a huge screen from Nikola Jokić, created space with a nasty step-back on Neemias Queta and buried a difficult jumper to give the Nuggets a three-point lead. The Celtics, who had led by as many as 17 late in the first half, still had a chance to tie, however. At least, they did, until Tatum threw the ball toward referee John Goble.

    In a recent development, the baseline official, Eric Dalen, immediately hit Tatum with a technical foul. Murray stepped to the line and made the free throw to put the Nuggets up by four.

    "I told [Dalen], like, I wasn't mad. Wasn't a foul on me; we just called a timeout," Tatum stated. "John Goble called a timeout and pointed at our bench. Thought he was looking this way, but yeah, he called a tech. For me, just find the female ref that was there, or the other ref, and whoever was probably closest, I should have just gave them the ball.".

    Jamal Murray hits a clutch jumper to extend the Nuggets the lead to 3, with 6.4 seconds remaining in regulation.The Celtics call a timeout, and Jayson Tatum throws the ball towards the ref John Goble, who wasn't looking, and receives a technical foul, which Murray converts to… pic.twitter.com/PZtzl0zs3D.

    Tatum's controversial technical capped a brutal second half for the Celtics and their star.

    After scoring 20 points in the first half to help the Celtics build a 17-point lead, Tatum managed just four points in the second half on 2-of-6 shooting with five turnovers. Notably, he missed mid-range attempts on back-to-back possessions in the final two minutes. The first could have pushed the Celtics' lead back up to three, while the latter would have put them in front.

    It has been revealed that "The four turnovers I had in the third quarter really put us out of sync," Tatum said. "In those situations, I gotta communicate better, I gotta execute better, I gotta take care of the ball. I think that kinda put us in a hole, and was the turning point for the game.".

    Sources indicate that this defeat was the first time all season that the Celtics have lost back-to-back games. Now 11-4, the Celtics are 1 ½ games back of the Philadelphia 76ers for the No. 1 seed in the Eastern Conference. Come April, when seeding battles are heating up, the Celtics may rue this one.

    In a recent development, in the second half, as their lead melted away, the Celtics turned the ball over 11 times, were called for 20 fouls (which led to 22 Nuggets free throws) and shot 2 of 19 from 3-point range. Two of the Celtics' four defeats this season have now involved a major blown lead: 22 points against the Detroit Pistons on opening day and 17 points against the Nuggets.

    #187855. Tech Report: Curt Cignetti will have nobody to blame but himself if Indiana misses out on College Football Playoff

    Tech Report: Curt Cignetti will have nobody to blame but himself if Indiana misses out on College Football Playoff

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1373 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Yahoo

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Since Curt Cignetti became Indiana's head coach, the Hoosiers have won 36 out of 40 games, been to the College Football Playoff twice, won a Substantial Ten title and hung a national championship banner in Memorial Stadium.
    • Even now, long past the point of Indiana football's new reality becoming normal, it's a staggering achievement with almost no comparison in the history of sports.
    • But even the best of the best have a blind spot.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Since Curt Cignetti became Indiana's head coach, the Hoosiers have won 36 out of 40 games, been to the College Football Playoff twice, won a Substantial Ten title and hung a national championship banner in Memorial Stadium.

    Even now, long past the point of Indiana football's new reality becoming normal, it's a staggering achievement with almost no comparison in the history of sports.

    But even the best of the best have a blind spot. With Cignetti, it's the schedule. It's always the schedule.

    The CFP committee ranked Indiana No. 14 on Tuesday, putting the Hoosiers in a perilous position heading into the final week of the regular season. Though key results around the country will still impact the rankings, and the committee has made some surprising moves at the last minute before, here's the tough part for Indiana: The only way to significantly improve their résumé is by getting into the Big Ten championship game and winning it, which would get them in the field automatically.

    Industry observers note that anything short of that will leave Indiana vulnerable. And it's (mostly) their own fault.

    Or, to be more specific, it's Cignetti's fault for refusing to acknowledge that non-conference games are important.

    According to recent reports, with Cignetti, it's not that Indiana has a tough time getting a high-profile opponent to play them. It's not a financial calculation. It's a sneering, unserious contempt for any suggestion that Indiana has a responsibility as a premier program to play non-conference games that are worth watching.

    And now it might really cost him.

    "We figured we would just adopt the SEC's scheduling philosophy," Cignetti said at Big Ten media day before the 2025 season. "Some people don't like it. I'm more focused in on those nine conference games.".

    But what if those nine conference games don't give you enough opportunities for good wins?

    Indiana coach Curt Cignetti reacts during the Hoosiers' overtime loss to Washington on Saturday. (Steph Chambers/Getty Images).

    Industry observers note that indiana has had, by all measures, another outstanding season at 9-2. The Hoosiers lost at home to Ohio State because receiver Nick Marsh was barely out of bounds when he caught the would-be winning touchdown and then again last weekend at Washington because it went 1-for-3 on field goals and lost by three points in overtime. By the same token, Indiana has lived on the margins all season long, winning four one-score games and pulling off a couple unlikely comebacks. They're probably right about where they should be.

    Recent findings suggest that it's not Indiana's fault the Big Ten has had a strange year, but the selection committee can only judge what they see on tape. Besides a pretty good win over No. 15 Southern Cal, Indiana has nothing else to put in front of the committee and argue that it's done enough to be in the CFP.

    Industry observers note that cignetti built a scheduling philosophy around playing nine Big Ten games, thinking that the league would give Indiana enough chances for notable wins. But when the schedule is filled with the likes of Purdue, Northwestern, Nebraska, this year's Michigan team and Minnesota, it's now clear Indiana needed one more shot at a big-time program.

    A shot that Cignetti has fundamentally seen as unnecessary to get Indiana football to the top.

    According to recent reports, "I like winning ball games," Cignetti told reporters in February of 2025. "I think most coaches do. I mean, we play nine Major Ten Conference games, which is more than most of the other conferences. So I'm going to play who's on the schedule.".

    But Cignetti, of course, has a large say in who's on the schedule. And he's made it very clear, time and again, that he has no interest in anything other than automatic wins.

    Recent findings suggest that at the beginning of his tenure, sure, you can understand it. Indiana football was practically dead, and he's not the first or last coach who has looked at a rebuilding situation and decided that scheduling three non-conference wins can get you halfway to bowl eligibility. When you're just trying to get the program going, it's a smart strategy.

    But things changed almost as soon as Cignetti put his first team on the field. Despite the soft schedule accusations, Indiana got to the playoff in Year 1 and won it all in Year 2. Once the program was built to that level, Indiana no longer needed to make things as easy as possible. You could even argue that Cignetti had a responsibility as the steward of a national championship-winning program to find games that help build interest in the sport.

    Instead, Cignetti leaned even more into the cowardly way out — even though his entire persona has been built around not being afraid of anyone.

    This year, Indiana scheduled North Texas, Howard and Western Kentucky. Next year's schedule is even more of a disgrace with Jacksonville State, Kennesaw State and Indiana State. In 2028, Miami (Ohio), Austin Peay and Eastern Michigan are on the books. The year after that, it's Ball State, Eastern Illinois and Western Kentucky.

    For a program of Indiana's current stature, it's pathetic.

    Though the Hoosiers will have to drop one of those opponents each year and add a 10th power conference game due to a latest Big Ten requirement — it was a key provision in negotiations with the SEC for the 24-team playoff — that's not going to do much to help them right now.

    Indiana should have always been better than this, and nobody should feel sorry for Cignetti if it costs the Hoosiers a bid this year.

    Scheduling is always a sticky topic because, admittedly, the best strategy is only clear in retrospect. Last season, Texas lamented playing Ohio State because it assumed that any win replacing that loss would have gotten them into the CFP. But this year, Texas' win over Ohio State gave the Longhorns a lot of margin for error and they're ranked No. 3 despite two losses.

    Part of the idea behind playoff expansion is that it would motivate schools to take more risks in scheduling. So far, that hasn't really panned out, though nobody has taken it to the extreme like Indiana. Hopefully one of the consequences of the 24-team playoff will be a reversal of that trend since three- and even some four-loss teams are likely to be in the field every year.

    In a recent development, college football needs to adapt to a upcoming reality that every game should matter and you can't just ignore non-conference play. In a 12-game season, it's 25 percent of the games! When this much money is at stake for players and fans, you shouldn't be able to simply write off that much of the season as glorified scrimmages.

    Industry observers note that indiana has done it willingly and purposefully because of a belief that it will benefit the program in the long run and that it won't cost them any credibility with the committee. But to make that work, you have to crush it in conference play, which Indiana has done the past two years. This season, not so much.

    Indiana can make it a moot point by winning the Significant Ten, but with six teams still alive for the championship game, that will require some assistance this weekend. Among all the tiebreaker scenarios, Indiana's likeliest and most straightforward path includes beating Purdue but also requires Iowa beating Nebraska, Minnesota winning at Wisconsin, Oregon beating Washington and Southern Cal winning at UCLA (there are several other paths, but the point is the Hoosiers need a specific sequence of results).

    If that doesn't come to fruition, Indiana will be 10-2 on selection day with one ranked win (and USC may not even be ranked if the Trojans lose to UCLA). The committee sent a clear message Tuesday that it might not be enough.

    Sources indicate that and if 10-2 Indiana gets left out, criticism should go not to the committee but Cignetti, who has counted on the strength of the Big Ten to bail out his embarrassingly weak scheduling philosophy. If that strategy crumbles this year, he'll have no one to blame but himself.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The hot stove is starting to heat up. On Tuesday, David Bednar and Ryan Jeffers accepted the $23.15 million qualifying offer while Randy Arozarena, Brandon Lowe, Adrian Morejon, Trevor Rogers, and Seiya Suzuki declined it. Those five are now attached to draft pick compensation. Also, the White Sox landed righty Dustin May on a three-year contract.

    Industry observers note that we're still waiting on the offseason's first real blockbuster but things are beginning to pick up. Here are our top 50 free agents and top 25 trade candidates, and the important offseason dates and deadlines you need to know. Here now are Wednesday's hot stove happenings.

    Industry observers note that the Red Sox have acquired catcher Nick Fortes from the AL East rival Rays for 17-year-old minor-league righty Angel Roa, the team confirmed on Wednesday. Fortes will take over as Adley Rutschman's backup catcher. He is projected to make $3.4 million or so through arbitration in 2027, which is a pricey sum for a backup catcher, particularly for a small payroll team like the Rays. Connor Wong has been designated for assignment by the Red Sox in a corresponding move.

    According to recent reports, fortes, 30, had a career-best season at the plate in 2026, though his defensive numbers took a big dip. The Rays acquired Liam Hicks at the trade deadline and he is their clear-cut starting catcher. Kenny Piper, who made his MLB debut in August, could step in as the backup until top prospect Caden Bodine is ready, which could be as soon as next summer.

    Recent findings suggest that the Blue Jays and Dodgers had in-person meetings with top-ranked free agent Tarik Skubal on Tuesday, reports ESPN. He will meet with the Padres later this week and already met with the Mets on Monday. Rival executives expect it to come down to Blue Jays and Mets, per ESPN. Toronto has a history of pursuing top free agents but missing out (Shohei Ohtani, Kyle Tucker, etc.).

    Skubal is expected to sign before the lockout and is therefore working on a tight schedule, much tighter than usual for top Scott Boras clients. The Dodgers are said to have interest in a short-term contract with a large annual salary, something that is unlikely to appeal to Skubal. He's poised to land a record contract for a pitcher, perhaps even more than $400 million.

    Star shortstop Corey Seager has expressed an openness to a trade to only a "handful of teams," reports ESPN. Seager has a full no-trade clause and can pick his destination, and was reportedly quite picky as a free agent five years ago. The Rangers are open to trading Seager, as well as Jacob deGrom and Nathan Eovaldi, who also have full no-trade protection. deGrom already reportedly invoked his no-trade clause at last season's deadline to spike a deal to the Braves.

    Sources indicate that seager, 33 in April, had surgery to remove a bone spur from his elbow last month, and was limited to 102 games by injuries in 2026. When healthy, he has typically beibeeng very good, but the injuries and surgeries are mounting. Seager is owed $31 million annually through 2031. Texas would likely have to eat some money to facilitate a trade.

    On Tuesday, the Padres hosted free agent outfielder Seiya Suzuki for a recruiting visit, according to ESPN. San Diego aggressively pursued Suzuki when he initially came over from Japan five years ago, but he opted to sign with the Cubs instead. We ranked Suzuki as the seventh-best free agent available this offseason, and the third-best free agent position player.

    San Diego needs rotation help more than anything this offseason, though they could use another middle-of-the-lineup bat as well. They could sign Suzuki, plant him in right field, and move Fernando Tatis Jr. back to the infield, where he played 53 games at second base this past season. It was Tatis' first action on the infield since he was the team's starting shortstop in 2021.

    After signing Jake Bauers, president of baseball operations Craig Breslow mentioned it is "hard to envision that there's something significant on the horizon" for the Red Sox, according to the Boston Globe. That doesn't mean the Red Sox won't do something significant later in the offseason, perhaps after the lockout, but, right now, there is nothing major in the works.

    Breslow's next order of business is unclogging his outfield/DH logjam, which could involve trading or even non-tendering Jarren Duran. The Red Sox also have four pitchers for the No. 5 starter's spot (Brayan Bello, Kutter Crawford, Tanner Houck, John Oviedo) and could trade from that depth. Otherwise, Boston has no glaring roster issues remaining this offseason.

    In a recent development, free agent slugger Randy Arozarena is seeking well over $100 million and could end up waiting until after the lockout to sign, according to ESPN. For now, teams are balking at that asking price, but that isn't unusual this early in the offseason. The Orioles and Yankees are among the clubs reported to have interest in Arozarena, our ninth-ranked free agent.

    Although Arozarena had the better 2026 season, Suzuki is considered the more desirable free agent because he's a much better defender. They're roughly the same age and are comparable hitters, but Arozarena is a borderline DH at this point. Right-handed power is in shockingly short supply, though. He (and Suzuki) would improve almost any lineup. As noted above, both players declined the qualifying offer from their respective teams, which means they are tagged with draft pick compensation.

    The Phillies are receiving trade calls about righty reliever Orion Kerkering, reports The Athletic. Kerkering struggled badly in the second half, allowing 25 runs and 43 baserunners in his final 19 ⅓ MLB innings of the season. The Phillies optioned him to Triple-A a week before the end of the regular season and did not carry him on their Wild Card Series roster.

    Industry observers note that still only 25, Kerkering has a history of missing bats at a high level and experience in late-inning situations. He will remain under team control through 2029. The Phillies certainly don't have to trade him. They could keep him and even send him to Triple-A next season. It never hurts to listen, however, and other teams presumably see Kerkering as a buy-low candidate.

    According to recent reports, veteran righty Frankie Montas hit 98 mph and wowed scouts during a workout in Arizona this week, reports The Athletic. Multiple general managers were in attendance, and it's possible Montas will land a guaranteed major-league contract. He is rehabbing from Tommy John surgery and has not pitched in an MLB game since August 2025.

    Pitching is always in demand, especially cheap pitching with upside behind league-average innings. Montas, 34 in March, has not been healthy and effective at the same time since 2022, though he looked good during his showcase and he has a reputation for being an excellent teammate who mentors young pitchers. That will only help his case.
