    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • One of the greatest players in Tampa Bay Lightning history may soon be wearing a different jersey.
    • Kucherov, a two-time Stanley Cup champion and two-time Hart Trophy winner as league MVP, is one of the best players of his era.
    • It has been revealed that just last season, Kucherov posted 44 goals and 86 assists en route to his second Hart Trophy win.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    One of the greatest players in Tampa Bay Lightning history may soon be wearing a different jersey. According to Sportsnet, Nikita Kucherov has told the Lightning he won't sign a contract extension and has requested a trade.

    Kucherov, a two-time Stanley Cup champion and two-time Hart Trophy winner as league MVP, is one of the best players of his era. The 33-year-old just passed the legendary Steven Stamkos for the all-time franchise lead in points and has shown no signs of slowing down.

    It has been revealed that just last season, Kucherov posted 44 goals and 86 assists en route to his second Hart Trophy win. His underlying numbers were even better with a five-on-five goal differential of plus-38 and an expected goals share of 57.0 percent. Only a select few players can drive play from the wing like Kucherov, and that makes him a unicorn of sorts.

    Sources indicate that kucherov is in the final year of a contract that pays him $9.5 million per season, and with the salary cap rising rapidly, he's due for a gargantuan raise next summer. It sounds like Kucherov and the Lightning were too far apart on that number, so the superstar winger has shifted his focuse to a change of scenery.

    It's important to note that Kucherov has limited trade protection in the form of a 10-team trade list, but that should be more than enough for the Lightning to find a suitable trade partner. With that in mind, let's take a look at five teams that would be ideal fits for Kucherov as he prepares for the next chapter of his illustrious career.

    Right out of the gate, this is the most natural fit of all the potential landing spots. General manager Kent Hughes has done a superb job of locking down his young core on team-friendly contracts, and as a result, the Canadiens have nearly $30 million in projected cap space for next season. They also have a glaring need in their top two lines, and I'd say the reigning Hart Trophy winner would fill that role quite nicely.

    Sources indicate that montreal's moment to strike is now. It's an ascendant team with a great salary cap situtation and assets to spend. It's time to make a splash, and this would be a tsunami. Just imagine Kucherov on a power play unit with Nick Suzuki, Cole Caufield, Lane Hutson and Ivan Demidov. Kucherov would also be coached by former Lightning teammate Martin St. Louis, so a rapport would already exist between player and coach. I expect the Canadiens to do everything in their power to land Kucherov.

    Industry observers note that we already know the Wild are massive-game hunting at forward because they've been heavily linked to former Detroit Red Wings captain Dylan Larkin. If I were advising general manager Bill Guerin -- and I'm certainly not -- I would recommend Minnesota package whatever assets it has offered Detroit and redirect them to Tampa Bay. No, Kucherov is not a center,  and that's the Wild's biggest need.

    Industry observers note that however, Kucherov is a rare breed of winger in that he can drive play better than most first-line centers from the wing. Put him on a line with Kirill Kaprizov, and the only time opponents will touch the puck is when they're pulling out of the net.

    With Quinn Hughes also on an expiring contract, acquiring Kucherov would be a risky move for the Wild. What if they give up premium assets only to lose Kucherov and Hughes next summer? I don't think fear can dictate Minnesota's decisions. The team has a top-two defenseman in the world on its roster right now, and it has the opportunity to acquire a top-five forward. Worry about next summer when the time comes. Go all in to win the Cup while you have a chance.

    It was no secret that the Hurricanes were in on the Connor Hellebuyck sweepstakes but just missed out. So, if they can't get better at preventing goals, why not get much better at scoring them? Carolina doesn't exactly need any help offensively, but adding Kucherov would go a long way to helping the team repeat as Stanley Cup champions. Besides, Kucherov would provide another level of playmaking and finishing that the Canes don't currently have on their roster.

    Recent findings suggest that carolina has a good chunk of cap space available already, and it wouldn't need to shed much in order to make room for Kucherov. The Canes also have some enticing young players on their roster that might appeal to the Bolts, and they have three first-round picks over the next two drafts. Why not take a shot at landing a superstar winger?

    It has been revealed that similar to the Hurricanes, the Mammoth were in the mix to acquire Hellebucyk, and for good reason. The goaltending tandem of Karel Vejmelka and Sebastian Cossa has not been good, so Utah may have to outscore its problems until one of the goalies finds a groove. Offense may be the best defense for the Mammoth -- and if that's the case -- then Kucherov should be in the mix for the Norris Trophy. There is a great young core of forwards in Salt Lake City, and I think Kucherov would be a perfect fit alongside Logan Cooley, who is emerging as a franchise center.

    Recent findings suggest that utah also has plenty of draft capital with which to work, and it's projected for just over $25 million in salary cap space next season. The Mammoth don't have any major pending free agents on their cap sheet, so they're a suitor capable of signing Kucherov to a long-term extension.

    Recent findings suggest that allow me to get a little bold on the fifth and final destination. The Stars have already failed to sign 27-year-old winger Jason Robertson to a long-term extension once. The two sides agreed to a one-year deal worth $12 million prior to the season, but Robertson's future with the team is still very much in doubt. What if Dallas and Tampa Bay executed a true "hockey trade" -- one player for one player?

    Recent findings suggest that dallas would get the better player in Kucherov, but there are no guarantees regarding an extension. The Stars are in win-now mode, and Kucherov could help them get over the Cup hump immediately. Tampa Bay would get a younger player in Robertson, and although he doesn't have the elite playmaking ability of Kucherov, he's still an exceptionally talented scorer. Perhaps the Bolts could get him to join the team's core and sign a multi-year contract. This deal could work for both sides.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The uncertain 2026-27 Major League Baseball offseason is fully underway.
    • Recent findings suggest that thanks to that prospect of a hastened pace, offseason rumors are flowing.
    • The buzz at the GM Meetings last week was that the Mets offered top free agent Tarik Skubal a nine-year contract worth almost $400 million, reports MLB Network Radio.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The uncertain 2026-27 Major League Baseball offseason is fully underway. The ongoing CBA negotiations and the near-certainty of an owner-implemented lockout on Dec. 2 loom over all, and it may indeed mean a flurry of trades and free-agent signings leading up to that date. That was certainly the case leading up to the last lockout of 2021-22, and this time around we've already seen some leading examples.

    Recent findings suggest that thanks to that prospect of a hastened pace, offseason rumors are flowing. Speaking of which, we'll be here each day to round up what's out there. You can find Friday's supply just below.

    The buzz at the GM Meetings last week was that the Mets offered top free agent Tarik Skubal a nine-year contract worth almost $400 million, reports MLB Network Radio. If the deal is worth at least $390 million, it would set fresh records for total guarantee and average annual value given to a pitcher. Here are the current pitcher contract records:.

    1. Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Dodgers: $325M.

    2. Justin Verlander, Mets: $43.3M.

    Recent findings suggest that 3. Stephen Strasburg, Nationals: $245M.

    3. Zack Wheeler, Phillies: $42M.

    Industry observers note that 4. Framber Valdez, Tigers: $38.3M.

    Given the player and the deep-pocketed teams involved in the bidding (Blue Jays, Dodgers, Mets, etc.), Skubal is well-positioned to shatter Yamamoto's record. He could beat Scherzer's and Verlander's record as well. The expected lockout will begin after the collective bargaining agreement expires at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec. 1. Skubal is likely to sign before then.

    According to recent reports, the Diamondbacks are set to acquire righty Johan Oviedo from the Red Sox for minor-league lefty Luke Dotson and a player to be named later, reports the Arizona Republic. Boston had four pitchers for the No. 5 starter's spot (Oviedo, Brayan Bello, Kutter Crawford, Tanner Houck) and always seemed likely to trade one to ease the logjam.

    Industry observers note that acquired from the Pirates last offseason, Oviedo made just one ineffective appearance around elbow trouble in 2026. He returned from Tommy John surgery in 2025 and looked excellent, and Arizona will hope Oviedo rediscovers that magic as he gets further away from his injuries. Dotson is not a top prospect. It's a low-cost flier for the D-backs.

    Sources indicate that the Tigers have signed right-hander Troy Melton to a six-year extension worth $46.5 million, reports ESPN. There is a club option for a seventh year and escalators can push the total guarantee to $80 million. Melton still had five years of team control. The upcoming extension buys out his five team control years and one free agent year with an option for another free agent year.

    Industry observers note that melton, 26 next month, missed the start of the season with elbow inflammation and finished the season on the injured list with more elbow woes. Between injuries, he made 20 starts with a sub-3.00 ERA with strong under-the-hood numbers. The Tigers know him better than anyone and are obviously comfortable with Melton's medicals to lock him up long-term.

    Industry observers note that the New York Yankees have agreed to a two-year contract with veteran right-hander Jonathan Loáisiga, ESPN reports. The deal also includes a club option for 2029 and is worth roughly $18 million, according to MLB.com.

    Loáisiga, 32, is coming off that strong season above for the Arizona Diamondbacks, and for his career boasts an ERA+ of 128 across parts of nine MLB seasons. He's worked in relief for almost all of that span, and eight of those nine seasons came with the Yankees.

    Sources indicate that new York Yankees general manager Brian Cashman was recently asked if he'd be willing to play Spencer Jones in center field. In response, he told media, including SNY, this:.

    Industry observers note that "I would be comfortable with that. At the same time Jasson Domínguez is pounding the ball in winter ball. The entire industry is noticing that based on the phone calls I'm getting.".

    In a recent development, the 23-year-old Domínguez still has significant-time power potential, and defensively he's best suited to center field. For his career in the Bronx, he has an OPS+ of 93, but his 751 plate appearances have been doled out erratically across four seasons. As things stand now, he'll once again be subject to a playing-time crunch. Aaron Judge and Cody Bellinger are installed at the outfield corners, and Giancarlo Stanton, if healthy, should get much of the playing time at DH. That leaves center field for Jones or Domínguez. Other teams no doubt see that bottleneck and are seeing if Cashman and the Yankees are willing to relieve it through trade.

    Lefty ace and two-time American League Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal remains far and away the top talent on the free-agent market. While the Fresh York Mets and incumbent Los Angeles Dodgers seem like the favorites to secure his services, the San Diego Padres also have significant interest in him. That interest took the next step on Thursday with an in-person meeting, The Athletic reports. The Padres are the fourth team to meet with Skubal, who turned 30 on Friday. Previously, the Dodgers, Mets, and Toronto Blue Jays met with him.

    The Padres have a pronounced need in the rotation, especially if free-agent right-hander Michael King signs elsewhere. Last winter, they also lost Dylan Cease to the Blue Jays via free agency.

    The Padres and left-handed platoon hitter Gavin Sheets have agreed to a three-year, $11 million contract extension that includes two opt-outs, FanSided reports. Sheets, who'll turn 31 in April, had been slated for free agency after the upcoming season. Instead, he and the Padres will now be potentially committed through the 2029 season, depending on whether Sheets exercises any of his opt-outs. While he's not much of a hitter for average, he does draw walks and hit for power. In two seasons with San Diego, he's tallied 36 home runs and 44 doubles in 855 at-bats while seeing DH, first base, and the outfield corners.

    In a recent development, the New York Mets have agreed to a three-year, $12 million deal with right-handed reliever Darwinzon Hernández, reports José F. Rivera.

    Hernández, who turns 30 in December, hasn't pitched in MLB since 2022 and instead has revived his career with four strong seasons in Japan. Over that span for Softbank of the NPB, he's put up an ERA of 2.46 in 131 ⅔ innings with 168 strikeouts and 42 unintentional walks. Prior to rebuilding himself in Japan, Hernández had a 5.06 ERA and a 1.82 K/BB ratio over parts of four seasons with the Boston Red Sox.

But we also saw injuries, a disappointing first handful of games from Mikal Bridges and an Eastern Conference that is not nearly as dominant as it was supposed to be.

    Those are three of the biggest letdowns of the young season. Here's our John Gonzalez on why Bridges might be the greatest dud of any individual player:.

    In a recent development, another major disappointment: The Kings. How can a team underperform expectations when those expectations are already about as low as they come? Well, Sacramento sure has found a way. With a 1-13 record and after a puzzling trade, the Kings earned their spot in our ranking of the NBA's most hopeless teams.

    According to recent reports, the College Football Selection Committee is in love with the SEC. Only one time in three different rankings have the bracket-makers ranked a team from that conference lower than AP Top 25 voters. Whether or not you think it's fair, the numbers largely back it up.     Here's how to watch the biggest games of Week 12 and our picks for each of them:.

    This is easily the most lopsided week of the NFL season. The Bills and Chiefs are three-score favorites. The Bears and Broncos are also favored by double digits. The Cowboys, Lions, Jaguars and Bengals are all favored by about a touchdown. You know how these things go, though. One of these favorites is bound to lose. We put a few of them on upset alert, and a handful of our experts are in agreement that the Lions are among the most vulnerable.

    Industry observers note that first of all, the Buccaneers have just as much to play for as the Lions. Both of them are locked into tightly contested division battles. The motivation will be there for a Tampa Bay team that could somehow sneak into the playoffs even with a losing record. And then there's the Tampa Bay defense, which has forced at least four turnovers in each of its last three games. Our Tyler Sullivan said it would not surprise him if Jared Goff's interception streak continues.

    And even though our Jordan Dajani could not bring himself to pick the upset outright, he does see the Buccaneers keeping this one highly competitive.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Friday marked the non-tender deadline in Major League Baseball.
    • According to recent reports, most such decisions are easy and obvious.
    • Industry observers note that all that sets the stage for what follows, which is our list of the most compelling non-tendered players who are now on the market and available for hire.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Friday marked the non-tender deadline in Major League Baseball. That important date on the offseason calendar is when clubs must make, or "tender," contract offers for the upcoming season to all their arbitration-eligible and pre-arbitration players on the 40-player roster. That's every player who isn't a free agent or isn't presently signed to a multi-year contract. Players who are tendered a contract by that deadline remain with their current organizations. Players who aren't offered a contract become free agents.

    According to recent reports, most such decisions are easy and obvious. Others, however, present difficult calls for the organization because of roster crunches, crowded depth charts, or, more commonly, reluctance to retain a player as his salary rises through the arbitration process. While a number of non-tendered players are likely on their way out of the league, a select few others qualify as at least interesting to other teams and, on occasion, a few will even be coveted to varying degrees.

    Industry observers note that all that sets the stage for what follows, which is our list of the most compelling non-tendered players who are now on the market and available for hire. Let's get to it ….

    Recent findings suggest that the 2024 AL Rookie of the Year, Gil has been injured and ineffective the last two seasons. He missed time with a shoulder issue this past season and also spent time in Triple-A. The Yankees moved him to the bullpen late in the season to see whether he could contribute that way, though Gil was unable to make a strong impression in that role. Now 28, Gil still has another three seasons of team control remaining. Whichever team signs him will be able to keep him through 2029, and that extra control, plus his Rookie of the Year pedigree, will no doubt land Gil with a newly introduced team before Opening Day.

    As a 23-year-old in 2023, the infielder and former first-rounder hit 27 home runs in 119 games and looked like a future cornerstone for the Cardinals. Gorman, however, has gotten steadily worse since then thanks largely to his persistent strikeout concerns. Last season, he wound up back at Triple-A for an extended stretch and didn't fare any better upon being recalled. Long-term, the Cardinals will likely look to hand the third base position to rising power prospect Jesús Báez, who was recently added to the 40-player roster. Gorman can be a plus at third and probably still get by at second, and no doubt some team will take a chance on his power.

    On the downside, Larnach is a defensive minus at the corner outfield spots and probably needs to be a DH, and he's also a platoon bat. On the upside, he's been a steady producer from the left side of the plate. This past season, he put up a .352 OBP and an OPS+ of 120 for Minnesota. For his career, he has an OPS+ of 106 across parts of six MLB seasons. He out-hit his underlying indicators by a bit in 2026, but Larnach is still going to be an appealing part-time bat for some teams.

    It has been revealed that the Twins cut bait on a right-hander who's made 139 career starts for them since his 2021 big-league debut. Ober boasts a career OPS+ of 102, but that figure has slid over the last two seasons. What's also slid is Ober's fastball velocity, which may be why he's on this list. In his rookie season, he averaged a fringy 92.4 mph with his four-seamer, but last season that figure was down all the way to 88 mph. That put him in the very bottom percentile among MLB hurlers. The 31-year-old Ober still should draw some interest as a depth piece.

    A platoon extraordinaire, Raley has always hit for power against righties, including 15 home runs in only 290 plate appearances against them in 2026. He's sneaky fast and a very good athlete for his size (6-foot-3 and 235 lbs.), good enough to handle the corner outfield spots competently. Raley also has first base experience and can patrol center field in a pinch. The Mariners cut him loose even though he will remain under team control through 2028. Raley's power against righties and an extra year of control could make him a solid bench option moving forward.

    Victor Wembanyama has dunked so much he hurt his hand, so he came up with a unique solution: The 'shunk'

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (537 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that remember at the end of Space Jam, when Michael Jordan released himself off of the butt of a MonStar to dunk from the half-court line?
    • The San Antonio Spurs are leading the Los Angeles Clippers by 12 points with under four minutes remaining.
    • In a recent development, did Wemby just...
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that remember at the end of Space Jam, when Michael Jordan released himself off of the butt of a MonStar to dunk from the half-court line? Well, imagine the exact opposite of that play. Instead of an impossibly long dunk, Thursday night's NBA action gave us an impossibly short jumper.

    Let's set the stage here. The San Antonio Spurs are leading the Los Angeles Clippers by 12 points with under four minutes remaining. Victor Wembanyama is alone under the basket. He led the NBA with 71 dunks on the season to that point. Nobody else, as of the beginning of play Thursday, had reached even 50. But Wembanyama does not take this opportunity to slam down dunk No. 72, at least not intentionally. No, San Antonio's Martian with an eight-foot wingspan jumps directly in front of the basket... and flicks his wrist downward in what was seemingly a shooting motion. It swishes through the rim. Two points.

    In a recent development, did Wemby just... shoot it from above the rim??? 🤯😲 pic.twitter.com/1YDxy8mwy8.

    Officially, it will count as dunk No. 72 on the season for Wembanyama. Unofficially, as coined by Spurs broadcaster Sean Elliott, it was the first "shunk" of his season. Or, well, perhaps anyone's. It takes a perfect storm of circumstances to create a shunk: an uncommonly large basketball player, a lane open enough to ensure no defensive resistance, and perhaps rarest of all, a center disinterested in dunking.

    It has been revealed that that begs an important question: what compelled this maneuver? Well, as is so often the case, necessity was the mother of invention.

    Wembanyama has a blister on his right hand. He doesn't know when exactly it came, but he knows where it came from. "It definitely came from dunking a lot," he told reporters after the game Thursday. The math here checks out. Wembanyama dunked 178 times in 64 games last season. That's around 2.8 dunks per game. Even if we discount the shunk, he's at 71 dunks through 16 games this season, or around 4.4.

    It has been revealed that fortunately for the Spurs, Wembanyama has no plans to stop dunking, "but if I can avoid it, I would," he stated after the win. The blister, according to Wembanyama, is quite painful. You'd hardly know it from watching him play. Wembanyama is averaging career-highs in points, rebounds, blocks and field goal percentage thus far this season. He is leading a 13-3 Spurs team that is tied for the NBA's best record thus far, and along with Luka Dončić, he is one of the two heavy favorites to win this season's MVP award.

    According to recent reports, if he's looking for a fringe benefit here, the "shunk" might save him from the "run and just dunk" esque criticism that Giannis Antetokounmpo recevied during his MVP pursuits. This is genuine innovation in the short-distance conversion space. Innovation is rarely in short supply in San Antonio. Earlier this week, Wembanyama threw himself multiple passes off of the backboard in a single quarter. Every time you turn on a Spurs game, there's a real chance Wembanyama does something you've never seen before, and the shunk is no exception.

    • According to recent reports, bucks fans are supposed to stay standing until their team scores.
    • In a recent development, lillard's return to the court where he tore his Achilles a little more than a year ago -- which came just one night after the Bucks faced Giannis Antetokounmpo for the first time -- was yet another reminder of how wrong things have gone in Milwaukee over the last few years, and the grim future the franchise faces.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    MILWAUKEE -- "Stay up! Stay up!" The pleading voice of the Milwaukee Bucks' in-arena host was still echoing around a half-empty Fiserv Forum early on Thursday night when Damian Lillard knocked the ball away from Tyler Herro and coasted the other way for the first points of a 124-114 Portland Trail Blazers victory.

    According to recent reports, bucks fans are supposed to stay standing until their team scores. Those who are still proud enough to show up and follow the tradition get much more time on their feet than they did when Lillard was still in a Bucks jersey. They waited nearly two minutes on Thursday, then spent the next two hours watching Lillard pour in a season-high 33 points to send the Bucks to their 12th consecutive defeat and an NBA-worst 1-15 record.

    In a recent development, lillard's return to the court where he tore his Achilles a little more than a year ago -- which came just one night after the Bucks faced Giannis Antetokounmpo for the first time -- was yet another reminder of how wrong things have gone in Milwaukee over the last few years, and the grim future the franchise faces. Jrue Holiday's 22 points, seven assists and four steals on Thursday only added to the misery.

    Trail Blazers coach Micah Nori joked pre-game that this might be the "first and only revenge game" of Lillard's career. Afterward, Lillard, who was waived by Milwaukee mere weeks after his injury, downplayed its significance. It was just a normal game, he remarked, "other than it just being the first time that I've played on the court since I got hurt.".

    In a recent development, lillard's aggressiveness may have suggested otherwise, but both he and Nori attributed his approach to the Blazers being without Deni Avdija and Ja Morant. "When you're down your next two top scorers, I knew that I would need to be a little more assertive," Lillard mentioned.

    No one knew what to expect from the 36-year-old Lillard this season after such an extended layoff, but through 15 games he's averaging 20.9 points and 4.1 assists, and shooting 35.8% from 3-point range.

    "He still has the stop and go, which has made him so effective. Obviously, the jumper and his legs. I think the biggest difference would be, 18 months without playing, I don't know if you want to call it rust or timing, that's the only thing you see," Nori said pre-game. "And it's coming back. Every single day, you can see it. But when you're playing against the best athletes in the world, the best players in the world, the best defenders in the world, it is gonna take you a little bit of time to get back up to speed. But as far as from a health standpoint, you really wouldn't know it.".

    The moment Lillard's Achilles snapped 572 days ago during Game 4 of a first-round playoff series against the Indiana Pacers, everyone knew it was a turning point for the Bucks. But no one could have foreseen everything that's happened since then.

    The Bucks waived Lillard not even two months after the injury and stretched the remaining $113 million on his contract over five years in order to create the cap space to sign Myles Turner to a four-year, $107 million deal with a player option for the 2028-29 season.

    It has been revealed that "I thought it was pretty simple. I was injured. I wasn't gonna be available to play last season, and the team was focused on bringing somebody in here that they could pair with Giannis so that they could still be a competitive team, which is the business side of it," Lillard said Thursday morning at shootaround. "I saw it for what it was, and I moved on.".

    Recent findings suggest that the desperate ploy to keep Antetokounmpo happy didn't work. Now, both he and Lillard are gone, while Turner is averaging just 7.1 points and six rebounds on 36.2% shooting this season and the Bucks are still paying Lillard $22,516,603 each year through 2030. If you break that figure down by game, they gave Lillard $247,592 for the trouble of beating them on Thursday while Turner sat and watched with a shoulder injury.

    It has been revealed that five years ago, Antetokounmpo and Holiday were carrying the Larry O'Brien trophy through the streets of Milwaukee. Three years ago, Holiday was traded for Lillard. Just over a year ago, Lillard tore his Achilles in the most recent playoff game at Fiserv Forum and was waived. Now, Antetokounmpo is leading the 9-6 Miami Heat, who sit in fourth place in the Eastern Conference, while Holiday and Lillard are together in the same backcourt for the 10-5 Trail Blazers, who occupy sixth in the Western Conference.

    And the Bucks, who haven't won a playoff series since 2022 and don't own their own first-round pick until 2031, the year after they'll stop paying Lillard? They're 1-15, have the worst record in the league and are in the midst of the second-longest losing streak in franchise history. Oh, and they're also under investigation for salary cap circumvention relating to Gary Trent Jr.'s $64 million contract.

    No team has a bleaker present or future than the Bucks.

    In a recent development, just how bad are the vibes in Milwaukee? Major Goolsby's, a sports bar down the street from the arena, has started running a new promotion on game nights: everything's free if the Bucks win.

    Unai Emery’s Aston Villa 2.0 remain under construction but from the wreckage of a difficult summer there has emerged a potential star for the future.

    In a recent development, emery may have now suffered four successive defeats in the Super Cup, yet the major positive from a balmy night in Salzburg was the performance of teenage forward Brian Madjo. Aged 17 years and 212 days, Madjo became the youngest player to start and score in this continental showpiece, just over a week after he was given permission to play for his club.

    In a recent development, signed from Metz for £10m in January, Madjo had been prevented from playing because of Fifa’s rules on the international transfer of minors. Villa’s appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport to have him registered was upheld on August 4 and what a prospect he appears.

    Born in Enfield but raised in Luxembourg, there has been a huge buzz around him since his arrival in the latest year.

    Paris St-Germain have produced an abundance of talented teenagers over the years and Madjo did not look out of place here.Désiré Doué’s second-half strike secured PSG the Super Cup – contested by the winners of the Champions League and Europa League – for the second successive year, but Emery will have seen enough to give him renewed confidence.

    Desire Doue puts PSG 2-1 ahead despite originally being flagged offside 🫣📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vnMIZCWJaj.

    His team played with all the resilience and bravery that has become a trademark, epitomised by the powerful Madjo and another teenager in midfielder George Hemmings.

    Emery stated: “Brian has scored goals for us in pre-season and has shown his capacity to work in our idea. I am so happy because the young players were involved in our work and not playing last season.

    “Of course there is still work to do but they showed they can play with us. They have responded fantastically and will then feel the confidence. With a loss you can never be happy but overall I am proud of all the players and everything we’ve done. Some changes will be needed but we’re confident.”.

    According to recent reports, this was a fine Villa performance to silence the doom merchants who have been fearing a troubled season. After the painful sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, Villa are clearly a team in transition. They are operating under restrictions to comply with Uefa’s financial rules and there is still the possibility of another key player leaving before the transfer deadline day.

    England centre-back Ezri Konsa remains a priority target for Premier League champions Arsenal, and was absent here. Konsa, Emiliano Martínez and Ollie Watkins were all granted extended leave after their participation in the World Cup, which has done little to ease the fears of supporters over more departures. The trio will return to training this weekend.

    According to recent reports, while some outsiders are predicting a difficult season for Villa, do not bother telling Emery. He has turned putting noses out of joint into an art form since sweeping into Villa Park and with him around anything feels possible.

    In a recent development, the Basque remains optimistic about the future and those hopes will only have been underlined by the performance of Madjo. He bullied PSG centre-back Willian Pacho for much of the evening and even managed to steal the limelight from PSG’s magician Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

    Hemmings, 19, has emerged from the academy and already made a real impression on his manager. Despite the high regard for those youngsters, this always appeared likely to be a tough proposition against a full-strength PSG team. Indeed, before this game in Salzburg only 39 per cent of Europa League winners have beaten their Champions League rivals in this fixture.

    The French champions did start slowly, but had been cranking up the pressure before taking a 20th minute lead with a spectacular strike from their Georgian superstar.

    Doué forced a save from Marco Bizot and, after Villa failed to clear, the loose ball landed in the path of Kvaratskhelia, who cut inside on the left to his right foot before smashing a shot into the roof of the net.

    Khvicha Kvaratskhelia puts PSG 1-0 ahead vs Aston Villa 🔥📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/BIf8njpaSx.

    It was a strike of sheer power and accuracy, catching Bizot by surprise. PSG briefly appeared in control, but Villa responded superbly. In 17 minutes they created six goal-scoring chances before the outstanding Madjo finally made one of them count.

    It has been revealed that before his goal, he had narrowly missed the target twice with a pair of headers from John McGinn’s crosses. Villa also had another opportunity 10 minutes before half-time, when Pacho’s mistake allowed Hemmings to run from the centre circle unopposed. As he entered the penalty area, the PSG defenders had raced back to recover and a promising moment ended with Madjo curling a shot wide.

    Brian Madjo with a substantial chance to put Aston Villa level 😮📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pqsC5Hor15.

    PSG goalkeeper Matvey Safonov then produced his first save just before the break, turning away Boubacar Kamara’s close-range header. Villa did carve out another golden chance when Madjo’s strength took hm past Pacho, but he hit the outside of the post. Madjo’s moment did come, though, as he once again bullied Pacho to divert a McGinn cross into the roof of the net.

    Brian Madjo at 17-years-old scores in the UEFA Super Cup Final 🤯📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/PccX7FxjAr.

    Industry observers note that villa were buoyant, but it was PSG who scored the crucial second goal after Doué was awarded the goal following a VAR review. Doué was sent clear down the right by substitute Ousmane Dembélé and confidently beat Bizot, with reviews concluding that he had been played onside by Matty Cash.

    The game was refereed by Omar Artan, the Somali referee who was supposed to officiate at the World Cup but was denied entry to the United States.

    In a recent development, it became rather fractious as time began to tick away, with McGinn booked after complaining over the placement of a free-kick. Madjo was replaced by Tammy Abraham with 17 minutes left and this will be an evening he will never forget.

    Recent findings suggest that what will we learn from the “upcoming Aston Villa” tonight? After the sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, this is a Villa team in transition.

    It has been revealed that unai Emery virtually admitted last night it could be another slow start to the season, like last year. Villa face a full-strength PSG team hoping to win the Super Cup for the second time in a row.

    In a recent development, I don’t think we can take much from this result tonight, whatever it is. Villa cannot be properly judged until the window closes. Don’t bother telling that to Unai Emery, though. He is ready to continue defying the doubters.

    Sources indicate that the Champions League and Europa League winners fight it out in the Uefa Super Cup in Salzburg as PSG take on Aston Villa. PSG took on English opposition in the Super Cup a year ago, when they played Tottenham. PSG fell 2-0 down in that game in Udine but scored two late goals to take it to penalties, where they won 4-3. These sides met in the Champions League knockout stages two seasons ago; PSG did progress from the quarter-final encounter as they went on to win the competition but not without a scare as Aston Villa did win at Villa Park and PSG only progressed 5-4 on aggregate. The two clubs have been involved in a transfer this week, with left-back Lucas Digne re-joining PSG from Aston Villa.

    Aston Villa have played in the Super Cup once before back in 1982 when they took in Barcelona. They lost the first leg 1-0 over at Camp Nou but fought back to win the second leg 3-0 at Villa Park to claim the trophy. Aston Villa were last in action out in the Far East last Friday, falling to a 2-1 defeat to Bayern Munich in Hong Kong. It has been a big summer of change at the club, with key starters like Morgan Rogers and Youri Tielemans departing and the likes of Alejandro Garnacho and Joao Gomes arriving.

    “I feel like the club is in a upcoming era, with this possibility to fight for trophies,” Unai Emery told Uefa. “We are trying to be successful through, firstly, [building] a winning team, and then aiming for the positive consequences after it; winning trophies. To play the UEFA Super Cup is another opportunity to be there, the opportunity to win a trophy, to play against Paris Saint-Germain; the [best] team in the world now and another team we can compare [ourselves] with.”.

    Emery has confirmed that Ezri Konsa, Ollie Watkins and Emiliano Martinez will not be involved as they are still on their breaks following the World Cup.

    PSG have now won back-to-back Champions Leagues, beating Arsenal in the final last season. They have only played a couple of friendlies in pre-season, losing 3-0 to Mallorca before drawing 1-1 against Manchester United. Luis Enrique’s side will take on Lens in the Trophée des Champions on Sunday before kicking off the defence of their Ligue 1 title at home to Rennes.

    Industry observers note that “I focus on renewing that desire to win again,” Enrique told Uefa. “It is difficult to keep winning. Right now, we have a unique challenge; something that is practically unprecedented in the history of European football, which is to draw level with Real Madrid if we can win a third consecutive Champions League. No-one in history has won three in a row, only Real Madrid. We can equal them. But I do not think there is any team in Europe more motivated than us.

    “No-one rules out PSG any more. Two years ago, it was impossible to put us among the favourites; not impossible, but we were not one of the favourites. Now, no one would say that Paris Saint-Germain are not the favourites. That is something we have earned, but if we are going to maintain that position, we have to work even harder.”.

    In a recent development, PSG have added Monaco winger Maghnes Akliouche and Digne to their ranks this summer. They are also pushing to sign Ferran Torres from Barcelona and Mika Godts from Ajax. Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye have both been linked with moves to Liverpool but have been included in their squad for tonight’s game, as have Akliouche and Digne.

    NBA One-Month Superlatives: MVP, top rookie, best surprise and fresh title predictions

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 18 min read (3696 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~18 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Memphis Grizzlies pounded the Golden State Warriors on Thursday to move to 12-4 on the year.
    • And then there's been everything in between.
    • So much has happened over the first month of the season that we're going to pause for a moment, take stock of what we've seen, and hand out a few bits of early hardware.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Memphis Grizzlies pounded the Golden State Warriors on Thursday to move to 12-4 on the year. The Grizzlies were a popular pick to surprise some folks this year, but nobody saw this coming. On the other hand, Luka Dončić and Victor Wembanyama are lording over the league like castles on a hill, and that wasn't so hard to predict.

    And then there's been everything in between. All the injuries, perhaps most notably. The Raptors and Pacers entered the season being hyped as upcoming-look contenders, but so far Tyrese Haliburton and Kawhi Leonard have combined to play six games. The Warriors went from an eight-game winning streak to the Washington Generals with one Stephen Curry abdominal tweak. The 76ers can't lose a clutch game in a maze. Paul George has been reborn in Boston. The Rockets are flying. The Heat are getting hot. The Knicks' fog is lifting. It feels like Damian Lillard never left the Blazers. This rookie class looks potentially historic.

    So much has happened over the first month of the season that we're going to pause for a moment, take stock of what we've seen, and hand out a few bits of early hardware. Who's been the MVP so far? What about the best rookie? What has been the biggest surprise? Biggest disappointment? In light of what we've seen so far, is anyone ready to change their preseason Finals pick? Our staff took a collective shot at tackling these topics below.

    It has been revealed that botkin: It's a two-horse race so far and nobody is going to argue much with either pick, but I'm going with Luka. I thought the Lakers would be good (their over/under 46.5 win total was way too low), but not tied-for-the-best-record-in-the-league good. Likewise, we all knew Luka would score huge, but not damn-near 40 PPG huge. Throw in north of seven assists and seven rebounds and almost two steals a night, and the numbers are simply too overwhelming to deny.

    It has been revealed that gonzalez: This is really tough. Luka Dončić has been playing some of the best basketball of his career, and he's a huge reason why the Lakers are down as my big surprise over the first month of the season. But for as good as Luka has been, Wemby's two-way dominance gives him the edge here. Wembanyama had the second 50-point game of his career against the Mavs, and he's averaging a 28-point double-double on 53% shooting from the field. He's also blocking an outrageous 4.1 shots per game and averaging more than a steal per outing. There's no answer for him at either end of the floor.

    Kalland: Wemby's been awesome but for the first month it's gotta be Luka. He's averaging 38 points per game on 47/38/86 splits! The Lakers are 13-3 in spite of defensive concerns, and it's because Dončić is out of his mind. What's amazing is he's going to have to keep up this ridiculous pace to win MVP and for the Lakers to remain at the top of the West. I'm excited to see how long he can maintain this level.

    In a recent development, maloney: I won't argue with anyone who picks Luka Dončić when he's averaging nearly 40 points per game, but I'm going with Wembanyama because of his two-way dominance. He's third in scoring, fourth in rebounding and first in blocks by a significant margin. The 1.7 blocks-per-game gap between Wembanyama (3.9) and Donovan Clingan (2.2), who sits in second, is as significant as the gap between Clingan and Dean Wade (0.5), who ranks 102nd in the league. In 483 minutes with Wembanyama on the floor this season, the Spurs have a 98.7 defensive rating; in 290 minutes without him, they have a 123.4 defensive rating. Overall, Wembanyama has an unfathomable +41.5 net rating differential.

    Quinn: Dončić is flirting with 40 points per game. He's leading the NBA in both 3-point attempts and free throws. He's the undisputed engine of the NBA's best offense, one that dies whenever he rests. The Lakers have the NBA's best record because Luka Dončić is on their team. That's it. They're average at basically everything else: rebounding, defense, you name it. But their offense dominates because he is on their team. Victor Wembanyama has much more to work with around him. No one else is even in their galaxy, though Stephen Curry might've had a case had he stayed healthy.

    Salerno: I've been pleasantly surprised with the Lakers so far. The pieces are working together nicely. However, the Lakers obviously wouldn't obvousuly be this good without Dončić, who is somehow taking his game to an entirely new level. He's on a mission to win MVP. He's been the best player in the league for the first month of the season. I think this will be the year he finally wins the award.

    In a recent development, botkin: I actually think Darius Acuff's numbers are actually too good in the sense that voters can't fathom a rookie averaging 26 and 7 without it being some fishy gimmick. It's not a gimmick. He just has total control of an NBA offense, which would make any player's numbers go up, Luka Dončić included. That said, Lendeborg has been better as both a real go-to player on a real team and from a scoring efficiency standpoint. The honeymoon has been heavily interrupted with Stephen Curry's injury as the Warriors look, well, like the Kings. But as of now Lendeborg deserves the award. Long term, I'm really watching Darryn Peterson as Utah's season promptly circles the drain. His numbers are rising quickly, and it may not be long before his development becomes Utah's undisputed top priority.

    Sources indicate that gonzalez: Lendeborg picked a fight with Luka in his very first game as a pro, trash-talked while guarding the Lakers superstar, then noted he lost all respect for him afterward. He stepped into the starting lineup and immediately looked like he belonged for an injury-plagued Warriors team that sorely needed his presence. And he was so unnerved by a blowout loss to the Spurs that he chopped off his hair, leaving Steve Kerr to tell the media "apparently that's his response to getting beat by 40, is to go right to the barber." His personality alone wins him the award. The numbers are good, too.

    Sources indicate that kalland: This rookie class has lived up to the hype so far, but right now I have to give the edge to the Warriors rookie sensation. Lendeborg came into the league talking that talk, and while he's put his foot in his mouth here and there, he's largely walked the walk to back it up. What separates him from the likes of Darius Acuff and Cameron Boozer at the moment is his combination of productivity and efficiency. But we've already seen that take a dip without Stephen Curry so there is certainly an opportunity for others to make up ground as the Warriors struggle without their top star.

    Sources indicate that maloney: Lendeborg has started to fade a bit, and so have the Warriors since Steph Curry went down with an oblique injury, but the No. 11 pick has still done enough to earn the nod ahead of Darius Acuff and Cameron Boozer. Everyone liked the Lendeborg pick for the Warriors, but no one expected this. He's come in and immediately established himself as their second-best player while doing a little bit of everything. He's second among rookies in scoring, second in rebounding, fifth in assists and tied for fourth in steals, all while shooting 37.2% from 3-point range.

    Industry observers note that quinn: Cameron Boozer is probably trending toward winning. His 3-point shooting is coming around, his interior scoring is progressing, and he does all of the little things everyone promised. Darius Acuff has the biggest numbers, but they're fake. Not fake in the empty calories sense, but fake in that all of the other rookies are being asked to play roles on real basketball teams, whereas Sacramento has elected to devote its entire season to Acuff's development by letting him do basically whatever he wants. If we're simply naming the best rookie thus far this season, though, the answer is obviously Yaxel Lendeborg. Things have gotten harder with Stephen Curry sidelined, but Lendeborg has resuscitated Golden State's postseason ambitions. He's scoring efficiently, shouldering an enormous defensive load and has fit into a system that is notoriously tricky for the wrong kinds of players. Boozer may get there by the end of the season, but for now, this is Yaxel's trophy.

    Salerno: In my rookie rankings released earlier this week, I had Yaxel Lendeborg No. 1. However, I would give strong consideration to Acuff because he is being asked to do more than any other rookie in his class. He is putting up elite numbers on a very bad Kings team that would be even worse if he wasn't in the lineup. I don't think you can go wrong with any of the top contenders. Darryn Peterson has also played very well as of late and will end up being in the mix down the stretch.

    Botkin: So many good options here. Obviously the Grizzlies, who are probably the correct answer. I certainly didn't foresee Minnesota holding this tightly to the rope without Anthony Edwards. But I'm going with the 76ers, who felt like a team that was going to take a while to figure things out but instead are out to a 13-3 record. There are some qualifiers. A perfect 11-0 mark in clutch games is unsustainable, and they can't keep digging themselves into holes (six comeback wins from at least 10 down). But the bottom line is this is a team that looks like it has played together for far longer than it has. The roles clarified almost immediately. Joel Embiid hasn't gotten hurt yet. There's a mental toughness to this team that I suppose makes sense given the individual players we're talking about, but collectively this thing is way more tied together than I thought possible this early in the season.

    Recent findings suggest that gonzalez: There weren't many people outside of Los Angeles who predicted the Lakers would be atop the Western Conference a month into the season. There might not have been that many inside Los Angeles either. The skepticism can be forgiven considering the Lakers bid goodbye to arguably the greatest player of all time during the summer, then overhauled a large portion of the roster. In came Walker Kessler, Quentin Grimes, Collin Sexton, Sandro Mamukelashvili and Matisse Thybulle, among others. After the reconstruction, head coach JJ Redick noted that for the first time in his tenure "the pieces actually fit together." That's been the case so far on the offensive end. The Lakers are first in points per game and third in offensive rating. It definitely helps that Luka Dončić is playing some of the best basketball of his career and leading the league in scoring by a wide margin. While Dončić battles Victor Wembanyama for MVP frontrunner status, his Lakers are in a race with the Spurs for the top slot in the West. The former isn't much of a surprise, but the latter certainly is.

    Kalland: Yes, the Grizzlies have faced a very generous schedule through the first month of the season, but even with that context, no one predicted a 12-4 start with Ty Jerome hanging out among the league's leading scorers. Cam Boozer's a strong ROY candidate (and is slowly improving his shooting efficiency) and the Grizzlies just keep finding diamonds in the rough to maintain competitiveness. They've got eight guys averaging 10+ points per game and are top 10 in offensive and defensive rating. Reality may arrive soon, but even so, this hot start has given them a great chance at emerging as a Play-In squad in the West.

    Sources indicate that maloney: The NBA intellegencia was high on the Grizzlies coming into the season, but in the sense that they would surpass their win total projection and make a run at the Play-In Tournament. Instead, they've jumped out to a 12-4 start, which has them in fourth place in the Western Conference and is good for the fifth-best record in the league. They lead the league in offensive rating (121.2) and are third in net rating (+9.9) behind only the Spurs and the Celtics. Even though they've had the easiest schedule in the league thus far, this is still remarkable.

    Quinn: For four games with Anthony Edwards, the Timberwolves looked like the NBA's best offense. Then their best player got hurt ... and they became the NBA's best defense. They're hardly slouching as scorers either. LaMelo Ball's playmaking has facilitated breakout years for Jaden McDaniels and Ayo Dosunmu. Jonathan Kuminga is making 3s and defending like the Warriors always wanted him to. Minnesota's transition from moodiness to giddiness is palpable whenever they play, and when they get Edwards back, they're going to be terrifying.

    Salerno: Here is a wild stat for you: Cameron Boozer has a 159-21 record across games in high school, college and the NBA (during the first month of the season). He is the ultimate winner who elevates his respective teams to greater heights. Between Boozer being firmly in the Rookie of the Year race and Ty Jerome making a case as the Most Improved Player, the Grizzlies have been quite entertaining to watch. Memphis has pushed the right buttons.

    Botkin: I'm probably a little biased on this one. I'm a lifelong Warriors fan and figured they would stink this year, but I allowed myself to get my hopes up with the way the team came out of the gate. I should've known better. As soon as Curry went down, which was probably inevitable, the Warriors turned into one of the worst teams in the league. It's a complete bummer. Hopefully he won't be out too much longer, and the Warriors can pick back up where he left off, but this is just a harsh reminder of how thin the margin is for this team, and it's just not likely to go their way over the long haul. If I was born in Indiana, I would say the same thing about Tyrese Haliburton's injury. Same goes for the Toronto fans with Kawhi only managing two games so far. All the injuries stink. But Curry's has hit the hardest.

    Gonzalez: Moving to the 3-2-1 system was unnecessary. The league overcorrected for last year's perfect tanking storm and didn't account for a simple truth of basketball: sometimes teams are just bad. No amount of tinkering is going to stop that. More than half the teams in the East are under .500. The West has four more such teams, bringing the total league-wide to 12. Adam Silver didn't want to incentivize tanking, but by putting too much of the league's thumb on the scale, they've made it harder on the worst teams to get better. Not to mention that the odd entertainment value of fans checking their lottery odds in the tank wars sideshow has been somewhat stripped away. [Stands up and repeats himself yet again] Tanking wasn't actually a problem.

    Kalland: The injuries so far this season have been brutal. Just about every team you'd point to as a disappointment -- Utah, Indiana, Toronto -- can point to injuries as a major reason for their early struggles. The frustrating thing is there's not an easy solve to the injury issue (schedule length is hard to blame for injuries in the first month) and every year it feels like we're playing injury roulette to determine who can and can't be a contender. The wheel started spinning earlier than usual in 2026-27.

    Industry observers note that maloney: I'm going with Robby here. The absurd amount of injuries, coupled with who is getting injured, has been the story of the season so far. You could form an All-Star team with all of the guys who have gone down with multi-week ailments: Jalen Williams, Chet Holmgren, Anthony Edwards, Tyrese Haliburton, Paolo Banchero, Kawhi Leonard, Stephen Curry, Austin Reaves, Dylan Harper, Jalen Duren, Lauri Markkanen, Jaren Jackson Jr., Kon Knueppel, Ja Morant, Caleb Wilson, Cason Wallace.

    Sources indicate that quinn: Look, we knew Charlotte was taking a step back when the team traded LaMelo Ball. The Hornets have been plagued by injuries all season. Some of this can be explained. Fine. Their offense still makes me want to vomit. No team turns the ball over more often. No team shoots less efficiently. No team is forced to take more shots in the last four seconds of the shot clock. No team leaves you feeling as though you're watching a panicked 14-year-old try to play minutes for the varsity squad more often. I had very high hopes for No. 1 option Brandon Miller. I trusted the system Charles Lee built last season. I figured they'd be worse, but still respectable, because this organization has displayed a genuine, systemic competence over the past few years. I think that will win out in the end. For now, I pity the poor souls in Charlotte buying tickets to these games, because they're quite nearly unwatchable.

    Salerno: Yes, Utah has been bad this season, largely due to the injury bug, but I was bullish on this team heading into the season. I had Utah finishing sixth in the West and making the playoffs outright. Instead, Utah is heading toward the lottery again, where it doesn't even own its own first-round pick in what should end up being a lackluster draft. The organization's top priority for the remainder of the season is developing Darryn Peterson.

    Botkin: Spurs over Knicks. The Spurs are the clear Western Conference favorite with all the OKC injuries. The Wolves, Lakers and Rockets deserve to be in the conversation, but they're all second-paragraph entries. It's the Spurs until they get hit with some major injury, too, but let's not jinx it. In the East, I could make a case for four teams. The 76ers have the late-game goods and individual creation that is exponentially impactful in the postseason. The Celtics look incredible with Paul George flourishing. The Pistons are just flat-out tough and they've been doing it without Jalen Duren. But I'm still picking the Knicks, who are starting to come out of their fog. They are so perfectly built for the playoffs, and remember, they weren't a great regular-season team last year, either.

    Gonzalez: Spurs over Celtics. After losing their first two games to start the season, the Spurs look every bit as good as they did during last season's run to the finals -- if not better. The three-guard starting unit hasn't slowed them down at all, and Wemby has been unreal at both ends of the floor. And while the Celtics took a lot of heat in the immediate aftermath of the Jaylen Brown for Paul George trade, we all should have known that they would still be among the best teams in the East this season. Both franchises are smart and steady. Meeting this summer would make for an excellent Finals.

    Kalland: Spurs over Celtics. I have to stick with my preseason Finals prediction because it's not every year a preseason pick still looks that good a month in. The Spurs look like a juggernaut, and their top competitor in the West, the OKC Thunder, will once again (likely) be without Jalen Williams for the playoffs. We'll see what the Timberwolves look like when Anthony Edwards returns, but for now it still feels like San Antonio and everyone else. In the East, I felt good about this Celtics team entering the season, and nothing has changed my belief they have what it takes to win the conference.

    Maloney: Spurs over Celtics. I picked Thunder over Celtics ahead of the season, in large part because of how difficult it has been for teams to get back to the Finals in consecutive seasons during this parity era. But now that the Thunder have been decimated with injuries, the Spurs have what appears to be a clear path through the West. I'll stick with the Celtics in the East, which has not been anywhere near as good as we expected this season.

    Recent findings suggest that quinn: Spurs over Knicks. Oklahoma City's injuries are really all that's changed to me. I don't think the Lakers have the defense or frontcourt depth to win three straight series in the West. I don't think the Rockets will be able to create good enough shots. I need to see Ball prove it in a playoff setting before I trust Minnesota. The star-studded 76ers have thus far been clutch merchants. The underlying numbers are lower on them than their record suggests. The opposite is true for Boston, who is blowing everyone out of the gym, but is going to have issues creating shots off of the dribble in the playoffs and defending man-to-man against the best offenses. I have an eyebrow quirked at Indiana and Toronto when they get their best players back. I'll reengage with the Thunder if and when they cash in some of their trade chips. For now, though, nothing has convinced me that last year's finalists are going to be dethroned. The Knicks and Spurs are the most complete teams in their respective conferences, and I'd expect San Antonio to learn from last June's defeat in a revenge series this time around.

    Salerno: 76ers over Timberwolves. Yes, I'm switching it up. I had the Thunder beating the 76ers in my preseason prediction, but I'm not sure OKC has enough firepower to make a deep run given their injuries. Minnesota is staying afloat even though Anthony Edwards is set to miss more time. LaMelo Ball has been fantastic this season. When Edwards gets back, I'm excited to see them play again. As for the East, it's really a toss-up to say who will make it out of the conference. Boston has been great. Detroit is playing good basketball. The Knicks and Heat are looking better. I still trust Philly's roster over all of them.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, if there is any truth to the adage that the NFL season does not truly start until Thanksgiving, then now is the time to start taking the playoff race seriously. As the calendar turns to Week 12 and a loaded holiday slate, all seven seeds in both conferences are up for grabs, and there are a number of teams beyond the current cut line that could not only make their way into the bracket but also compete for home-field advantage in the postseason.

    Anyone that aims to lock up a first-round bye in the NFC has to get through the San Francisco 49ers, which is a daunting task considering how dominant they appeared on the Week 11 edition of "Sunday Night Football.".

    And in the AFC, the Jacksonville Jaguars learned a difficult lesson on Sunday about how slim the margins are in the race for the No. 1 seed when they suffered a costly setback against the Newly introduced York Giants.

    With seven weeks of regular-season action to go, here is a snapshot of the playoff picture in both NFL conferences.

    It has been revealed that remaining schedule: vs. Chiefs, at Patriots, at Packers, vs. Bears, at Broncos, at Dolphins, vs. Jets.

    The only blemish on the Bills' resume is a three-point divisional loss to the Patriots, but that should not come back to bite them in the AFC East race as they hold a commanding four-game lead. It does make them vulnerable in the battle for the conference's No. 1 seed, though. The schedule is about to stiffen up following a four-game stretch in which Josh Allen feasted on beleaguered opponents and the defense corrected its early-season woes by allowing no more than 12 points in any of those contests.

    Industry observers note that remaining schedule: at Steelers, vs. Dolphins, at Jets, at Raiders, vs. Bills, at Patriots, vs. Chargers.

    Recent findings suggest that that the Broncos fended off Fernando Mendoza and the Raiders was critical for Denver's chances of winning the AFC West. Sean Payton's squad holds a tiebreaker over the Chiefs thanks to their higher win percentage against common opponents. It was a rare win by double digits for a team that is prolific at squeaking out victories by a one-score margin and increased the win streak to six games, which is tied for the longest in the conference.

    According to recent reports, remaining schedule: vs. Titans, at Bears, vs. Steelers, at Texans, at Cowboys, vs. Commanders, at Colts.

    Tech Report: The Timing Game – MH
