    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • An injury-time penalty from returning hero Raul Jimenez ensured Wolves came away with a point in their Championship opener after Blackburn had produced a comeback.
    • Wolves led through Marshall Munetsi’s cool finish on 18 minutes only for Sean McLoughlin’s first Blackburn goal to draw the visitors level on 27 minutes with a well-timed run and header.
    • The visitors turned the game around on 48 minutes through Andri Gudjohnsen’s close-range strike only for substitute Jimenez to level the game three minutes into injury time from the spot after Ryan Alebiosu handled the ball in the box.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    An injury-time penalty from returning hero Raul Jimenez ensured Wolves came away with a point in their Championship opener after Blackburn had produced a comeback.

    Wolves led through Marshall Munetsi’s cool finish on 18 minutes only for Sean McLoughlin’s first Blackburn goal to draw the visitors level on 27 minutes with a well-timed run and header.

    The visitors turned the game around on 48 minutes through Andri Gudjohnsen’s close-range strike only for substitute Jimenez to level the game three minutes into injury time from the spot after Ryan Alebiosu handled the ball in the box. Jimenez and his wife marked his return to Molineux by giving 5,000 fans black scarves emblazoned with the words ‘Si Senor’ - a nod to his song - and Jimenez did not disappoint as he rifled in his penalty.

    LATE DRAMA! 😱Raul Jimenez cooly converts from the penalty spot, deep into added time to save a point for Wolves 🔥 pic.twitter.com/5h2lMxcHNU.

    In a recent development, cesar Peixoto wants Wolves to play with their heads rather than their hearts after the home side rescued a late point in the first game of the Championship season following relegation. Wolves replaced Rob Edwards with Portuguese coach Peixoto during the summer and he felt his side’s loss of organisation allowed Blackburn to take control of the game.

    Peixoto noted: “One point is not what we want, we want three points. We lost some organisation in the second half and played more with our hearts and not our heads and brains.

    “We have to keep our mental stability during the 90 minutes because we’re better when we’re organised. We need to play our way with our identity. It’s a lesson for us to understand when we lose organisation it’s more difficult for us and more easy for the opposition.

    “We’re working hard to bring more solutions [into the club] but we need to work hard with the players we have. It’s the first game, there’s a lot to work on and a lot to improve.”.

    Tony Mowbray took charge of Blackburn in the league for the first time since returning to the club for a second stint in the dugout. Rovers recorded their lowest league finish since Mowbray’s first stint in charge of the club last term but the Blackburn boss is confident his side have enough to beat the drop and climb up the table this campaign.

    In a recent development, mowbray said: “Ultimately, it feels like a defeat, it’s a bit disappointing and a bit frustrating. I just felt a lot of decisions were starting to swing their way. It’s harsh to take, I don’t think they deserved a second goal. We asked the players to be brave and we were collectively very strong.

    Sources indicate that “Everybody has us relegated, probably on the back of finishing 20th last season and losing a couple of our better players and not spending much money, which is a good motivation for the team. We deserved to win the game, we highlighted there’s enough quality to give teams problems and I hope there’s help on the way [in the transfer window].”.

    The first chance of the season came the way of Blackburn as a cross-field pass found Alebiosu down the right, who floated a ball into the box only for an unmarked Oladipo Afolayan to head wide from eight-yards out.

    However, Wolves scored the first goal of the new campaign when Fer Lopez played a defence-splitting through ball into the path of Munetsi, who coolly found the net with a first time effort from the edge of the penalty area.

    "A vibrant Molineux rejoices!" 🎉Marshall Munetsi cooly slots home for Wolves to give them the lead on the opening night of the Championship season 🥶 pic.twitter.com/tVHdbNv3Hq.

    Blackburn drew level through an unlikely source just nine minutes later as McLoughlin headed in his first-ever goal in English football in more than 150 games when he met Ryoya Morishita’s cross from the right at the near post.

    The home side had chances to retake the lead before the break as Lopez curled a shot narrowly over the top from 20-yards while Kieran Trippier teed up Mateus Mane for a chance as the teenager found the top of the net from distance.

    Blackburn turned the game on its head minutes after the break as Gudjohnsen turned home Afolayan’s deflected ball in from the right from close range to stun Molineux into silence.

    "It's brilliantly worked by Blackburn Rovers!" 💥Andri Guðjohnsen finishes from close range to turn the game around and the visitors the lead 👏 pic.twitter.com/vkKQQezicK.

    Peixoto introduced Jimenez from the bench on the hour mark but even the Mexican could not lift Wolves with Blackburn comfortable for long periods as frustration grew in the stands.

    However, Alebiosu handled Jackson Tchatchoua’s cross from the left in injury time and the referee awarded a spot kick which allowed Jimenez to mark his Wolves return with an equaliser from 12-yards as he sent Balazs Toth the wrong way.

    Industry observers note that the 2026/27 Championship season kicks off at Molineux as Wolves host Blackburn, with the home side hoping to put the bad memories of last season firmly behind them. There are newly introduced playoff rules in place for this season, with six places now up for grabs in the play-offs.

    Recent findings suggest that wolves are aiming to return to the Premier League at the first attempt, having endured a miserable season in the top flight last year as they finished bottom with just three wins to their name. It has been a summer of change at the club as they chose to change managers. Rob Edwards lost his job in what was a shock move and was replaced by 46-year-old Cesar Peixoto, with this being his first head coaching position outside of his home country Portugal. Back in 2017/18, Wolves won the Championship title led by Peixoto’s compatriot Nuno Espirito Santo.

    “I am ready,” Peixoto told Wolves’ club website. “We have worked very hard during pre-season, and I think we have had a great pre-season. All the players have worked very, very hard and they understand what I want from them. I am ready and confident going into the first game. Football is football, whether it is in Portugal or England, but there are different characteristics to the game here. We have watched, observed and analysed the Championship. We did that work before I came to the club, so we know what to expect.

    “It is going to be a tough season with good teams, but we are prepared to fight for the three points game after game and week after week. We know what we want from the team and we know what our big goal is. We’re going to work very hard and fight to achieve that goal.”.

    Industry observers note that they have brought in vast experience on the player side in the shape of Kieran Trippier and Raul Jimenez, who is back at Molineux three years after leaving for Fulham. Although they have lost Brazilian midfielder Joao Gomes to Aston Villa, most of their squad has stayed intact as they pursue promotion back to the top flight. It is a special year for the club as they celebrate their 150th anniversary.

    According to recent reports, blackburn, led by experienced manager Tony Mowbray, did not enjoy a great season in the Championship last year, finishing down in 20th place and just five points above the relegation zone. 14 years have now passed since Blackburn last played in the top flight.

    It has been revealed that “I think it is a tough start,” Mowbray mentioned. “On paper, I would suggest the first couple of games, particularly, jumped out as a tough start. One of the Premier League sides from last season, away from home. They have got a very talented squad, a pretty expensive squad. They have got some very good individual talent. Yet, there is an argument to say they have not won many football matches in the last calendar year. So, what we get, we will have to wait and see.”.

    These sides last met in the FA Cup during the 2024/25 season, with Wolves winning that fourth-round tie 2-0 thanks to goals from Matheus Cunha and Gomes, both of whom are now plying their trade elsewhere. The omens would appear to be on Wolves’ side as they are unbeaten in their last eight league meetings with Blackburn. Both sides progressed to the second round of the League Cup last weekend, with Wolves beating Port Vale 3-0 and Blackburn overcoming Burton Albion 2-1.

    Industry News: Victor Wembanyama takes hypocritical jab at 'stat-padding peers' after hunting his own 50-piece

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (699 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, victor Wembanyama is hard to put into words.
    • Industry observers note that so here we go again, trying to write about the indescribable Wembanyama, who put 50 points, 19 boards, five blocks and four steals on the Pelicans on Saturday.
    • Just take a look at this guy making the greatest basketball players in the world look like children.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, victor Wembanyama is hard to put into words. Stephen Curry is the only player I can remember thinking of the same way in the post-Michael Jordan era. Nobody else. With Steph and Wemby, you can't fully describe what you've seen. You try, but in the end you just have to see them to understand. It's totally different than anything you've ever witnessed on a basketball court.

    Industry observers note that so here we go again, trying to write about the indescribable Wembanyama, who put 50 points, 19 boards, five blocks and four steals on the Pelicans on Saturday. It feels like we're qualifying one of his "first in history" stat lines about once a week, and indeed, Wembanyama is the first player since blocks and steals became an official stat in 1973 to record those single-game numbers.

    Just take a look at this guy making the greatest basketball players in the world look like children.

    VICTOR WEMBANYAMA BECOMES THE FIRST PLAYER SINCE 1973-74 TO RECORD 50+ PTS, 15+ REB, 4+ STL AND 5+ BLK IN A GAME!🤯 50 PTS🤯 18 REB🤯 5 BLK🤯 4 STL🤯 5 3PM🤯 32 MINSPURS WIN THEIR 14TH IN 15 GAMES. pic.twitter.com/lPKk3jYNjL.

    According to recent reports, before the halftime buzzer had even sounded, Wembanyama had already tallied 32 points, 13 rebounds, three steals and three blocks. That would be a career game for a lot of NBA players. He had played 18 minutes. You can only laugh at this point.

    What was even funnier, however, was Wembanyama's comment after the game, when he took a clear stab at, well, whoever he considers his "peers" to be by calling them out for, shall we say, unethical statistical pursuits.

    "It is very special," Wembanyama said of reaching the 50-point mark for the second time this season and third time in his career. "But unlike many of my peers, I'm not good at stat-padding. So I haven't reached it as many times as I should have.".

    Victor Wembanyama after scoring 50 points: “Unlike many of my peers, I'm not very good at statpadding.” pic.twitter.com/OAogFCa2oi.

    Industry observers note that so here's what's interesting about this little dig: Wembanyama was definitely guilty of stat-padding his way to 50 in this game. With just more than eight minutes remaining and the Spurs up by 24, Wembanyama could've stayed on the bench after the timeout. The Spurs have made a concerted effort to limit his minutes whenever possible this year. Even in the golden age of comebacks, this game was over.

    But Wemby stayed in and proceeded to take five straight shots on the next five possessions. He was hunting the 50. No question about it. He even admitted as much.

    "The greats of the game, they don't care [about stat-padding]," Wemby mentioned, via The Athletic. "I don't think Wilt [Chamberlain] thought about that when he had 98 points. ... That stepback 3, going right, that I took, it doesn't correlate with this. It didn't fit to the definition [of ethical basketball], for example. So I did try [to stat-pad] at the end.".

    Good on Wemby for acknowledging his own hypocrisy, but it raises the question: if you just did the very thing you are railing against, why take the jab in the first place? Every player who has been within range of 50 points has gone for it as long as it's not a competitive game in which quality shots still matter. It's not that significant a deal.

    In a recent development, but Wemby has done this before. In December of 2025, after the Spurs had just defeated the Thunder, he said, "I'm just glad to be part of something that's growing to be so beautiful — pure and ethical basketball.".

    Recent findings suggest that this was a definite jab at Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's foul-baiting. Wemby, meanwhile, has turned into one of the more theatrical floppers in the league. In almost every way, Wembanyama is different than any other basketball player in the world. But when it comes to this ethical, non-stat-padding basketball soapbox he has climbed upon on numerous occasions, the truth is he's just like everyone else. So enough with the jabs.

    NFL Thanksgiving schedule: What to know about Thanksgiving Eve, Turkey Day, and Black Friday games

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The NFL has cooked up something special for this year's Thanksgiving.
    • Each game has storylines big enough to fill any plate.
    • It has been revealed that what to know: Wednesday night is when Micah Parsons is expected to make his highly anticipated return following last year's season-ending injury.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The NFL has cooked up something special for this year's Thanksgiving. For the first time, a Thanksgiving Eve game has been added to the Thanksgiving week slate. It's essentially an appetizer for Thursday's triple-header feast, with the dessert coming Friday with the Black Friday game.

    Each game has storylines big enough to fill any plate. In order to keep up with everything, we've provided a rundown on how to follow the games in real time. We've also included the major thing to know for each matchup.

    It has been revealed that what to know: Wednesday night is when Micah Parsons is expected to make his highly anticipated return following last year's season-ending injury. If he plays, Parsons will share a field with reigning Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett and three-time DPOY recipient Aaron Donald. Talk about defensive star power.

    Recent findings suggest that in addition to Parsons, a storyline for this game will be which team can overcome the loss of other star players. The Rams will be without Puka Nacua after he underwent potentially season-ending knee surgery. His absence will likely lead to more opportunities for running backs Kyren Williams and Blake Corum, who have become arguably the NFL's best running back duo.

    According to recent reports, josh Jacobs, who missed Green Bay's Week 11 loss to the Vikings, was limited during Monday's practice as he continues to deal with a finger injury. Green Bay's running game has been non-existent this season without Jacobs.

    Industry observers note that what to know: While he's had a lot of success in Chicago, Ben Johnson is 0-2 against Detroit, his former team. Johnson's former boss, Dan Campbell, has won four straight games against Chicago, seven of his last eight in the series and has a 7-3 overall record against the Bears.

    Coaches aside, this is a matchup between two of the NFL's hottest teams. The Bears have won five straight games, while the Lions enter Thursday with a six-game winning streak. The winner of this game will take sole possession of first place in the NFC North.

    It has been revealed that it'll be especially interesting when the Lions' fifth-ranked offense is on the field against Chicago's sixth-ranked defense. Jahmyr Gibbs, who is one touchdown away from breaking Barry Sanders' NFL record for the most touchdowns by a player before his 25th birthday, should have his moments. He's facing a run defense that is just 25th in the NFL in average yards-per-carry allowed.

    What to know: Dallas is a sizable favorite, but there are several reasons to believe that the Eagles are ripe for an upset.

    It has been revealed that the Cowboys were 10-point favorites when they were upset by then-winless Tampa Bay Buccaneers back in Week 5. Dallas lost that game to a backup quarterback (rookie Jalon Daniels), and they'll face another backup Thursday in Joe Milton III, who used to play for America's Team. Milton just won his first career start Sunday against the Steelers. He made several clutch plays, including his third-down conversion to DeVonta Smith that iced the game.

    If Dallas wins on Thursday, it will be the first time it's won back-to-back games under Brian Schottenheimer. The Cowboys' inability to string together consecutive wins is yet another reason why Philadelphia could successfully play the role of spoiler.

    Sources indicate that what to know: This game will be billed as the latest chapter in the Josh Allen-Patrick Mahomes rivalry. Overall, the Allen-Mahomes series is tied up at five wins apiece, which makes Thursday night's game a rubber match. Allen is 0-4 against Mahomes-led teams in the playoffs, but he has a 5-1 record in regular-season starts against Mahomes that includes five straight victories.

    Recent findings suggest that both quarterbacks will look to put on a show, but the winner of this game will likely come down to which supporting cast outperforms the other. On paper, the Chiefs have a few advantages, most notably their second-ranked scoring defense that will look to exploit Allen's Kryptonite: turning the ball over. Allen has thrown nine interceptions this year, including five in his last four games.

    It'll be interesting to see how the Chiefs' young players fare in a big-time environment, especially Emmett Johnson, Kansas City's rookie running back, who has tallied consecutive 100-yard rushing performances while filling in for injured starter Kenneth Walker III.

    Sources indicate that what to know: This game is pretty simple. If the Steelers are going to pull off an upset, they're going to have to take advantage of Denver's suspect run defense and third-down offense. If they can't do either of those things, the Broncos will more than likely hand them their third straight loss.

    Jaylen Warren was having a monster season for Pittsburgh until he and the rest of the Steelers' offense hit a wall over the last two weeks. Pittsburgh's lack of depth at receiver has led defenses to crowd the line of scrimmage, leaving little running room for Warren and back mate Rico Dowdle.

    According to recent reports, A positive for Pittsburgh is the emergence of wideout Max Hurleman, who caught a team-high six passes for 61 yards and a score against the Eagles. Plus, the recent return of Roman Wilson and the possible return of Michael Pittman, who hasn't played since Week 4, are bright spots. The Steelers will also have DK Metcalf after the league decided not to suspend him following his ejection during Sunday's loss in Philadelphia.

    MLB rumors: Mets' Tarik Skubal follow-up, where Blue Jays turn now, plus Yankees, Phillies, Red Sox, more

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1124 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The offseason's biggest domino fell late Sunday evening: Tarik Skubal agreed to a nine-year, $450 million contract with the Mets.
    • In a recent development, it should be a busy week on the hot stove leading up to the expiration of the collective bargaining agreement at 11:59 p.m.
    • The Yankees and left-hander Brent Suter have agreed to a one-year contract worth $4 million, reports the Upcoming York Post.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The offseason's biggest domino fell late Sunday evening: Tarik Skubal agreed to a nine-year, $450 million contract with the Mets. It is far and away the richest pitching contract in history, crushing Yoshinobu Yamamoto's $325 million deal with the Dodgers. The Mets still have other things to address, including adding another starter, but they landed the winter's best free agent.

    In a recent development, it should be a busy week on the hot stove leading up to the expiration of the collective bargaining agreement at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec. 1. Here are our top 50 free agents and top 25 trade candidates, and the notable offseason dates and deadlines you need to know. Here now are Monday's hot stove happenings.

    The Yankees and left-hander Brent Suter have agreed to a one-year contract worth $4 million, reports the Upcoming York Post. Suter will make $3.75 million in 2026, and there's a $3.5 million club option for 2027 with a $250,000 buyout. He is the fourth reliever the Yankees have signed this offseason, joining David Bednar (accepted qualifying offer), Tim Hill, and Jonathan Loáisiga.

    In a recent development, with the bullpen mostly assembled, the Yankees figure to pivot to offense the rest of the offseason. They need a third base upgrade over Ryan McMahon and a right-handed hitting catcher to pair with the lefty-swinging Austin Wells. It seems likely the Yankees will go with Anthony Volpe at second base and Spencer Jones in center field, but those positions can be improved as well.

    The Mets have agreed to a deal with free agent first baseman Paul Goldschmidt, reports the Newly introduced York Post. It's a one-year deal worth $8 million, according to The Athletic. He will presumably pair with Jared Young in a first base platoon. We did not rank Goldschmidt, 39, among our top 50 free agents. He accepted a reduced role for the Yankees over the last two seasons and was a valuable clubhouse presence.

    At this point in his career, Goldschmidt is no longer an everyday player, but he remains a solid platoon bat. He hit .317/.402/.572 against lefties over the last two years, compared to .235/.271/.337 against righties. Goldschmidt can still play a nifty first base as well. The Mets received the worst first base production in the sport in 2027. Even late-career Goldschmidt should be an upgrade.

    It has been revealed that after missing out on Tarik Skubal, the Blue Jays are now believed to be prioritizing Freddy Peralta, according to MLB Network. Toronto has a very good one-two punch in Dylan Cease and José Soriano. Behind them are Spencer Arrighetti, Cody Ponce (returning from a torn ACL), Trey Yesavage, and maybe Jake Bloss and Ricky Tiedemann. There's room for another starter, for sure.

    Peralta, Michael King, and Trevor Rogers are the best available free agent starters now that Skubal has signed. Rogers declined the qualifying offer and is attached to draft pick compensation, which perhaps makes King or Peralta more desirable. Any of the three would boost a Blue Jays rotation that has upside but not much in the way of reliability behind Cease and Soriano.

    The Dodgers are not expected to aggressively pursue pitching help after losing out on Tarik Skubal, reports The Athletic. They're comfortable letting things play out and seeing what shakes loose among second- and third-tier free agents. As much as the Dodgers would have liked to retain Skubal, they're in a spot where they didn't absolutely need him.

    Despite this year's biceps and knee injuries, Shohei Ohtani is expected to pitch next season. He'll join Tyler Glasnow, Roki Sasaki, Blake Snell, and Yoshinobu Yamamoto in the rotation. Emmet Sheehan, Gavin Stone, and Justin Wrobleski are next in line, with prospects Jackson Ferris and Christian Zazueta not far away. The Dodgers could use another starter but aren't desperate for one.

    Recent findings suggest that the Mariners, Padres, and Phillies are among the teams interested in Red Sox outfielder Jarred Duran, according to MassLive. The Red Sox tendered Duran a contract at Friday's deadline and will now look to trade him. The Jake Bauers signing pushed Duran, who had a .266 on-base percentage in 2026, out of the regular lineup. A trade is the logical next step.

    Philadelphia and San Diego badly need outfield help and are obvious fits for Duran. Even if the Mariners manage to re-sign Randy Arozarena, they could use another outfielder, though Duran would be a less-than-stellar fit for a lineup that is already heavily left-handed. Regardless, it seems unlikely Duran will be with the Red Sox by the time Opening Day arrives.

    Industry observers note that the Blue Jays, Phillies, and Yankees are considered the favorites for Japanese slugger Teruaki Sato, reports MLB.com. The Cubs and Mets are believed to have interest as well. Sato primarily played third base for the Hanshin Tigers but is not regarded as a strong defender, and it is likely that he will play first base or a corner outfield spot in MLB.

    Industry observers note that this past season, Sato, 28 in March, hit .306/.383/.609 with 39 home runs and won Japan's Triple Crown. He is similar to Munetaka Murakami in that he has big left-handed power, swing-and-miss concerns, and defensive issues. Murakami is a much more patient hitter, however. Sato is an aggressive swinger and is unlikely to walk much or post a strong on-base percentage.

    The Blue Jays offered Tarik Skubal a nine-year contract in the $400 million range before he signed with the Mets, according to The Athletic. Meanwhile, the Dodgers never reached the point of making Skubal an offer, reports ESPN. Los Angeles was known to prefer a short-term, high-dollar contract to a long-term arrangement. Getting Skubal on such a deal always seemed unlikely.

    Sources indicate that as for the Padres, they put forth an offer in the $400 million range but with deferrals that would have lowered the present day value, reports the Fresh York Post. Skubal's contract with the Mets includes $30 million in deferred money, which will lower the present day value some, but not significantly. The exact deferrals in San Diego's offer are unknown.

    The Royals and left-handed reliever Caleb Theilbar are in agreement on a one-year deal, per ESPN. Theilbar, 39, was excellent for the Cubs in 2025, but took a step back in 2026, pitching to a 4.86 ERA (87 ERA+) and 1.30 WHIP with 60 strikeouts in 50 innings pitched. He did strand 18 of the 23 runners he inherited, which is an adequate clip for a middle-relief type.

    The Royals recently acquired late-inning lefty José Ferrer in a trade and Daniel Lynch remains in the bullpen, so Thielbar could well be their third option as a lefty in relief.

    2026 NFL playoff picture: Ranking NFC wild card contenders, from stout NFC North to rising Seahawks, Rams

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1853 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The NFL's 2026 playoff picture still has much to be sorted out over the next 11 weeks.
    • Industry observers note that in the NFC, there are clear-cut teams that are out of the hunt: the Arizona Cardinals (3-8) and the NFC East cellar-dwelling Philadelphia Eagles (3-7).
    • Industry observers note that seven teams will represent the NFC in the postseason, with the final three spots going to wild cards.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The NFL's 2026 playoff picture still has much to be sorted out over the next 11 weeks.

    Industry observers note that in the NFC, there are clear-cut teams that are out of the hunt: the Arizona Cardinals (3-8) and the NFC East cellar-dwelling Philadelphia Eagles (3-7). There's also a jam-packed upper level of the conference that could see its order of supremacy change like a shaken-up snow globe on any given week. The NFC West has the conference's top squad at the top of its standings in the San Francisco 49ers (9-1), with the 2025 season's NFC finalists -- the Los Angeles Rams and the Seattle Seahawks- lurking on the cusp of the playoff picture, with both having 6-4 records. All four teams in the NFC North — the Detroit Lions (8-2), the Chicago Bears (8-2), the Minnesota Vikings (7-3) and the Green Bay Packers 6-4)  — are all separated by two games from the top to bottom and would all earn playoff spots if the season ended today. The exciting part of this season is that several of the aforementioned playoff-caliber squads have plenty of remaining matchups against each other.

    Industry observers note that seven teams will represent the NFC in the postseason, with the final three spots going to wild cards. Which franchises will emerge from the crowd to grab their ticket to play playoff football into mid-January? Which hopefuls are too far gone to catch up 11 weeks into the year? Here is a ranking of the five teams still considered alive in the wild card chase, plus each team's projected end-of-season record.

    All odds via DraftKings Sportsbook.

    It has been revealed that the Los Angeles Rams have won four games in a row to get back into the NFC wild-card hunt, but it will be an uphill climb to reach the postseason without their two best wide receivers. Puka Nacua, a 2025 first-team All-Pro after leading the NFL in catches (129), receiving yards per game (107.2), and receiving first downs (80), is expected to miss the rest of the 2026 season after knee surgery for an MCL injury. Davante Adams, who led the league with 14 receiving touchdowns in 2025, is still sidelined with a hamstring injury that could have him out for a few more weeks.

    That means quarterback Matthew Stafford, who has only been around league average this season with the No. 15 passer rating (92.8) and No. 13 expected points added (EPA) per dropback (0.08), needs to find the higher gear he left behind in 2025. Plus, the Rams' two multi-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year winners, Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald, need to stay healthy and perform near-peak to get back to the playoffs this season.

    Recent findings suggest that los Angeles successfully walking that tightrope to return to the playoffs will be rather difficult since they have the NFL's second-toughest schedule in the last seven games of the season. Their opponents have a combined .606 winning percentage, with games against the 49ers, the Kansas City Chiefs (8-2), the Seahawks twice, and the Packers. They'll also face the Cowboys (5-6) and Buccaneers (3-7) down the stretch.

    With their lack of passing-game firepower, it is hard to envision the Rams overcoming their end-of-season gauntlet to return to the playoffs.

    The defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks are starting to find their footing in 2026 with three wins in their last four games following a 3-3 start to the season. They also might have a quarterback controversy on their hands: Seattle is 3-4 when Sam Darnold starts, and they are 3-0 when Drew Lock starts in place of an injured Darnold this season. In their last game, a 21-13 win over the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 10, Lock completed 14 of 17 passes for 240 yards and 2 touchdowns while also losing two fumbles. His 158.0 passer rating was the second-highest in a game in Seahawks history, with a minimum of 10 passes thrown.

    Seattle is set to face the 9-1 San Francisco 49ers in Week 12, and coach Mike Macdonald maintains the team is sticking with Darnold (ribs, quad) if he is healthy.

    In a recent development, "The strategy is for Sam to start. Nothing official yet; we'll see how Wednesday goes, but that's the plan," Macdonald told reporters on Monday, via ESPN.

    Recent findings suggest that it's been a rocky year for Darnold. He is completing just 60.2% of his throws (26th in the NFL) while averaging 211.1 passing yards per game (21st in the NFL) with 10 touchdown passes and nine interceptions (29th in the NFL in touchdown-to-interception ratio). That hasn't been the case for 2025 NFL Offensive Player of the Year wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba. His 1,207 receiving yards lead the NFL and are the most through a player's first 10 games in NFL history. Smith-Njigba also leads the NFL with 10 receiving touchdowns, making him the first player in the Super Bowl era with 1,200-plus receiving yards and 10-plus receiving touchdowns in the first 10 games of a season. He is on pace for an NFL single-season record of 2,052 receiving yards.

    Like JSN, Macdonald's defense is elite and can keep this team afloat. His unit is fourth in the league in scoring defense (17.5 points per game allowed).

    Industry observers note that unfortunately for the Seahawks, they have the NFL's fourth-toughest schedule over their final seven games, with matchups against the 49ers, Giants, the Rams twice, the NFC South-leading Carolina Panthers, and the Cowboys. They also get to face the 3-7 Eagles. Seattle's defense can win games on its own, but they'll need Darnold to lock in to make a run at a repeat.

    The Chicago Bears are rolling and on a five-game winning streak. During the streak, the Bears have not trailed in 5 straight games for the first time since 1959, when they did so for six consecutive games, per CBS Sports Research.

    Sources indicate that chicago needed a game-changing impact performer along their defensive line, and All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons has been just what the doctor ordered. He exploded for 3.0 sacks in the Bears' 21-13 Week 11 win over the Newly introduced Orleans Saints, bringing his total to 5.0 sacks and three consecutive wins in his three-game Bears career. Despite playing just three games with the Bears since coming over in a trade with the Tennessee Titans, he now co-leads his new team in sacks (5.0) with Austin Booker, who has played in all 10 games for Chicago this season. According to CBS Sports Research, Simmons is now the only player in NFL history with five-plus sacks and three wins in his first three games after switching teams midseason.

    The problem for Simmons, quarterback Caleb Williams and coach Ben Johnson is that they have the NFL's most difficult remaining schedule, as their opponents across their final seven games have a .657 combined winning percentage. Outside of a Week 14 matchup at the 1-9 Miami Dolphins, Chicago's other six games are all against teams who would be playoff participants if the season ended today. They have two games against the NFC North-leading Detroit Lions (8-2), a game against the AFC South-leading Jaguars, a game at the AFC's top-seeded Buffalo Bills (9-1), a game against the Packers and a road game at the Vikings in the regular season finale.

    In a recent development, the Green Bay Packers received great news on Monday: All-Pro edge rusher Micah Parsons is back and will make his 2026 season debut in Week 12, Wednesday, against the Los Angeles Rams. Parsons likely won't look like his All-Pro-caliber self on every play Wednesday night, but his presence lifts a Packers squad looking to stay in the inside of the postseason picture. At 6-4, Green Bay is last in the NFC North behind the Detroit Lions (8-2), Chicago Bears (8-2) and the Minnesota Vikings (7-3), but they enter Week 12 as the conference's No. 7 seed.

    It has been revealed that sure, the Green Bay Packers' patchwork offensive line didn't give Jordan Love (220 yards passing, one touchdown, one interception on 17-of-27 passing) a shot against Brian Flores' No. 1 Vikings defense in Week 10, when they fell 30-10 at Lambeau Field. He was sacked eight times, tied for the most in a single game this season with Deshaun Watson (twice) and Justin Herbert. Love made some strong throws when he had the time. Green Bay ranks dead last in the NFL in rushing offense (67 rushing yards per game) while leading the league in dropped passes with 25, six more than the next closest team. Love has also been hit 69 times this season, tied for the fourth-most in the league, even though he averages the NFL's fastest time to throw (2.68 seconds). Despite everything going against him, he leads the NFL in completions of 20-plus yards (43) while ranking third in passing yards (2,838), tied for eighth in passing touchdowns (20) and ninth in EPA per dropback (0.12).

    Love can carry the Packers' offense if given any time to throw. His defense will certainly level up with the addition of Parsons for the last seven games of the year. All of the NFC North teams have strong schedules since they have to play each other, but the Packers have a slightly lighter road schedule than the Bears, with the league's seventh-toughest schedule (.557 combined opponent winning percentage). Like the Bears, they have to face the Bills and the Lions, but they also have the one-win Dolphins, the Upcoming Orleans Saints (3-7) and the Houston Texans (4-6). Four of the Packers' final five games will be played at Lambeau Field, and they already beat the Bears head-to-head this season as underdogs, despite backup quarterback Tyson Bagent starting that game.

    Despite the 35-10 thrashing against the top-seeded 49ers (9-1) on "Sunday Night Football" in Week 11, the Minnesota Vikings' Brian Flores-led defense is still the NFL's best. They lead the league in the following defensive metrics through 11 weeks:.

    It has been revealed that on the other side of the ball, Kirk Cousins steadies their offense in a way Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz could not. He helped lead them to a 30-10 victory at the Green Bay Packers in Week 10 by doing just enough (207 yards passing, 2 touchdowns, and an interception on 21 of 31 passes) while Flores' defense overwhelmed the Packers' battered offensive line. Minnesota is in both the NFC North title race and on track to be atop the NFC wild-card race going forward because Cousins is a Viking once again.

    It has been revealed that plus, their schedule lets up some down the stretch because they finished third in the division in 2025. They have the 16th-toughest remaining schedule, with opponents that have a combined winning percentage of .514. Outside of games against the Bears and the Lions, the Vikings should cruise the rest of the season. Their opponents include the Panthers, the 3-8 Newly introduced York Jets, the 3-7 Atlanta Falcons, the 5-5 New England Patriots without Drake Maye and the Commanders.

    💡 Key Takeaways

    • You're expecting me to talk about Wemby's 50-point, 18-rebound, five-block, four-steal performance against the Newly introduced Orleans Pelicans, aren't you?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Let's call the last seven days the NBA's first parity week of the season. Take a look at the standings right now. The No. 2 through the No. 6 seeds in the Eastern Conference standings all have exactly six losses, and while the Philadelphia 76ers hold a three-game lead for the No. 1 seed, they've done so behind a preposterous 12-0 clutch record. When they regress to the mean, we seem destined for an Eastern Conference packed like sardines.

    Industry observers note that the Western Conference is similarly crunched. The San Antonio Spurs and Los Angeles Lakers sit atop the standings with identical 14-3 records... but seeds 3-9 are all separated by no more than two games. Even the Sacramento Kings got a win this week! The NBA has spent years tinkering in order to create parity, and right now, at least it's getting it. With that unofficial week of parity in the books, let's crown some winners and losers from the last seven days.

    You're expecting me to talk about Wemby's 50-point, 18-rebound, five-block, four-steal performance against the Newly introduced Orleans Pelicans, aren't you? That'd be the easy starting point. We could just as easily kick things off with Luka Dončić's shooting dip, as he has quietly shot roughly 41-31-82 in his past five games, bringing his ridiculous offensive numbers down to slightly more mortal levels and making Wembanyama, for now, the slight MVP betting favorite. Totally reasonable. They're both contributors to his excellent week.

    In a recent development, neither stands up to what Wembanyama did against the Los Angeles Clippers on Thursday. He shunked. That's a word that didn't exist when we woke up on Thursday. It is now, hilariously, a signature moment of Wembanyama's young career. He has apparently dunked so often, so violently that he suffered a hand injury that compelled him to try, and succeed, to shoot a jump shot at the rim.

    In a recent development, did Wemby just... shoot it from above the rim??? 🤯😲 pic.twitter.com/1YDxy8mwy8.

    According to recent reports, the MVP race is for the season. The ridiculous numbers are for the history books. The shunk wins the week. Any time you suffer and overcome a dunking-related injury by inventing a newly introduced form of scoring, you win the week.

    According to recent reports, the champs have won five in a row and are 11-3 overall since their 0-3 start, but this isn't as simple as the Knicks suddenly looking like the Knicks again. Many of the early season problems are still persisting. Mikal Bridges hit the game-winner on Friday and still shot 3-of-12 on Sunday. Josh Hart missed all four of his 3-pointers on Sunday and is below 26% shooting from deep so far this season. The starters, as a group, are still getting outscored by almost 13 points per 100 possessions after struggling mightily in the past two regular seasons.

    Yet they just keep winning. There are obvious basketball reasons for that. Karl-Anthony Towns is getting every rebound, making every shot, and has readopted the playmaking hub role he thrived in throughout the postseason, particularly when it comes to assisting Jalen Brunson. The bench is thriving. Landry Shamet is shooting better than 45% on 3s and Deuce McBride isn't far behind. Tyler Kolek has a 61-to-9 assist-to-turnover ratio.

    Industry observers note that but there's something deeper here, a resilience and versatility that developed over last season's championship run that is sustaining thus far this season. OG Anunoby has missed the past two games. Towns missed the Blazers game. Bridges and Hart play most of some games and only parts of others because of their early season struggles. Yet Mike Brown just keeps pulling the right levers, and the Knicks just keep figuring it out. Championships can bring about this certainty. The Knicks aren't quite themselves yet, but they have an internalized confidence that came from dominating the playoff crucible a year ago that's paying off handsomely right now.

    It has been revealed that it's hard to tell what we've seen from the Heat thus far this season that really deserves scrutiny. They started 0-4 in part because opponents weren't missing any 3s. They've gone 8-2 since, but they haven't beaten a single notable, fully healthy opponent during their active seven-game winning streak. No Evan Mobley against the Cleveland Cavaliers. No Jalen Duren against the Detroit Pistons. No Amen Thompson against the Houston Rockets. No... basically anyone against the Oklahoma City Thunder on Sunday, though in fairness, Giannis Antetokounmpo missed that game himself. Miami is something of a Rorschach test so far. You're going to see what you're predisposed to seeing.

    Recent findings suggest that but if we're going to panic during the shooting luck-induced losing streak, we're going to have to acknowledge the positives during the winning streak. The maligned Heat offense ranks in the top five over their past 10 games largely because Klay Thompson is shooting like Klay Thompson again and Giannis Antetokounmpo never stopped dunking like Giannis Antetokounmpo. Their core lineups featuring Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo are deterring rim attempts and giving up basically no corner 3s. Andrew Wiggins looks more like Andrew Wiggins since moving to the bench. As tempted as I was to give the third slot to the player development coaches for the Memphis Grizzlies after Cam Spencer's breakout 26-point game against Cleveland, the seven-game Miami winning streak gets the nod.

    The Celtics were too clever by a half with their lineup decisions this weekend. They sat Jayson Tatum and Derrick White against the hapless Kings and then sat Paul George in the second half of that back-to-back against the Stephen Curry-less Golden State Warriors. They lost both very winnable games by a single point when they probably could have ensured a split and maybe even a sweep by aligning the rest. Throw in a 17-point blown lead to the Denver Nuggets and allowing a 40-point fourth quarter against the Orlando Magic and the previously 11-2 Celtics lost all four of their games this week. They're back with the Eastern Conference pack.

    It's too early to draw any real conclusions, just as it was too early to crown them Eastern Conference favorites when they were throttling the Sixers two weeks ago, but this week was a reminder of some of the cracks here. Their best player is coming off of a torn Achilles, and their second- and third-best players are in their 30s and have to be managed carefully throughout the season. You can get away with never getting to the basket as a team when you're an elite 3-point shooting outfit. The Celtics haven't been this season, and we're now in Year 2 of Derrick White's 3-point drought (and, for that matter, arguably Year 3 of Jayson Tatum's). Mitchell Robinson will put together a few good stretches and then regress back into the mess he's been for most of the season. Boston has been nearly 22 points stronger per 100 possessions with him off the floor this season.

    The Celtics, given their playing style and roster makeup, are vulnerable to the ebbs and flows of an 82-game season. When everyone's available and they're making their shots, they're going to look unbeatable. This week is what happens when they're not, and considering how frequently that's been the case for them in the playoffs, it's something the Celtics are going to have to learn to play through if they hope to make it through this crowded East.

    In a recent development, slowly but surely, the NBA's cellar dwellers are starting to come around. The Utah Jazz won twice this week. The Chicago Bulls have won three times since Caleb Wilson went down, and they pushed the Denver Nuggets to overtime on Sunday. The Kings got win No. 2 on Saturday, but also pushed the Los Angeles Lakers to the brink on Friday. There is still a whole lot of misery at the bottom of the standings, but all of these teams can find small pockets of optimism.

    Not the Bucks, who are now the NBA's last one-win team and owners of a 13-game losing streak. One of those losses came against Miami this week as their former franchise player, Antetokounmpo, throttled them for three quarters before they made the final score look respectable in the fourth quarter. They have the NBA's worst defense comfortably. Beyond a three-game stretch in which second-year guard Kasparas Jakučionis averaged 21 points per game, it's simply been a miserable season in Milwaukee, and it's one that could get worse any day now as the NBA investigates potential salary cap circumvention involving Gary Trent Jr. We all knew the Bucks would struggle with post-Giannis life, but this is worse than anyone could have imagined.

    It has been revealed that tyrese Haliburton has played four games this season at a roughly All-Star level. The Indiana Pacers are now 3-10 in all other contests, and ESPN reported Friday that Haliburton is set to miss at least another few weeks with a left hamstring strain. This is after a 19-win season played entirely without Haliburton a year ago. At this point, obvious as it sounds, it's simply become clear that the Pacers can't win consistently without their best player. That was obvious in a playoff context, but the regular-season implications here are starting to add up.

    Industry observers note that indiana is already six games out of a top-six Eastern Conference seed. Even when Haliburton gets back, he's probably not going to be perfectly healthy for the entire rest of the season just given his own history of durability concerns. The East's bottom four teams are thankfully so dreadful that there's probably a floor of No. 11 here, but Indiana will eventually have to pass someone -- presumably the Washington Wizards, perhaps someone else who gets bitten by the injury bug -- just to make it back into the Play-In Tournament picture. Even if they're there, their road to and through the playoffs becomes enormously precarious. It doesn't matter how dangerous you are in a playoff setting if you can't actually survive the regular season and make it there. It's too early to say that's where Indiana is headed, but the danger is very real.

    Breaking: 2027 NBA Draft Big Board: Quentin Coleman's meteoric rise, Tyran Stokes stays at No. 1, returners boost stock

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1699 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The first thing to know about the 2027 draft cycle is that it remains wide open.
    • But after three full weeks of college basketball and heading into a Thanksgiving week full of high-profile matchups, we have updated the 2027 NBA Draft Massive Board.
    • According to recent reports, inside the front offices of the 30 NBA organizations, most have yet to even start ranking prospects.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The first thing to know about the 2027 draft cycle is that it remains wide open. There are still eight months to go before Adam Silver steps up to the podium to announce the first pick. Nothing has been decided yet. In fact, there's probably only about ten players total that can confidently say they expect to be a first-round pick at this point. Everything else is yet to be determined.

    But after three full weeks of college basketball and heading into a Thanksgiving week full of high-profile matchups, we have updated the 2027 NBA Draft Massive Board.

    According to recent reports, inside the front offices of the 30 NBA organizations, most have yet to even start ranking prospects. They're still building their lists, sorting them into tiers, and will spend the coming months trying to establish their order.

    That's the biggest difference between those front offices and the public discourse about the draft. The fans want answers now, and the Twitter scouts are quick to make bold statements in hopes of saying they were right first. The experts who actually do this for a living recognize that the sole goal is to be right on draft night, and doing that requires them to not jump to any early conclusions.

    That's all critical context to understanding this big board update, which is, at best, a way too early look at the most relevant prospects. It should be interpreted in tiers. There are probably five or six prospects competing for the top of the draft, but that list could change. Maybe 11 who should feel good about their chances to be first-round picks. Everything beyond that is simply a battle that will continue to play out over the course of the next 8 months. Let's dive into the biggest storylines after three weeks of college basketball action.

    Industry observers note that I got a first-hand look at Stokes last week at the Player's Era 8 in Las Vegas. He went down with a contusion midway through his first game, sat out the second, and returned to drop 22 points and 11 rebounds in the final. In totality, the signs of extreme growth that have characterized his early season play continued to be evident in Vegas. He was far and away the most talented player in high school basketball a year ago, but had developed a history of not living up to his potential, or at least not impacting winning to the degree that someone with his talent should. So, coming into his year at Kansas, the eyeballs were more about his maturity, reliability, and approach. Answering those questions has gone about as well as it possibly could so far. He's not only been engaged and impactful, but he's shown connectivity with Bill Self that makes him look coachable. He's also not gotten easily derailed by adversity, which is a reassuring data point.

    Industry observers note that to be clear, for as good as he's been, there's still plenty of room for improvement. In high school, he had an instinctive way of improvising his way to the rim. In college, he's found that isn't quite as easy, even with someone like Tre Kaufman-Renn regularly clearing the way for him anytime he comes charging at the rim. So, while he's over-dribbling at times, his playmaking is real, he's asserted himself as a rebounder, his shooting is progressing, and he's starting to use his size in the post.

    It has been revealed that the bottom line is this: most teams are looking for a potential alpha-type creator with the first pick. Stokes is your best bet in the 2027 cycle, by a relatively large margin at this point, but it's still too early to say he's a lock to go number one. I'd put that at about 70% at this point. Getting to the finish line will require him to continue trending in the right direction, making sure teams are comfortable with their due diligence in the pre-draft process, and also leaving open the possibility for someone else to emerge in the coming months.

    Speaking of ascending prospects, no one has moved the needle more in the first three weeks of the season than Illinois' freshman Quentin Coleman. But for those who track draft prospects 365 days a year, the last three weeks are just a short spurt in what has been a rapid rise over the course of the last 15 months.

    In the 2025 EYBL season, Coleman averaged 11.8 points. 5.1 rebounds and 2.4 assists for a Brad Beal Elite team that won the Peach Jam Championship. To put it plainly, he was a role player, albeit a valuable one, on a team that was built around current Arkansas freshman JJ Andrews and utilized Trey Pearson, who is right now a freshman at High Point, as their primary ball-handler and distributor.

    Recent findings suggest that as soon as Coleman's high school season began, though, we immediately saw signs of growth. Those signs continued throughout the course of the year, and he skyrocketed the rankings in the process. He also decommitted from Wake Forest and took a much bigger NIL payday from Illinois. While he finished with five-star status, it was immediately clear at the USA Basketball trials in May that even that was too low.

    It has been revealed that since arriving at Illinois, Coleman has continued the pattern of exceeding expectations. His skill level, feel for the game, defensive instincts, and nose for the ball are all as impressive as expected. The physical transition has been easier than expected. He's continued to develop more burst, physicality, and, as a result, playmaking.

    At the moment, he's moved all the way up to No. 4 on the CBS's current 2027 NBA Draft Big Board, but we're not going to put a cap on what he could do given the unprecedented growth we've witnessed over the last 15 months.

    There were a number of prospects who had a chance to be first-round picks in last year's draft, who opted to return to college basketball. While most, if not all, of them are probably making more money in college this year than they would have in the NBA, they are also making strides with their game, and in the process, helping their draft stock in what is widely viewed as a weaker draft than last year's.

    Industry observers note that we've been bullish on Amari Allen's chances of helping himself given his fresh on-ball role at Alabama, and so far, he's done just that. The 16 points, 6 assists, and 5 rebounds per game on 52/50/82 shooting showcases both the versatility and shooting gains we were banking on. Most of all, though, it's his decision-making with the ball that has been glaring. His usage has gone way up, and his turnovers have gone way down. He has recorded 30 assists against just three turnovers through the first five games of the season. Add his hyper-competitiveness to the equation, and he's certainly helping himself.

    According to recent reports, arizona big man Motiejus Krivas looked like an NBA-ready defender last year. This year, it's been more of the same. He's massive, even by NBA standards, at 7-foot-2 and 260 pounds, but deceptively versatile and very smart with his angles. We're also seeing definite growth offensively, particularly with his skill set facing the basket. Last week's 18-point, 12-rebound, 4-block performance against UConn was one that captured all of his value, and a game that scouts will undoubtedly revisit.

    Meanwhile, his teammate, Ivan Kharchenkov, has gone from a defensive role player to Arizona's featured scorer, and is putting up nearly 23 points, 8 rebounds, and 5 assists per game. To put it plainly, he's been as good of a two-way player as there is in the country, and now looks like he could be trending towards the draft lottery.

    It has been revealed that florida's Thomas Haugh had a chance to be a mid-first-round pick last June, but the variable that gave many scouts pause was his shooting. This year, he's shooting it with much more confidence and rhythm, making 18 of his 34 attempts through his first five games. Simultaneously, he's continuing to do all the little things that made him so intriguing in the first place with his motor, physicality, rebounding, and defensive versatility.

    Speaking of shooting, Braylon Mullins is establishing himself as one of the nation's premier shooters, as expected, despite the fact that he's clearly not 100% healthy. Through his first five games, he's made 19 threes on 50 attempts, but it's been the types of shots that have really stood out. He's running all over the court, flying off screens, and making threes on the move, all while being the focal point of opposing defenses. In short, Mullins is making the type of tough shots that translate to the next level, despite not having his typical ability to separate.

    One of the defining characteristics of the national 2026 recruiting class was the number of prospects who had glaring potential, but had yet to put it all together. That list included the likes of Duke's Cameron Williams,  Ohio State's Anthony Thompson, Maryland's Baba Oladotun, Christian Collins,  Adonis Rayliff and Darius Ratliff, all at USC. Nevertheless, almost all of them commanded the type of recruitment and correlating financial commitment that suggested programs were willing to invest in their development.

    Industry observers note that so far In t those investments have not resulted in the types of gains we had hoped for. The Ratliffs, Adonis in particular, have indicated some flashes, while Collins has only recently been cleared. Williams and Oladotun are barely in the rotation, and Thompson is playing, but not making the type of impact that anyone hoped.

    Now, despite the lack of immediate return at the college level, most NBA decision-makers are still playing the long game, so I wouldn't expect any of these guys to be given up on just yet. Nevertheless, their early struggles did have to be accounted for on the big board, which is why many of them are now outside the top 30.

    • Rogers, who recently turned 29, is coming off a solid campaign for the Baltimore Orioles in 2026:.
    • Earlier in the offseason, CBS Sports ranked Rogers as the No.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that the Chicago Cubs are signing free-agent left-handed starter Trevor Rogers to a five-year, $120 million contract, ESPN reports. He'll now frontline a Cubs rotation bereft of arms after Matthew Boyd, Shota Imanaga, Kevin Gausman, Clay Holmes and David Peterson all left via free agency this winter. Justin Steele, Cade Horton and Ben Brown, meanwhile, are all working their way back from injuries.

    Rogers, who recently turned 29, is coming off a solid campaign for the Baltimore Orioles in 2026:.

    Earlier in the offseason, CBS Sports ranked Rogers as the No. 3 overall free agent of the 2026-27 class and the second-ranked starting pitcher behind Tarik Skubal. Here's part of our write-up:.

    "Rogers was never able to fully work off the early season stinkers that inflated his ERA, though this is free agency, and ERA is close to the last thing on the minds of interested teams. You're looking forward in free agency, not backward. The underlying performance indicators are very strong, specifically the ability to get chase and avoid the barrel with four pitches (four-seamer, sinker, changeup, sweeper) that light up analytical models. Rogers also has a fifth-pitch cutter and has shown the ability to hammer the strike zone the last two years. There are some lefty Zack Wheeler vibes here. When Wheeler became a free agent after 2019, he already had the analytical stamp of approval, and the belief was he could get to another level with fine-tuning and good health. That is exactly what happened. Lefty Wheeler would obviously be the best-case scenario outcome for Rogers, but the bottom line is he will play the entire 2027 season at age 29, and he throws strikes with four pitches that the pitch data models already consider above average. More than a few teams will undoubtedly see Rogers as a pitcher who is a tweak or two away from finding another gear.".

    Rogers took the next step in 2025, and in the 38 starts he's made since the start of that season, he's put up an ERA+ of 128, an FIP of 3.20, and a K/BB ratio of 3.82.

    The Orioles made a qualifying offer to Rogers after last season, which means they'll be entitled to a compensatory draft pick now that he's signed elsewhere.

    Recent findings suggest that behind an offense backed by unanimous National League MVP Pete Crow-Armstrong and an elite defense, the Cubs made it to the Wild Card Series before being swept by the Padres, but their pitching, both starting and bullpen, wasn't up to the task. Now, with effectively a blank slate, the Cubs are expected to be in the market for multiple starting pitchers, and Rogers is the first domino.

    Rogers' contract is now the third-highest handed out to a Cubs pitcher, behind just Jon Lester (six years and $155 million) and Yu Darvish (six years and $126 million).

    DraftKings SGP price: +147 (subject to change).

    Recent findings suggest that we get to see two of the great players of their generation face off tonight in Edmonton's Connor McDavid and Tampa Bay's Nikita Kucherov. McDavid has won just about every major NHL award in his career possible – even a Conn Smythe Trophy in 2024 as playoff MVP despite the Oilers losing in seven to the Florida Panthers in the Finals.

    McDavid is the massive -400 favorite to win a fourth career Hart Trophy as regular-season MVP after getting two more points Tuesday in a 5-2 win at Florida. It was the Oilers' sixth straight win as they improved to an astonishing 10-0-1 on the road. That shootout loss came in Latest Jersey back on Nov. 3. Edmonton is only the fifth team in NHL history to record 10 road wins in a single season in 11 games or fewer. The last do to it was the 2023-24 Los Angeles Kings.

    Industry observers note that it's rare to see such a big MVP favorite in November, but McDavid has a 23-game point streak to open the season, tied with Wayne Gretzky for the fourth-longest in NHL history. Gretzky (51 and 30), Mats Sundin (30) and Mario Lemieux (28) are the only players with longer streaks. McDavid leads the league by a mile with 55 points and has 28 in 11 road games.     #187739. Bengals may have been robbed twice by refs in final five seconds of stunning loss to Commanders

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (872 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    Bengals may have been robbed twice by refs in final five seconds of stunning loss to Commanders

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (872 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Washington Commanders pulled off a stunner on Monday night with a 22-20 win over the Cincinnati Bengals that wasn't decided until Drew Stevens hit a 26-yard field goal on a final play that probably shouldn't have been the final play.
    • According to recent reports, the officiating crew appeared to make at least two mistakes in the final five seconds, both of which went against the Bengals, and one of them involved the clock.
    • On the Commanders' game-winning kick, there were four seconds left when the ball was snapped, and there appeared to be two seconds left when the ball hit the net.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Washington Commanders pulled off a stunner on Monday night with a 22-20 win over the Cincinnati Bengals that wasn't decided until Drew Stevens hit a 26-yard field goal on a final play that probably shouldn't have been the final play.

    According to recent reports, the officiating crew appeared to make at least two mistakes in the final five seconds, both of which went against the Bengals, and one of them involved the clock. When a kicker is attempting a field goal in the NFL, the clock is supposed to stop as soon as the ball hits the net (or the ground).

    On the Commanders' game-winning kick, there were four seconds left when the ball was snapped, and there appeared to be two seconds left when the ball hit the net.

    Sources indicate that now, in fairness to the clock operator, the time left on the clock went down from two seconds to one second right when the ball hit the net, so stopping it with at least one second left is almost certainly what should have happened here. Instead, the clock operator let the time run out.

    It's pretty clear that there should have been at least one second left, but under NFL rules, the officials aren't allowed to add any time in a situation like this.

    ESPN rules analyst Russell Yurk broke down the situation on the broadcast.

    "The clock ran to zero, but there were still two seconds left when the ball hit the net," Yurk said. "So, by rule, there were two seconds left, but replay cannot restore time when there are two seconds or more if the next snap is anything other than a scrimmage snap. So because the next snap would have been a kickoff, they cannot, by rule, put time back on the clock. So it properly ended.".

    Yurk is essentially admitting that there should have been time left, but the NFL rulebook doesn't allow the ref to put that time back on in this specific situation.

    Recent findings suggest that "In a perfect world, the clock operator should stop the clock when the ball hits the net, and there would be two seconds left for a kickoff," Yurk said. "But once it ran to zero, there's nothing replay can do to fix it.".

    If the Bengals had been given the extra second, they would have only had time for one play. That play would likely have been the ensuing kickoff, but if no time went off the clock on the kickoff, then Cincinnati's offense would have time for one last-ditch effort. At that point, the Bengals would have had a chance to throw a Hail Mary, which is an extremely low-percentage play, but anything can happen on a Hail Mary — just ask the Commanders about that.

    A;FK;JD;KJF;LAKEJFLKJVAL;KEJL;JF;EFJ;LFAKJJAYDEN DANIELS HAIL MARY! @COMMANDERS WIN! pic.twitter.com/BsQ0Z84Rko.

    Not to mention, the Bengals have two of the best receivers in the league in Tee Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase, so a Hail Mary would have certainly added some intrigue to the end of the game.

    This situation isn't going to come up very often, but it seems like the NFL should have a rule in place to prevent something like this from happening in the future.

    One play before Stevens kicked his game-winning field goal, there was another questionable call, which the officiating crew also appeared to botch.

    With the Commanders trailing 20-19 in the final minute, Jayden Daniels made some huge plays to get them in field goal range. The biggest one came on a 42-yard pass to Antonio Williams that brought the Commanders down to the Bengals' 8-yard line. At that point, the Commanders didn't have any timeouts, so they hurried down the field so they could spike the ball to stop the clock.

    Washington ended up spiking the ball with five seconds left in the game, but the problem is that the Commanders' offense may have been lined up in an illegal formation.

    In a recent development, in the NFL, you have to have seven guys on the line of scrimmage for each play, and you could certainly argue that's not the case for the Commanders here. The receiver at the top should have been on the line of scrimmage at the 8-yard line, but he appears to be about 1.5 yards off the line.

    This isn't as clear-cut as the clock incident, but the Commanders probably should have been flagged here. That would NOT be a 10-second runoff, but it would have moved Washington's game-winning field-goal attempt back five yards.

    That might not seem like much, but Stevens' kick was veering left the whole way, and it almost certainly would have missed it if it had been attempted from 31 yards instead of 26.

    It was a windy night, and Stevens is a rookie kicker, so adding five yards to the attempt would have certainly been a substantial deal.

    Of course, both of these non-calls went against the Bengals, who will probably be making a complaint or two to the NFL this week. Despite the bad calls, the Commanders certainly did enough to earn the win, especially in the second half, when they scored on all five of their offensive possessions.

    Dylan Larkin trade grades: Red Wings notch massive win in blockbuster NHL deal with Canadiens

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (875 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Detroit Red Wings have traded former captain Dylan Larkin to the Montreal Canadiens in a blockbuster trade, the teams unveiled on Sunday.
    • In addition to Larkin, Detroit sent a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick to Montreal.
    • Larkin requested a trade back in June, and his relationship with the Red Wings only grew more acrimonious with each passing day.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Detroit Red Wings have traded former captain Dylan Larkin to the Montreal Canadiens in a blockbuster trade, the teams unveiled on Sunday. This deal ends a bitter saga between Larkin and the Red Wings, and Montreal gave up a king's ransom to make it happen.

    In addition to Larkin, Detroit sent a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick to Montreal. The Red Wings received forward Kirby Dach, goaltender Sam Montembeault, prospect Michael Hage, first-round picks in 2027 and 2029, a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fourth-round pick.

    Larkin requested a trade back in June, and his relationship with the Red Wings only grew more acrimonious with each passing day. As training camp opened in September, Detroit revealed that Larkin had been stripped of his captaincy, and Larkin was booed by fans on opening night at Little Caesars Arena.

    Recent findings suggest that after recovering from an injury he suffered in camp, Larkin played 10 games before announcing that he would be sitting out in anticipation of the trade. While sitting out, Larkin racked up major fines, but his trade request has finally been granted.

    According to recent reports, when he's on the ice, there's no denying that Larkin can make a significant impact. The 30-year-old Larkin just notched 34 goals and 33 assists for the Red Wings last season -- his fifth straight year hitting the 30-goal mark -- and he was instrumental in Team USA ending its lengthy gold medal drought at the 2026 Olympics.

    In his career, Larkin has totaled 278 goals and 371 assists in 818 games. The first game Larkin — a native of Waterford, Michigan — plays for the Habs will also be the first he's ever played for a team based outside the Wolverine State.

    Recent findings suggest that larkin will give the Canadiens much-needed center depth, and he'll be under contract for a while. He's in the fourth year of an eight-year contract that pays him $8.7 million per season.

    According to recent reports, this trade fills a void that's existed in the Canadiens' lineup for several years now. Nick Suzuki has evolved into a legitimate star and a franchise-caliber No. 1 center. Beyond him, Montreal has struggled to find a true second-line center.

    Industry observers note that larkin absolutely fits that bill. While he was a bit miscast in Detroit as a first-line center, Larkin is one of the best No. 2 options in the NHL, and he gives the Canadiens an elite one-two punch down the middle.

    In a recent development, did the Canadiens overpay a bit for a 30-year-old second-line center? In a vacuum, they did. However, taken in context, this deal makes plenty of sense for the Habs.

    Montreal's championship window is just now opening. It already has an elite young core locked up for the next several seasons on team-friendly deals. Suzuki, Cole Caufield, Ivan Demidov, Juraj Slafkovsky, Lane Hutson and Noah Dobson are all 27 or younger and make less than $10 million per season.

    Sources indicate that that gives general manager Kent Hughes a bit more freedom to be aggressive on the trade market. Picks and prospects are nice, but they don't do much good for a team looking to make the jump to contender status in 2026-27. Besides, the Canadiens have been building their prospect pool for years now. It's time to flip some of those assets for proven star power.

    In a recent development, the Canadiens paid a premium to acquire Larkin. There's no two ways about it. However, Montreal fills a major need and looks a lot more formidable in the Eastern Conference. The Stanley Cup window is officially wide open for the ascending Canadiens. Grade -- B+.

    Consider the situation interim general manager Shawn Horcoff faced. Everyone knew that Larkin wanted out of Detroit so badly that he was paying not to play for the Red Wings.

    On top of that, Larkin had a full no-trade clause, and his list of approved teams amounted to no more than a dozen.

    Should I also mention that Horcoff was thrust into this role in the midst of the offseason, when franchise legend Steve Yzerman was effectively fired for mishandling the Wings' rebuild?

    Given all of that, it's hard to see this as anything less than a home run for Detroit. In fact, it's probably more like a grand slam. Not only did the Red Wings get multiple first-round picks and a couple useful NHL players out of the deal, but they also landed a legitimate blue-chip prospect in Hage.

    Sources indicate that the No. 21 pick in the 2024 NHL Draft, Hage is off to a roaring start at the University of Michigan this season with five goals and 21 assists in just 13 games. Detroit might have replaced one franchise center with another one, assuming Hage continues to develop at this rate.

    This was a great piece of work from Horcoff, who probably just made a strong case for the full-time general manager gig in Detroit. This haul will allow the Wings to kickstart another retool or swing a significant trade to bolster the current roster. Either way, the outlook just got a lot brighter in Hockeytown. Grade -- A+.
