    The Problem of Passivity – MX

    📅 25 Oct 2025 | ⏱️ 19 min read (3776 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Spielverlagerung

    ⏱️ ~19 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • von Next Generation am 25.10.2025 in den Kategorien Champions League mit 0 Kommentaren.
    • A solid start was masked by an overly passive 5-4-1 and ultimately ended in a 5-1 defeat for Dino Toppmöller and Eintracht Frankfurt.
    • It has been revealed that after three winless games, Eintracht Frankfurt faced Liverpool on Wednesday evening.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    von Next Generation am 25.10.2025 in den Kategorien Champions League mit 0 Kommentaren.

    A solid start was masked by an overly passive 5-4-1 and ultimately ended in a 5-1 defeat for Dino Toppmöller and Eintracht Frankfurt.

    It has been revealed that after three winless games, Eintracht Frankfurt faced Liverpool on Wednesday evening. Dino Toppmöller lined up in a 3-4-3 formation. Zetterer started in goal after extended discussions in the media. Amenda and Theate took up the half-back positions, while Koch operated as the central center-back. On the flanks, Kristensen and Brown were deployed. In midfield, Götze and Larsson formed the double-eight, with Doan and Bahoya on the wings and Knauff starting as the central striker.

    It has been revealed that the visitors from Liverpool arrived in Frankfurt with a similar situation: four consecutive defeats, including losses to underdogs like Crystal Palace and Istanbul. Arne Slot lined up in a 4-4-2 formation. Mamardashvili started in goal, with Konaté and van Dijk forming the central defense. On the flanks, Frimpong and Robertson defended, while Jones and Szoboszlai operated in central midfield as number eights. Gakpo and Wirtz occupied the wings, and up front, Isak and Ekitike formed the striking duo.

    In a recent development, after the game, Markus Krösche stated: “In the end, it’s about showing a completely different level of aggressiveness in the duels.” A topic that has been omnipresent around Frankfurt for weeks—and came into the spotlight again against Liverpool. But why did Frankfurt struggle so much to even engage in the duels?

    This is a translated analysis. You can find the original here: https://spielverlagerung.de/2025/10/24/die-sache-mit-der-passivitaet-mx/.

    Liverpool with Incompact Number Eights.

    According to recent reports, from the home side’s perspective, the game initially unfolded differently than the overall narrative suggested: it started off stable. In the first ten minutes, Dino Toppmöller’s side largely operated from a 3-4-3 structure in their higher build-up, with particular focus on the half-backs Theate and Amenda. Liverpool’s two forwards in the 4-4-2 mid-block struggled to gain access to the half-backs positioned in the half-spaces due to their narrow starting positions.

    This repeatedly created horizontal pressing angles—i.e., side approaches—which carried a high risk of being dribbled past. Theate, in particular, was able to exploit this thanks to his very vertical first touch. Consequently, Liverpool’s number eights, especially Szoboszlai on Theate’s side, were often forced to move from the center into the half-space to press the advancing half-back. This opened central spaces next to them, into which Frankfurt’s number eights could advance and increasingly become available as passing options.

    Hugo Larsson, in particular, was able to receive the ball from Theate multiple times, as the right number eight—Götze, or sometimes Doan and Knauff when positioned deeper—tied up Jones in Liverpool’s right half-space. This created, in the opening minutes, large pockets of space between Liverpool’s central number eights, allowing Larsson to push forward relatively freely.

    Frankfurt Finds Larsson in the Center.

    It has been revealed that this initially meant that Liverpool struggled to immediately disrupt Frankfurt’s build-up after the half-backs carried the ball forward. Often, the visitors responded by having Jones instinctively step out onto Larsson. However, due to the long pressing distance from the half-space into the center, he usually arrived late in the duel, allowing Larsson to hold onto the ball with his composure and often stabilize play via a relieving pass back to Theate. Jones stepping out also forced Gakpo, the far-side winger, to move into the half-space, reducing his ability to provide width for potential switches. Frankfurt, however, made too little direct use of these far-side spaces in the opening phase.

    Larsson’s Focus on Breaking Free.

    Recent findings suggest that despite dropping deeper, Larsson’s focus was also on another problematic area in Liverpool’s pressing: the space between the first and second lines. The narrow positioning of the two forwards is meant to isolate passing lanes from Frankfurt’s first build-up line into the defensive midfielder. In practice, though, their adjustment to players dropping behind them—beyond their tight starting positions—was limited.

    Larsson frequently found pockets in the blind spot between the two forwards and became available through central center-back Koch in the defensive midfield zone. Szoboszlai and Jones were often tied up in the half-spaces by the inward-running Bahoya or Kristensen, and the gaps between Liverpool’s first and second pressing lines were relatively wide, preventing them from intuitively stepping out onto Larsson.

    Against the forwards’ rearward pressing, the Swede was able to turn effectively and drive into the center with the ball. In some cases, this movement primarily served to draw Liverpool’s double-striker formation together, thereby giving the half-backs more space for diagonal dribbles—here, Larsson often simply laid the ball off. At other times, he actively sought progression and diagonal switches to advancing players in wide areas, most often targeting Brown on the left flank, which proved fairly effective in the opening phase.

    Recent findings suggest that however, Wirtz’s active rearward pressing limited space for Bahoya in the deep left half-space, meaning left-back Frimpong didn’t need to step out. As a result, Brown was frequently isolated on the wing, repeatedly facing 1v1 situations, which he struggled to handle consistently.

    Liverpool Reveals Spaces Both Wide and Centrally.

    Speaking of Bahoya: He frequently looked to make diagonal runs into the space behind Szoboszlai to get into the center and be vertically available for Larsson. However, Larsson struggled noticeably in these situations to find Bahoya in the right spaces. On one hand, this was because during his diagonal dribbles he focused heavily on the flank, sometimes neglecting scanning toward the center. On the other hand, this orientation also exacerbated Brown’s isolation on the left wing: with Bahoya positioned centrally, there were often few nearby support options, while Theate rarely pushed up consistently in these moments. As a result, Brown was frequently isolated in 1v1 situations without passing options.

    Too Fragmented or Well-Focused?

    As Brown became increasingly involved in Frankfurt’s play, a new dynamic emerged: Wirtz pressed closer and more directly onto Brown, which opened up the vertical passing lane from Theate in the half-space to Bahoya, who repeatedly offered dropping movements.

    At this point, one could discuss whether Liverpool’s pressing appeared too fragmented: on the one hand, the number eights were oriented too man-focused (see above), creating central spaces that were potentially exploitable. On the other hand, Wirtz’s wider positioning and Szoboszlai’s lack of compensatory movement meant these spaces were actively playable for Frankfurt. Or not?

    On the other hand, it must be noted: what appears fragmented can also be well-prepared or intentional. While Bahoya was technically available as a passing option, Liverpool reacted very effectively in these situations. Right-back Frimpong tracked his dropping movements directly and consistently, while Wirtz and Szoboszlai stepped up, creating situations in the half-space where Bahoya faced 1v2 or even 1v3 disadvantages, simultaneously closing potential lateral passing options. Considering that Bahoya is primarily a player who looks to provide vertical depth rather than withstand direct pressure, this approach made sense: Brown was pressed more directly, Theate was forced into the half-space, and Bahoya came under immediate pressure, often leaving him with only the option of a backward pass.

    Wirtz’s more direct stepping up also addressed an matter from the opening minutes. Frankfurt’s narrow starting positions had allowed Brown to remain available laterally to Theate, creating a very horizontal pressing angle. This enabled Brown to open up vertically and play deeper to Bahoya or carry the ball himself—something that ideally should have been prevented.

    According to recent reports, after Frankfurt’s relatively stable start—facilitated by higher initial possession that gradually decreased due to enforced verticality—Liverpool increasingly found their rhythm. This was mainly because Frankfurt allowed it. The Eagles set up in a 5-4-1 deep block, prioritizing blocking rather than actively pressing. This was particularly evident with striker Knauff: he lightly tracked Liverpool’s half-space dribbles but rarely contested the duels actively. Consequently, there was no isolation on lateral passes from the first pressing line, allowing Liverpool to shift play between the center-backs and repeatedly dribble forward. Frankfurt’s midfield was forced into constant lateral shifts, which repeatedly opened spaces within the 5-4-1 block.

    Liverpool thus created excellent conditions to exploit gaps inside Frankfurt’s 5-4-1 structure. Both number eights, Jones and Szoboszlai, occasionally broke forward ahead of Frankfurt’s second pressing line, acting as part of the first build-up line between center-backs and half-backs (or “wing backs”), creating temporary 5-0-5/3-2-5 spacing. The intent was twofold: first, technically strong players like Szoboszlai and Jones could dribble and exploit small diagonal spaces; second, the expansive build-up created direct backward passing options via central center-back van Dijk, enabling quicker lateral switches and further straining Frankfurt’s shifting.

    Recent findings suggest that the main aim, however, was to position as many players as possible around the block—both in front and behind—to force Frankfurt’s number eights to step out reactively onto Liverpool’s dribblers in the half-space, while simultaneously opening “blind-spot” spaces in front of the defensive line. Structurally, this was facilitated on the right by Konaté, who could push Szoboszlai wider from the half-right position. This, in turn, pulled Frankfurt’s left winger Bahoya slightly out of compactness (likely to prevent a 2v1 in width behind him), while Larsson was forced into more active blocking—slightly stepping up without actively contesting duels, creating minimal defensive shadow. As a result of these positional adjustments, spaces often emerged between Bahoya and Larsson, which Florian Wirtz sought diagonally.

    Liverpool Seeks Ways Around the Block.

    This created some interesting patterns in the lay-off play. Ekitiké occasionally moved into the number 10 zone, positioning himself horizontally to the right following Wirtz’s diagonal runs, allowing Wirtz to lay the ball off to him. Since Wirtz immediately stepped back into the “play & move” rhythm, these pressure situations occasionally opened opportunities for direct forward progression into deeper areas—even if they were not fully exploited in the opening phase.

    It also became apparent that a defensive focus on blocking inherently involves some degree of reactivity. Drops from the last line were not actively tracked but responded to reactively. The priority was securing depth first and defending only upon receiving passes. This approach gave Wirtz and Ekitiké additional freedom in the half-space—players of their quality can exploit such pockets effectively. This was particularly noticeable in the first-touch lay-off patterns.

    Because Liverpool could switch the ball with ease, it was increasingly played from one wing-back to another. Personnel shifts were very dynamic: Jones, Wirtz, or Szoboszlai occasionally operated wide as wing-backs, while Konaté and Robertson advanced into the half-spaces. Switches could be executed directly through the half-space movements of van Dijk. The core problem for Frankfurt lay in the 5-4-1 block: ball-far wingers and full-backs tended to drift too far into the half-space. After Liverpool’s switches, these players moved relatively uncontrollably back into width to track their direct opponents.

    At this point, the question arises as to why Frankfurt focused so heavily on blocking and, after deliberately allowing switches, responded in such a fragmented way by pushing out wide.

    It has been revealed that this repeatedly created pockets of space between full-back and half-back that Frankfurt’s 5-4-1 block was supposed to prevent, but Ekitiké consistently sought and exploited them between Theate and Brown. The glitch was compounded by the fact that, although Frankfurt tended to push out, the long pressing distance in width made it difficult to prevent Liverpool from seeking 1v1 situations. Brown was repeatedly placed under intense pressure in these duels, as diagonal pressing in a deep block is one of the most complex tasks: he needed to both close depth to block dribbles and runs from the half-space and defend the flank. Early on, however, Brown managed this reasonably well, and a subsequent ball win from him led to Frankfurt’s opening goal.

    Frankfurt’s wide players increasingly dropped back during Liverpool possession to support the full-backs in loose numerical superiority pressing. Yet, Doan on the right frequently failed to isolate the backward passing lane, often losing track of Jones and Robertson, allowing Gakpo to break free and enable another switch. On the left, the rotational setup was less dynamic, but Gakpo was slightly more proactive than Frimpong (later Bradley) in taking on Kristensen directly in 1v1s. Initially, however, there was insufficient depth support, leaving Gakpo relatively isolated. Kristensen’s effective blocking of crossing options further limited the Dutchman’s effectiveness in these situations.

    Higher wing-backs as the Key Point.

    After conceding, Liverpool pushed further forward, particularly in how their wing/full-back (depending on Szoboszlai’s temporary role in the back three) and number eights operated higher. Robertson and Jones increasingly formed a pair on the left side, while Gakpo moved more centrally in response to his earlier isolated position. Robertson pushed up as the left wing-back to free himself from Doan’s pressure and, together with Jones, create a 2v1 against Kristensen. This allowed Gakpo to repeatedly hint at depth in the half-space or actively position himself in the box—crucial since crosses had previously been only partially effective.

    Industry observers note that the width pair also allowed Doan to drop more frequently and shift from the half-space into wider positions, reopening spaces in the ball-side half-space. These were exploited primarily by Wirtz when diagonally dropping, forming a kind of dynamic trio with rotating coverage of width and half-space alongside Gakpo and Robertson. Typically, Wirtz, as the trigger for Phase 1 dynamics, dropped diagonally into the half-space and laid off to Robertson moving forward, while Jones pushed diagonally into the half-space center behind Wirtz, later being targeted by Robertson as the receiving player.

    In a recent development, the center. This splitting of the back five deliberately opened up deep half-space channels behind Frankfurt’s defensive line. At the same time, the Reds often sought to occupy the ball-far full-back and half-back, creating central spaces. Isak exploited these spaces with diagonal runs, using his pace advantage over Theate effectively.

    Recent findings suggest that when these spaces couldn’t be played directly, Liverpool remained in motion. One of Liverpool’s key strengths is maintaining this dynamic play through constant rotation of width. For example, Wirtz moved wide when the deep ball didn’t arrive, seeking 1v1 situations against Kristensen. The Frankfurt defender struggled against the German, who consistently cut inside. Through these inverted dribbles, Wirtz repeatedly found half-space areas—often connecting with Jones or Gakpo, who were probing the space in front of the defensive line. Frankfurt’s defenders continued to struggle with decisions between stepping out and securing depth.

    Recent findings suggest that it also became clear that the wing-backs increasingly made overlapping runs when the wingers had the ball. For full-back Kristensen, this meant he no longer consistently engaged directly with the winger, often leaving the duel to Doan to track the ball, while he dealt with the overlapping runner. Consequently, Frankfurt’s lateral dueling became more passive, giving the winger more space and time on the ball. Simultaneously, channels opened centrally in front of the defensive line because Kristensen was occupied by the overlapping full-back and Doan’s wide diagonal drop failed to fully isolate the passing lane to the center. This allowed Liverpool increasingly comfortable ball circulation on the wings with central connection options, opening opportunities for shots from the edge of the box—especially for the number eights, who could join centrally and occasionally shoot from distance.

    Sources indicate that this increasingly prominent Liverpool dynamic, combined with Frankfurt’s continued failure to isolate backward passes, forced Frankfurt in the middle of the first half to operate deeper in their 5-4-1 block, constantly defending in a low posture. The original initiative—to lure Liverpool out, provoke errors into the compact block, and then attack their rest defense on the counter—became progressively more difficult to execute.

    Recent findings suggest that this was largely because Frankfurt’s wide players, Bahoya and Doan, were increasingly drawn into defensive duties and had to drop deep, meaning they couldn’t provide the vertical width after winning the ball that they typically should as deep runners. At the same time, Liverpool tracked any vertical movements from Frankfurt’s wide players very effectively through their wing-backs; on the ball-far side (here Bradley), they aimed to anticipate the advance of the far-side winger and mark him with the far-side wing-back, making it difficult for him to break free.

    Additionally, Liverpool used their deeper number eight—usually Szoboszlai—and van Dijk to double up on the ball-near attacker Knauff in the half-space, preventing him from being played into effectively, which worked well: Knauff struggled to hold the ball for wall passes after turnovers. Konaté covered any spaces behind this double, particularly for second balls. However, the underlying problem remained that blocking implicitly assumes winning the ball within the defensive line when defending deep. After ball recoveries, Frankfurt could hardly progress from the back against Liverpool’s immediate numerical overload, which instantly triggered overloading counter-pressing and closed off vertical passing options to the number eights—the weak point in Liverpool’s rest defense system. As a result, Frankfurt’s defenders were often forced into long balls under pressure.

    Industry observers note that in other words, even after going 1-0 down, Frankfurt continued to lose possession. Because they operated deeper, these turnovers occurred in more advanced positions of Liverpool’s pressing, creating direct pressure and limiting structured buildup. The space that needed to be covered on counters was larger than in the mid-block early in the game.

    One could also discuss how a counter-attacking approach correlates with pressing and collective compactness. Frankfurt occasionally pressed individually and fragmentedly in response to certain cues (e.g., second dribbles in the half-space or wide distances), but lacked a clear, collective transition from the block into pressing. This allowed Liverpool to face minimal pressure in their first build-up line and develop their dynamic play, effectively freezing Frankfurt into passive blocking.

    It has been revealed that andrzejewski et al. (2022), in Analysis of team success based on match technical and running performance in a professional soccer league, analyzed over 600 Bundesliga games across two seasons and correlated various performance indicators with team success. One key point: more duels won correlated with more counterattacks. Similarly, Lepschy et al. (2021) found in analyses of the 2014 and 2018 World Cups that teams with higher duel success and effective counters were more successful. These findings suggest that both the quality and quantity of duels are linearly linked to successful counterattacking.

    It has been revealed that at the same time, Liverpool created relatively few chances from open play. They generated five major chances, with two goals from set-pieces and one counter leading to a 3-1 halftime lead. Their main struggles were in finishing crosses and chance creation around the box. A side effect of their play around Frankfurt’s block was that much creative personnel was positioned wide, limiting their effectiveness in tight spaces. Players like Wirtz and Jones rotated around the block with the wide players, sometimes causing problems in small-sided scenarios inside Frankfurt’s compactness. These options were therefore missing in key areas.

    Build-up should not be judged solely by whether it leads to goals but also by how it shifts game momentum. This increasingly shifted in Liverpool’s favor, largely due to their adjusted progressive play.

    After two corner goals just before halftime—each exploiting target players (van Dijk and Konaté) to find the “blind spot” created by horizontal movements of blockers like Ekitiké and Robertson—little else occurred in the first half. Liverpool continued to control the game against Frankfurt’s deep block, increasingly using direct diagonal switches to the far side to give their wide players more time 1v1 against Frankfurt’s ball-far full-backs or to create depth in the box.

    It has been revealed that these passes were occasionally imprecise, causing “ping-pong” situations in front of Frankfurt’s box around the central number eights. Liverpool faced minor counter-pressing problems but could usually manage them with collective back-pressing and tactical fouls.

    At halftime, Arne Slot brought on Chiesa for Isak, and Liverpool increasingly adopted a clear back-three setup in a 3-5-2 with slight adjustments. Wing-backs Robertson and Bradley operated deeper in their starting positions, intending to pull Frankfurt’s full-backs wider and open half-space channels for the inside wingers Wirtz and Gakpo. Diagonal breaking movements—acting as connectors between wing-back and number eight—remained visible, particularly Wirtz on the right. During ball possession, he would pull Konaté out, rapidly lay off to Bradley, and then exploit the space between Brown and Theate while moving in the “play & go” rhythm.

    According to recent reports, overall, Eintracht also struggled in the second half to consistently track or cover the drops from their last line in front of the second block. This repeatedly created 2v1 overload situations for Liverpool in width. Theate occasionally pushed out slightly but could not exert meaningful pressure on Wirtz. Instead, he often opened spaces in behind, which Chiesa repeatedly exploited to be played directly in behind—often from passes by Konaté.

    Direct diagonal balls to advancing wing-backs became more common, with these players benefiting from slightly deeper starting positions to gain a dynamic advantage over Frankfurt’s wide defenders (Brown in particular struggled against Bradley), allowing these balls to reach deep positions. The persistent concern, however, remained that Frankfurt struggled to get into the box.

    Frankfurt offered very little themselves. Apart from isolated actions following ball recoveries that couldn’t be converted directly into counterattacks, little developed. Even during brief periods of higher possession, the team remained vulnerable to Liverpool counters. This was primarily because Frankfurt’s number eights continued to operate high, leaving the space in front of the first-second line rest defense largely uncovered. Fast attackers—especially Ekitiké—and the dribble-capable Chiesa consistently exploited these half-space channels in Liverpool’s secondary attacks.

    The 4-1 goal came from a Liverpool turnover after Szoboszlai freed himself in the number eight zone with a dribble. Wirtz received the ball deep in the half-space between Brown and Theate. Gakpo drove forward from the space in front of Frankfurt’s number eights to the far post, exploiting the goalkeeper’s “blind spot,” and finished. (The goalkeeper’s blind spot is often an underestimated reference point for attackers.) The 5-1 was a long-range shot from Szoboszlai following a horizontal lay-off from the wide area into the half-space. Such lay-offs occurred frequently throughout the game but had rarely been finished consistently.

    Overall, it was an interesting game—predictable in some ways but also grinding at times. Frankfurt must significantly improve their defensive activity and pressing to get back on track in the coming weeks, particularly against top teams. Liverpool, on the other hand, secured important morale-boosting points. The team showed clear potential for improvement, but also remained prone to errors. Overall, it was a favorable game for Slot and Liverpool.

    MX made a name for himself in Regensburg with his tendency to overcomplicate the game. While flirting with the RB school, he remained a secret romantic at heart, drawn to Guardiola’s style of football.

    #187710. NBA Hater Report: Celtics can't shoot, neither can Trae Young and James Harden isn't close to a top 10 player

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 11m • 📚 Deep Dive (2155 w)

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    NBA Hater Report: Celtics can't shoot, neither can Trae Young and James Harden isn't close to a top 10 player

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2155 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Welcome back to the NBA Hater Report: A breakdown of some of the players, teams and trends around the league that are drawing the ire of yours truly.
    • Recent findings suggest that the Celtics are hitting their first skid of the season, having lost four straight to drop to 11-6, including a demoralizing back-to-back against the now two-win Kings and the sans-Stephen Curry Warriors.
    • Lack of rim pressure was always going to be, and has long been, an obstacle for the Celtics, who are averaging just 47 drives per game (third-fewest in the league).
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Welcome back to the NBA Hater Report: A breakdown of some of the players, teams and trends around the league that are drawing the ire of yours truly. If you're not a fellow pessimist, proceed with caution.

    Recent findings suggest that the Celtics are hitting their first skid of the season, having lost four straight to drop to 11-6, including a demoralizing back-to-back against the now two-win Kings and the sans-Stephen Curry Warriors. They failed to hit 100 points against the Kings and their 28th-ranked defense. They managed just 87 at Golden State.

    Lack of rim pressure was always going to be, and has long been, an obstacle for the Celtics, who are averaging just 47 drives per game (third-fewest in the league). Only 25.6% of their shots are at the rim, the fourth-fewest in the league per Cleaning the Glass, and no team takes fewer shots per game from inside the restricted area.

    According to recent reports, they are about as extreme a jump-shooting team as you will find, and right now the shots are not going in. Over these last four, the Celtics have made just 28% of their 3s and 38% of their overall shots. Throw in 65% from the free-throw line and those are all bottom-two marks over that span, plus the 389 points they scored is the lowest over any four-game stretch since 2012 for a Boston offense.

    According to recent reports, it's not just the number of 3s the Celtics rely, sometimes more than others, it's the kinds of 3s. Every team wants the shots off ball and player movement, drives and kicks, drawing two and swinging, but when the Celtics aren't able to create the initial leverage by attacking the rim (they don't have to do this with just drives; they aim to do so by cutting and rolling, too), they end up taking more pull-up 3s than any team in the league, both as a total number and percentage of their overall shot diet.

    In a recent development, those are traditionally tougher shots, and indeed Boston is making them at a 33.5% clip. The Celtics also don't generate a ton of the coveted corner 3s (which are often a result of rim pressure) relative to their volume, and thus take more above-the-break 3s than any team. There are also a lot of one-on-one 3s; only the Lakers and Timberwolves take more 3s after three or more dribbles, and the Celtics make those at only 29%.

    Recent findings suggest that bottom line, Derrick White is shooting 28% from 3 for the year and has missed 22 of his last 25 from deep (he had so many premium looks against Golden State and they just will not go in for him). Payton Pritchard has missed 21 of his last 29 from deep. Jayson Tatum is having a stellar all-around season and is leveraging his scoring attention to find teammates more effectively than ever, but quietly his shooting is in the dumps, too.

    Industry observers note that tatum is shooting 42.6% overall and 33.6% from 3, both of which would be career lows if you discard the 15 games he played last season after returning ahead of schedule from the Achilles tear. Tatum has never been a particularly adept pull-up 3-point shooter, for which he'll probably always be prone to settling to at least some degree. Tatum's pull-up 3s over his last four full seasons:.

    In a recent development, any team that debuts as many 3s as the Celtics is going to endure some extreme ebbs and flows, and coach Joe Mazzulla remains committed to the course. "... If we're getting good shots, which more times than not we are, you have to be able to trust over the course of a season that that's going to work out," he mentioned.

    The truth is, the Celtics don't really have a choice other than to trust the shots to go in. They don't have a plan B to speak of. They don't get to the rim and they don't have a post presence. They have a gang of good shooters, but that doesn't guarantee good shooting.

    The Celtics rely on getting more shots than their opponents by winning the turnover and offensive-rebounding battles, which they generally do, but as Mazzulla also noted, "at some point you have to knock [the shots] down. That's just not happening right now.".

    After Harden scored 51 against the Pacers last Friday, Cleveland coach Kenny Atkinson did the increasingly cliché "we've got to appreciate this guy" dance while calling Harden a "top 10 of all-time" player.

    Kenny Atkinson after James Harden's 51-point game: "We've got to appreciate this guy. This guy is top 10 of all-time." pic.twitter.com/YUt2Y6pQYL.

    Remember, Atkinson is the guy who told reporters: "Analytically … we've won two out of three" right before the Cavaliers got swept by the Knicks in last year's Eastern Conference Finals. That was kind of overblown, to be fair. He was simply citing the types of shots the Cavs got vs. the ones the Knicks got, and that getting the right shots is a recipe for success more often than not, which every coach from the beginning of time has believed.

    Atkinson just would've been better off if he'd gone the "make or miss league" route. Once you start invoking analytical results over actual results, you're going to get rightfully roasted as the number nerd that you are.

    Through this lens, it makes sense that Atkinson thinks Harden is a top 10 all-time player. Numbers-wise, he's ninth all-time with almost 30,000 career points. He's 11th in assists and, barring injury, will almost surely pass Isiah Thomas for 10th by the end of the season. Only Stephen Curry has made more 3-pointers than Harden, who's piled up so many numbers he's actually top 20 all-time in steals.

    None of this adds up to top 10.

    Industry observers note that of course this is subjective, but this is my Hater Report, so allow me to hate. Harden was a manipulating machine of egregious proportions. I'm not saying he wasn't a great scorer, or even that he sometimes still isn't. Two things can indeed be true. But if we're going to start throwing around top 10, we're sure as hell going to factor heavily the conditions under which you dominated.

    Recent findings suggest that harden played in the NBA's version of the steroid era. It was juiced up on some level for every scorer, but nobody mastered the dark arts like Harden, who cheated his way to so many phony fouls that guys were literally starting to guard him with their hands behind their backs.

    According to recent reports, now listen, before you start with the "he wasn't breaking any rules" nonsense, keep in mind that steroids weren't technically illegal in baseball when Barry Bonds' head looked like it was going to pop. Harden scammed his way to more points than anyone in history. The flops and flails were impossible to stomach or, more importantly, defend against. Falling down on damn near every 3-pointer he took actually became part of his follow-through. I would only be mildly surprised if you hid a camera in his private workouts if he wasn't falling down in an empty gym, because he was so used to doing it.

    Recent findings suggest that this created more than just a gazillion free throws; it created a scoring environment in which Harden could operate against defenders who were way more frightened of fouling than being scored on. It was as if he was being perpetually defended by guys with five fouls.

    Industry observers note that now account for the one-man-show usage. I remember Raja Bell once telling me there are way more players than you think who could score 25 points per game if given the opportunity. Hell, Darius Acuff Jr. is doing it right now and until a week ago, he was a teenager.

    Industry observers note that that's not to say anyone could do what Harden did, but given his set of circumstances, it's irresponsible to call him one of the 10 greatest players ever on numbers alone. Back in 2022, ESPN ranked him 50th all time, which feels much closer to reality, and he's only gotten worse since then.

    Sources indicate that I mean, just start rattling names off the top of your head. Michael Jordan, LeBron James, Stephen Curry, Kevin Durant, Wilt Chamberlain, Larry Bird, Magic Johnson, Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, Hakeem Olajuwon, Kobe Bryant, Tim Duncan, Shaquille O'Neal. We're already at 12 and there's not even a debate with any of them.

    No coach in his right mind would take Harden over Nikola Jokić, Giannis Antetokounmpo, Kevin Garnett, Karl Malone, Scottie Pippen, Charles Barkley, Isiah Thomas, Dwyane Wade or prime Chris Paul. I never watched Oscar Robertson, Jerry West, Julius Erving, Moses Malone, Elgin Baylor or some guy named Bill Russell, but something tells me the vast majority of coaches are taking those guys over Harden, too.

    It bears repeating that none of this means to suggest Harden hasn't been an all-time player. He's a first-ballot Hall of Famer. He's not an empty-stats guy by any stretch; he led a team that very possibly would've won the championship in the middle of Golden State's dynasty were it not for a Chris Paul injury. But there are levels to this, and trying to elevate Harden into the top one on the strength of gaudy numbers in an absolutely juiced-up era of his game would be like trying to call Sammy Sosa one of the greatest hitters ever. It's just not even close to true.

    In a recent development, back in 2021, I called Young an average shooter who thinks he's Stephen Curry and got absolutely roasted for it. Turns out, I wasn't harsh enough on Young, whose shooting has been consistently deteriorating to the point that he is now a flat-out bad shooter. Even with a 7-for-15 run from 3 over his last two games, which at this point is a downright nuclear stretch for him, Young is shooting 32.5% from 3 and a pitiful 36.4% overall.

    Industry observers note that the fact that he's among the league leaders in assists means almost nothing; passing has always been his one elite gift (it goes largely hand in hand with his former ability to breach the paint at will), but it comes at the hefty cost of him controlling the ball for almost the same amount of time per possession as Luka Dončić this season. Just because those two were traded for one another doesn't mean they are, or ever have been, anywhere near the same caliber of player.

    Even at his peak when he was one of the league's better shot generators, it was debatable whether you could justify sponsoring Young's personal dribbling show with your offense, let alone paying him max money given the defensive trade-off. But now that he can't shoot or beat anyone off the dribble, that $212 million deal the Wizards gifted him this summer, which was a disaster the moment the ink dried, somehow looks even worse.

    Washington is trying to salvage some sort of value from Young. They're starting to take him off the ball some, which, given the good shooting the last few games, is going to give the apologists hope. Don't fall for it. The numbers, not just this year but going back a long time, speak for themselves.

    Sources indicate that there's a difference between a talented shooter and a good one. Young fooled people with range and confidence for a while, and he had an unearned marksman reputation that died hard. But the jig is up. This is an average shooter at best, and he's rarely at his best.

    After losing four straight games by 20-plus while also being held under 100 points in each (an equation of futility that goes unmatched by any other team this century), the Warriors finally got their first win since losing Curry to an oblique tear by beating the aforementioned ice-cold Celtics.

    It certainly wasn't because of their offense. The Warriors were once again held to double digits, managing just 88 points. Over this five-game stretch, the Warriors, who register a top-five offense with Curry, have scraped together an anemic 96.2 points per 100 possessions on 48.5% true-shooting, both being the worst marks in the league by a laughable margin.

    It has been revealed that over this five-game stretch, the Warriors have been outscored by 108 points. The 1997-98 team that also lost four straight by at least 20 points was a minus-104 over that stretch. That was the season that Latrell Sprewell choked P.J. Carlesimo, mind you. The Warriors won 19 games. That's the kind of manufacturer these Warriors are trolling in right now.

    If Curry doesn't get back soon, we might have to start worrying about Draymond Green putting Steve Kerr in a full nelson.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that veteran right-handed starter Freddy Peralta has signed with the Baltimore Orioles on a five-year deal, the team announced on Tuesday. The contract is worth $125 million with no deferrals or options, The Athletic reports.

    Recent findings suggest that peralta, who will be going into his age-31 season in 2027, is coming off a campaign in which he didn't pitch up to his usual standards during a disastrous stint with the Newly introduced York Mets. However, he did more like his old self following a deadline trade to the Tampa Bay Rays. On the Rays' watch, Peralta made a series of adjustments that helped him find better results on the mound, including being named the ALCS MVP.

    In a recent development, earlier this offseason, CBS Sports ranked Peralta as the No. 7 free agent of the 2026-27 class. Here's part of our write-up:.

    "It has been a roller coaster year for Peralta, who flopped with the Mets, rebounded with the Rays, then faced the Brewers (his former team) in the World Series and lost. The post-deadline stint with Tampa salvaged Peralta's free agent year. They made several adjustments, most notably raising his arm angle and getting him to pitch exclusively from the stretch, and the result was a livelier fastball and also better command. He's still five-and-fly Freddy. Even the best version of Peralta won't pitch deep into games and can be a tough watch because he nibbles and throws so many pitches per inning. They tend to be good innings, though, and the guy never misses a start. Worst case, Peralta is a mid-rotation starter you can count on to take the ball every fifth day. The best case is someone who can front a contender's rotation. Fastball Freddy was always going to be a great bounceback candidate this offseason. The Rays just beat everyone to it at the trade deadline.".

    Peralta isn't far removed from a 2023-25 stretch for the Milwaukee Brewers that saw him top 30 starts and 200 strikeouts in three straight seasons. In 2025, he earned his second All-Star selection and finished fifth in the National League Cy Young vote.

    Industry observers note that "Freddy has proven to be a winning player who understands what it takes to compete and succeed on the biggest stage," noted Orioles president of baseball operations Mike Elias said in a statement. "His professionalism, preparation, and commitment to winning will set a strong example for our organization and we believe he will have a significant impact on our team both on and off the field.".

    According to recent reports, after losing Trevor Rogers to free agency (he agreed to a five-year contract with the Chicago Cubs earlier on Tuesday), the Orioles were searching for a fresh frontline starter to join a rotation that includes Kyle Bradish, Shane Baz and some combination of Brandon Young, Cade Povich and Trey Gibson. Elias has been hesitant to pay up for pitchers recently, but either his strategy has changed or he decided Peralta was worth the cost.

    It has been revealed that the Orioles' disappointing fourth-place AL East finish in 2026 has raised questions about the state of Baltimore's rebuild, particularly amid stalled growth from its promising young position players, including Jackson Holliday, Gunnar Henderson and Colton Cowser. Would-be franchise backstop Adley Rutschman was traded to the Boston Red Sox at the trade deadline.

    Because Peralta was traded during the 2026 season and was thus ineligible for the qualifying offer, the Orioles will not be penalized a draft pick for signing him.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that the Denver Broncos will play their Week 12 game against the Pittsburgh Steelers without running back J.K.
    • Although Dobbins leads the team in carries (99) and rushing yards (324), with three touchdowns on his ledger this season, he slipped in the pecking order in recent weeks behind RJ Harvey and rookie Jonah Coleman.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that the Denver Broncos will play their Week 12 game against the Pittsburgh Steelers without running back J.K. Dobbins. Coach Sean Payton unveiled that he suspended the veteran ball carrier for one game for conduct detrimental to the team, which takes him out of the offensive rotation for the Black Friday contest. Payton did not comment further on the suspension or what prompted his decision, adding that "it's better that way" to not speak on the matter.

    Although Dobbins leads the team in carries (99) and rushing yards (324), with three touchdowns on his ledger this season, he slipped in the pecking order in recent weeks behind RJ Harvey and rookie Jonah Coleman. Dobbins' role reached a new low in last week's win over the Las Vegas Raiders when he played just one snap.

    Coleman emerged as the primary option in the backfield and took firm command of the starting job when he set career highs with 28 touches, 129 scrimmage yards and three touchdowns in that victory against the Raiders.

    Harvey is on injured reserve due to a knee glitch that popped up in practice in late October. He will not play on Friday and is not eligible to return until Week 13 against the Miami Dolphins.

    With two of the top three running backs out for the matchup with the Steelers, Coleman projects to take on a sizable workload for the second time in as many weeks. Payton declined to answer questions about the group but insisted that the Broncos will have depth at the position. If anyone steps into a more meaningful role, it would likely be Cody Schrader, whom the Broncos activated to their 53-man roster for each of the last three games. Tyler Badie's practice window is open, but the Broncos have not activated him from injured reserve.

    Industry News: MLB rumors: Corey Seager willing to waive his NTC for Phillies, plus news on Mets, Nationals, Yankees, more

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1058 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that the uncertain 2026-27 Major League Baseball offseason is fully underway.
    • According to recent reports, thanks to that prospect of a hastened pace, offseason rumors are flowing.
    • Sources indicate that the Yankees are among the many teams with interest in top free agent reliever Adrian Morejon, reports the Upcoming York Post.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that the uncertain 2026-27 Major League Baseball offseason is fully underway. The ongoing CBA negotiations and the near certainty of an owner-implemented lockout on Dec. 2 loom over all, and it may indeed mean a flurry of trades and free agent signings leading up to that date. That was certainly the case leading up to the last lockout of 2021-22, and this time around we've already seen some leading examples. Just recently, for instance, the New York Mets landed the biggest fish in the pond by signing ace Tarik Skubal to a record contract. Not long after, the Chicago Cubs fortified their rotation with Trevor Rogers and their outfield with Teruaki Sato, and Freddy Peralta is headed to the Baltimore Orioles. More's surely to come before lockout day arrives.

    According to recent reports, thanks to that prospect of a hastened pace, offseason rumors are flowing. Speaking of which, we'll be here each day to round up what's out there. You can find Tuesday's supply just below.

    Sources indicate that the Yankees are among the many teams with interest in top free agent reliever Adrian Morejon, reports the Upcoming York Post. Some teams view him as a potential starter, though there were reports earlier this month that he prefers to stay in the bullpen. The Phillies, meanwhile, are not considered a serious candidate to sign Morejon, according to The Athletic. We ranked him as the second-best free agent available this offseason, in part due to his potential to start.

    In a recent development, adding to the bullpen has been the Yankees' primary focus so far this offseason. Closer David Bednar accepted the qualifying offer, they re-signed lefty matchup guy Tim Hill, and signed Jonathan Loáisiga and Tim Hill as free agents. At some point they will need to add to their lineup, particularly at third base, but there's always room for a reliever like Morejon in the bullpen.

    Industry observers note that the Philadelphia Phillies are open to moving Trea Turner off of shortstop given that he's now a pronounced defensive liability. Speaking of openness, veteran shortstop Corey Seager of the Texas Rangers is willing to waive his no-trade clause to join the Phillies and upgrade the position for them, NBC Sports Philadelphia reports.

    Now 32, Seager will always have health and durability concerns, but he remains a plus defensive shortstop who produces well at the plate by positional standards. Signed to a 10-year, $325 million deal prior to the 2022 season (just before the last lockout, in fact), Seager is owed another $155 million through the 2031 season. The Rangers are reportedly looking to shake things up. The Phillies, meantime, are trying to keep their contention window open. It's a fit both ways, at least in theory. Such a move would likely mean a move to the outfield for Turner, who himself has very little trade value thanks to his ongoing decline and massive contract.

    Recent findings suggest that even in a down 2026 year, Jazz Chisholm Jr. put up 19 homers and stole 41 bases while manning an up-the-middle position. Still just 28 years of age, he figures to have a healthy market this offseason. Speaking of which, the Washington Nationals are one of multiple teams presently in contact with Chisholm, FanSided reports.

    Industry observers note that earlier in the offseason, CBS Sports ranked Chisholm as the No. 6 free agent in the current class. Here's part of that write-up:.

    "In what was his worst season as a hitter since his rookie year in 2021, Chisholm was still a league-average bat in 2026, and his top-shelf defense and baserunning still landed him at 3.5 WAR. Chisholm is a style-over-substance player who is not for everyone, but his second base defense and near-MLB-best baserunning skills give him a very high floor. He's a reasonable bet for 20-ish home runs with the potential to go 30-30, and Chisholm has improved his plate discipline enough to run walk rates north of 10% the last two years. The downside is his propensity to swing and miss. Chisholm has posted below-average in-zone contact rates throughout his career and contact rates that low always come with risk. That risk is mitigated somewhat by the secondary skills (defense, etc.) and the fact that Chisholm will play the entire 2027 season at age 29. You probably don't want him as your best or second-best player, but he's also an overqualified No. 6-7 hitter who brings so much else to the table.".

    The Cleveland Guardians have agreed to a free-agent contract with left-hander Kris Bubic, Sportsnet reports. The contract is for $17.5 million over one year, according to ESPN. Bubic, 29, made nine starts for the Kansas City Royals last season, and after the trade to the Los Angeles Dodgers, he was used out of the bullpen. Bubic has an outlier fastball thanks to its rise and his unusual release point, and he's an interesting "ceiling" candidate in the rotation. However, his substantial history of injuries may mean he's best used out of the bullpen.

    In a recent development, the Detroit Tigers have added infield depth by agreeing to terms with Ha-Seong Kim on a one-year, $5 million free agent contract, ESPN reports. Kim, 31, is coming off a rough partial season with the Atlanta Braves, but he has a more palatable OPS+ of 91 for his career. He's been a primary shortstop in recent years and also has significant time spent at second base and third base.

    Even after achieving a reunion with veteran starting pitcher Sonny Gray, the Minnesota Twins are still looking to fortify their roster for a return to contention in 2027. The club still hopes to make one more significant addition this offseason and add another player who may not grab as many headlines, the Athletic reports. Atop the wishlist are a first baseman or a second baseman and another lefty reliever.

    In a recent development, even after the splash addition of Skubal, the Mets may not be done adding starting pitchers in the service of a rebound season in 2027. On that front, the Mets may be interested in adding a starting pitcher on a short-term deal for next season, the Athletic reports. That would likely limit them to the back half of the market, especially with so many bigger names reaching agreements.

    Rashford returns and Fernandes misses another penalty as Man Utd humbled by Amorim

    📅 15 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 14 min read (2842 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~14 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Bruno Fernandes missed a penalty for the second successive pre-season friendly as Manchester United were beaten 4-2 by former head coach Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan.
    • Fernandes, who rolled a spot-kick wide in a shoot-out against Leeds in midweek, was gifted the chance to open his pre-season account in Wroclaw, Poland.
    • His effort was on target this time, but Milan keeper Lorenzo Torriani dived to his right to beat the shot away.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Bruno Fernandes missed a penalty for the second successive pre-season friendly as Manchester United were beaten 4-2 by former head coach Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan.

    Fernandes, who rolled a spot-kick wide in a shoot-out against Leeds in midweek, was gifted the chance to open his pre-season account in Wroclaw, Poland.

    His effort was on target this time, but Milan keeper Lorenzo Torriani dived to his right to beat the shot away.

    Fernandes did at least get an assist, taking the second-minute corner which was powerfully headed home by Harry Maguire to give United the lead.

    Amorim’s Milan equalised after a defensive mix-up allowed Gonçalo Ramos to break into the area and square for Samuel Chukwueze to roll home.

    United were awarded their penalty just before half-time after Koni De Winter tugged back Youri Tielemans, but Torriani guessed correctly to leave Fernandes frustrated.

    United retook the lead after Patrick Dorgu pounced on a loose backpass from Filippo Terracciano, but Milan equalised again when Chukwueze’s wayward shot was poked in by Alphadjo Cissè at the far post.

    Marcus Rashford, who was frozen out by Amorim and loaned out to Aston Villa and then Barcelona, came on as a substitute on the hour for his first United appearance since returning from Spain.

    But Milan went ahead in the 68th minute when Chukwueze’s cross was headed home by Ramos, and three minutes later former Chelsea midfielder Ruben Loftus-Cheek raced through to hit the fourth and cap a performance that underlines United’s need for reinforcements before their season starts in earnest next Saturday, away at Hull City.

    According to recent reports, manchester United (4-2-3-1) Lammens; Mazraoui (Dalot 61), Maguire, Heaven (Martinez 61), Shaw; Tielemans, Santos (Mainoo 61); Diallo (Lacey 61), Fernandes, Dorgu (Rashford 61); Cunha (Mbeumo 61). Subs Zirkzee, Yoro, J Fletcher, T Fletcher, Amass, Collyer, Mee (g), Heath (g), Gabriel. Booked Dorgu.

    AC Milan (3-4-2-1) Torriani; Terracciano (Gila 60), Winter (Vladimirov 84), Pavlovic (Diawara 84); Chukwueze, Musah (Ricci 76), Jashari (Modric 60), Estupinan (Bartesaghi 61); Loftus-Cheek (Comotto 84), Cisse (Saelemaekers 60); Ramos (Camarda 75). Subs Pittarella (g), Bouyer (g). Booked Estupinan.

    Goals Chukwueze (37), Cisse (57), Ramos (68), Loftus-Cheek (71).

    That six-time Champions League winner Luka Modric raised the trophy with the one hand mentioned everything you need to know about this moment...

    Aug 22: Hull City vs Manchester United.

    Aug 30: Manchester United vs Ipswich Town.

    Sep 6: Everton vs Manchester United.

    Sep 13: Manchester United vs Manchester City.

    Sep 20: Fulham vs Manchester United.

    United’s pre-season ends in defeat. A wretched second half proves their undoing as Amorim’s Milan score four. Worth reminding that United led this match, twice.

    Milan are playing keep-ball in these latter stages and although Mainoo regains possession, his attempt to play forward is cut out and Modric’s outside-of-the-foot pass finds Comotto, who heads straight at Lammens.

    Four minutes of added time to be played...

    United now raining crosses down on Milan’s box but Torriani equal to it every time.

    For the second time this afternoon, Shaw directs a lovely ball into Fernandes’ path in behind Milan’s back line, but the Portugal international can’t bring it under his spell.

    In a recent development, martinez has added a little bit of urgency to United’s build-up. Mbeumo tries to feed Shaw down the line but the ball is cut out.

    In a recent development, more substitutions... Diawara, Vladimirov and Comotto enter the field of play in place of Pavlovic, De Winter and Loftus-Cheek.

    Substantial chance for Rashford! Martinez lofts a fantastic ball over the top but Rashford is not quite able to bring it under his spell, with Torriani and De Winter combing to clear their lines.

    Milan are now sitting off, settling into a back five as they look to preserve their advantage. Fernandes, Tielemans and Dalot combine well but such has been United’s fortunes this afternoon, the ball ricochets off the referee and play is halted.

    Good work from Rashford in the corner to regain possession, but his ball into the box is not picked up by a team-mate.

    Sources indicate that more changes... Ramos and Musah make way for Camarda and Ricci.

    It has been revealed that manchester United 2 AC Milan 4 (Loftus-Cheek) No sooner had the players returned after the second-half hydration break then Milan exploit United’s exposed left side (again). Ramos sends Loftus-Cheek through and the midfielder composes himself before bending the ball around Lammens.

    Manchester United 2 AC Milan 3 (Ramos) That’s too easy. United fail to learn their lesson, Shaw not getting tight enough to Chukwueze and the winger’s cross is met by latest signing Ramos, who powers a header back across goal and past Lammens.

    Loftus-Cheek and Ramos are doing a good job of cutting off the pass into United’s midfield in their build-up phase.

    Wholesale changes on the hour mark...

    Rashford (who makes his first United appearance in almost two years), Lacey, Dalot, Mbeumo, Mainoo and Martinez replace Dorgu, Amad, Mazraoui, Cunha, Santos and Heaven.

    For Milan, Saelemaekers, Bartesaghi, Gila and Modric are on for Cisse, Estupinan, Terracciano and Jashari.

    Sources indicate that manchester United 2 AC Milan 2 (Cisse) United have set a higher defensive line so far this half, with their front line pressing with more intensity to avoid the ball over the top. However Chukwueze is able to find space around the sides, coming in off the right and curling an effort goalwards which Cisse turns in at the far post. There are calls for offside, but with no VAR here, the goal stands.

    In a recent development, milan win a free-kick some 25 yards out after Fernandes clips Estupinan. Teenager Cisse steps up and fires straight into the United wall. Was always going to be difficult to trouble Lammens from there.

    Manchester United 2 AC Milan 1 (Dorgu) United wisely decide to keep hold of the ball for a while, the midfield three rotating to disrupt Milan’s out-of-possession shape and open up passing lanes. A Milan throw-in from the right-back berth is precedes an awful backpass by Terracciano which is pounced on by Dorgu who curls the ball beyond Torriani.

    Sources indicate that united have looked bright in the opening moments of this half. They win a free-kick midway into Milan’s half. The ball is delivered to the back post and, after some 18-yard-box pinball, a relieved Torriano pounces on it.

    Both teams remain unchanged as the second 45 minutes begin.

    All square at the break. Tough to know what to make of that half – United looked solid enough and could have taken a lead into the interval had Fernandes converted his penalty, but they failed to create a wealth of clear-cut chances. It will be interesting to see how Carrick approaches this second half.

    Milan have enjoyed just a tick over two-thirds of possession, which United have contributed to in part through some lackadaisical passing.

    It has been revealed that fernandes misses a spot-kick for the second time in two friendlies! Here, Torriani guesses correctly, diving to his right to palm Fernandes’ strike away.

    De Winter brings down Tielemans inside the box after Terracciano loses the ball attempting to play out from the back.

    Manchester United 1 AC Milan 1 (Chukwueze) It’s all a bit messy. Jashari causes Maguire and Santos to crash into each other (Kaka at Old Trafford, anyone?) off a throw-in, Ramos taking over with the United pair out of commission. He finds Chukwueze who finishes the move off at the far post.

    The match becomes stretched momentarily as Pavlovic, the centre-back, marauds forward, setting the ball to Estupinan who delivers another dangerous cross from the left, which Lammens does well to claim.

    Santos clips Loftus-Cheek near the byline and the referee awards Milan a free-kick. Chukwueze cuts the ball back to an unmarked Jashari on the edge of the box, but his side-footed effort flies wide.

    Milan supporters unfurl a banner paying tribute to the late, great Franco Baresi, who passed away on July 31 aged 66.

    Hermosa bandera a Franco Baresi.QUE EN PAZ DESCANSE, LEYENDA DEL FÚTBOL 🙏🏻 pic.twitter.com/fvE48nKVSs.

    United have picked their moments to press. Santos, who has enjoyed a wonderful pre-season, is a little too overzealous in his attempts to regain possession and gives away a foul. But the intent is correct.

    It has been revealed that shaw floats a delightful ball over the top for Fernandes to gallop on to. The Portuguese steals in ahead of De Winter but cannot find the target with his weaker left foot.

    Cisse escapes the clutches of Mazraoui down the left and fires a shot (more likely a mis-hit cross) straight into the gloves of Lammens.

    United finally get their foot on the ball, but Heaven attempts an ambitious cross-field pass and possession goes back to the Italians.

    Sources indicate that A Mexican wave has already begun. We’re only 21 minutes in...

    According to recent reports, carrick’s side continue to sit off, allowing Milan to keep hold of the ball. Cisse works in from the left, playing a neat one-two with Ramos before his curled strike sails well over.

    A period of extended possession for Milan, United dropping into a compact 4-4-2 mid-block. Estupinan rains in a dangerous cross from the left and the ball falls to Loftus-Cheek, whose effort is expertly saved by the right boot of Lammens.

    In a recent development, estupinan goes into the book after pulling Amad’s shirt as he looked to dart in behind after Tielemans had played a dangerous through-ball. Might possibly have been the last man?

    Tielemans cedes possession to the busy Jashari just outside his own box, the Swiss midfielder moving the ball on to Loftus-Cheek who fires a shot straight at Lammens.

    Amad picks Pavlovic’s pocket and the Milan centre-half is forced to concede a corner. United unable to score from this one.

    According to recent reports, milan are indeed in Amorim’s preferred 3-4-2-1 formation. They circulate the ball in front of United’s first line of pressure in an attempt to calm things down.

    Manchester United 1 AC Milan 0 (Maguire) Fernandes delivers an inswinger from the left and Maguire is there to meet it at the back post, striding past Musa to plant a header past Torriani.

    United make a fast start, Dorgu flashing a cross-cum-shot across the face of goal. Torriani gets a fingertip to it and thte ball goes behind for a corner.

    Szymon Marciniak, the experienced Polish referee, gets us under way. Milan send the ball back to goalkeeper Torriani.

    The players emerge from the tunnel, United debuting their lovely new cream third kit and Milan in their traditional red-and-black home colours. Smoke machines and pyrotechnics add to the atmosphere in Wroclaw...

    In a recent development, we are almost ready to go. Let us know your match predictions and thoughts on United’s prospects this season in the comments section beneath this blog.

    According to recent reports, manchester United defeated Leeds United on penalties to hoist the mighty Boyle Sports Cup at Croke Park. The match, a 1-1 draw, was brought to an abrupt end after five young pitch invaders ran to the middle of the field to take selfies with Bruno Fernandes. In the shoot-out it was James Justin who missed the “decisive” spot-kick, paving the way for Noussair Mazraoui to win it for United.

    According to recent reports, marcus Rashford is on the bench this afternoon and could make his first United appearance since his cameo in a Europa League win over Viktoria Plzen in December 2024. He was frozen out under Amorim and has since been loaned to Aston Villa and Barcelona, but his Old Trafford future under Carrick remains unclear.

    Michael Carrick believes Manchester United can push for the Premier League title, but has underlined the urgent need for signings.

    The United head coach has taken heart from his squad’s promising preparations for the new campaign and, speaking at their Co Kildare summer base, he explained why he was confident they could build on last season’s third-place finish.

    In a recent development, carrick has been thrilled to hear United’s players discussing what they might achieve and has dared supporters to dream that they can get closer to last year’s champions Arsenal. But he is also a realist and recognises he is not blessed with options.

    So far United have added Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Karl Darlow, a reserve goalkeeper, but their £83.3m spend is significantly less than what newly promoted clubs Ipswich Town (£109.4m) and Coventry City (£92.2m) have invested in their squads.

    Amorim’s side have gone intercontinental this summer, travelling from Scotland to Indonesia, via Australia, before arriving in Poland for the last of their four pre-season games.

    Aug 5: AC Milan 1 Inter Milan 1.

    In memory of Franco Baresi 🇮🇹♾️ pic.twitter.com/ULAJRjxDvE.

    Manchester United Lammens; Mazraoui, Maguire, Heaven, Shaw; Tielemans, Santos, Fernandes; Amad, Dorgu; Cunha.

    Subs Heath, Mee, Amass, Dalot, Martínez, Yoro, Collyer, J. Fletcher, T. Fletcher, Mainoo, Gabriel, Lacey, Mbeumo, Rashford, Zirkzee.

    AC Milan Torriani; Terracciano, De Winter, Pavlović; Chukwueze, Jashari, Musah, Estupiñán; Loftus-Cheek, Cissè; Ramos.

    Subs Bouyer, Pittarella, Gila, Diawara, Vladimirov, Ricci, Saelemaekers, Bartesaghi, Modrić, Comotto, Camarda.

    According to recent reports, at his AC Milan unveiling, Amorim was asked about the learnings from his United tenure that he would take into his upcoming role. He said: “The first thing is it’s hard to explain the mistakes because for that I would have to explain the context of the last adventure.

    “It’s hard to say to you every mistake. The only thing I can say is that I learned a lot and I made some mistakes.

    “I didn’t have the opportunity, and I’m sorry for that, I didn’t have the opportunity to say something to the Manchester United fans at the moment and I’m really proud to be their coach for a year in that time.

    “But now it’s a different history. There are a lot of things that I could do better in the last experience but sometimes it’s like that, you need to learn to find the right spot to reach a different level and that’s my thinking here.

    In a recent development, “Everyone learns from their experience. I learned a lot, I did some mistakes I will try to change, there are some thing you will never change but I think I will be a better manager, that’s all.”.

    Jul 18: Manchester United 0 Wrexham 1.

    Jul 24: Rosenborg 0 Manchester United 5.

    Aug 1: Manchester United 2 Atlético Madrid 1.

    Aug 8: Paris St-Germain 1 Manchester United 1.

    Aug 12: Manchester United 1 Leeds United 1 (5-4 pens).

    Gonçalo Ramos goes straight into Amorim’s starting XI after his switch from PSG.

    Upcoming signing Youri Tielemans handed first start as one of six changes to the XI that faced Leeds United.

    Our final starting XI of Tour 2026! 📋🤍ℹ️ Squad numbers worn in pre-season are provisional and yet to be finalised.

    Recent findings suggest that welcome to live coverage of Manchester United’s final pre-season match, against AC Milan in Wroclaw, Poland. Michael Carrick’s side will look to apply the finishing touches to a promising summer on the pitch, which has included victories over Rosenborg and Atlético Madrid, plus a draw against European champions Paris St-Germain. The team will fly back to Manchester with the big ones, the ones they have always wanted – the Snapdragon Cup and the Boyle Sports Cup – in tow.

    At the Tarczynski Stadium there will be a reunion with former manager Ruben Amorim, who was appointed AC Milan’s head coach in June, five months after being sacked by United. Following a frustrating season under Massimiliano Allegri in which Milan fell out of the Champions League spots on the final day, the Rossoneri mentioned Amorim would bring a “modern dominant tactical approach”. His methods failed to cut through at Old Trafford, though, during a tumultuous 14-month reign which finally ended after the Portuguese “blew up” during a heated meeting with director of football Jason Wilcox. At Milan, Amorim has persisted with the 3-4-2-1 formation that was doomed at United.

    In a recent development, carrick made clear this week that United must strengthen if they are to challenge for titles. So far the club have brought in Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Karl Darlow, but they are still in the market for a left-back and another midfielder. The future of Marcus Rashford has also been a topic of conversation among United fans. The forward has not played for his boyhood club since December 2024 but has joined up with his team-mates in Poland and it remains to be seen if he features in Carrick’s forward planning.

    According to recent reports, kobbie Mainoo, who did not play a minute at this summer’s World Cup, and Lisandro Martínez have also joined up with the team this week and could be handed their first minutes of pre-season having been named in the matchday squad. For Milan, new signing Gonçalo Ramos – bought from PSG for £63m – will make his first appearance in the famous red and black.
